en: May the divine waters be auspicious for our aid and for our drinking.
May the waters flow toward us for our well-being and prosperity.
O Waters, bestow healing medicine as a protection for my body.
And may we long behold the sun!
Soma has told me that within the waters are all healing medicines.
And Agni, the source of all prosperity; the sovereign lords of desirable things,
who dwell among the people.
I beg the waters for medicine.
The mothers go on their paths, the sisters of those performing the sacrifice.
Mixing their milk with honey— those waters which are near the sun,
or with which the sun is joined.
May they impel our sacrifice.
I address the divine waters where our cattle drink.
The oblation is to be prepared from the waters.
Within the waters is immortality; within the waters is healing;
and likewise in the praises of the waters.
Become swift horses, O possessors of vigor!
We know Parjanya, the father of the arrow, the one who provides abundant nourishment.
For we know his mother, the earth, who nourishes all;
[we bow] around him, the greater one.
—May our bodies be as stone!
O Virudhvin, drive far away those who act with hostility; cast away all enmities.
When the cows embraced the tree,
they praised the unshaking Śara, the skillful Ṛbhu;
O Indra, keep the missile, the Śara, far away from us.
May these waters and these plants be auspicious to us.
May Indra’s thunderbolt strike down the demons;
may arrows, when loosed, fall far away from us.
We know Parjanya as your father, the one of abundant seed;
with him, I shall bring well-being to your body.
"Let your pouring out be upon the earth;
let 'bahiṣ' be for you, 'bāl'!"—thus [he says].
By Indra, by Varuṇa, by Candra, and by Sūrya.
Whatever [is] in the intestines, in the two kidneys, or whatever has flowed into the bladder...
(see PS 1.4.3cd)
I open wide your urethra as one opens a gate; with that, I shall bring well-being to your body.
"Let your pouring out be upon the earth;
let 'bāl' be outside for you," as the arrow flies away.
"Released from the bow, even so let your urine be discharged; out, O hair!"—this [is used] for all [urinary disorders]. PS 1.4.5 (4)
Vaṣaṭ to you, O Pūṣan! Let Aryaman, the wise Hotar-priest, fashion this well-fashioned hymn for you; let the noble lady bestow it, and let the giver release it.
May the joints be loosened for the sake of giving birth;
may the four quarters, the four intermediate directions, and the earth as well [open wide].
The gods have brought forth the embryo; may they open it wide for birth.
Once born, may it open wide.
We cause you to leave the womb;
loosen it, O Sūṣaṇā!
Release it, you who are free from pain.
Let the speckled moss not settle upon his sinews, nor upon his joints, nor upon his hair, nor upon his nails.
For the dog to eat the placenta; neither in the flesh nor in the fat,
nor in anything else whatsoever am I extended.
May the afterbirth fall away.
(PS 1.5.5) Anuvāka 1.
Those who move thrice-sevenfold, encompassing all forms and bearing them,
their powers belong to Vācaspati.
May it bestow a body upon me today.
Come to us, O Lord of Speech, together with the divine mind.
O Lord of the Ashvattha tree,
cause my body to rest within me alone;
spread it forth right here.
Like two ends of a bow held by the string,
may the Lord of Speech restrain my body within myself alone.
The Lord of Speech has been invoked; I have been invoked by the Lord of Speech.
May I prosper through what has been heard.
May I not be deprived of what I have heard.
The divine Gandharva, who is the lord of the world,
worthy of praise among the people with reverence by those seeking the one goal.
I choose you with a sacred prayer, O divine one of heaven;
homage be to you! Your dwelling place is in heaven.
Touching the sky, you are worthy of sacrifice, having the skin of the sun.
May he who has warded off the divine fury,
the kindly Gandharva who is the sole companion and lord of the world, be gracious to us through our homage. PS_1,7.2
The Gandharva has united with these blameless Apsarases;
they say that the ocean is their dwelling place.
For from whence they go both hither and thither— O lightning of the clouds, O you who belong to the stars,
you who accompany Viśvāvasu the Gandharva.
To you, O goddesses, I offer this homage:
those who are glowering, who dwell in darkness, who crave dice, and who delude the mind.
To those wives of the Gandharvas,
the Apsarases, I have paid homage—
from that mountain yonder.
Thou art a well, a medicine; thou art a medicine, a good medicine,
that medicine which I prepare for thee.
O Aṅga, surely, O Aṅga, whether there be a hundred remedies for you, or even a thousand that belong to you—
Of these, you are the supreme,
free from outflows and free from disease;
this great [teaching] is the cessation of the wound.
Drawn forth from the earth,
that is the remedy for the discharge;
it has destroyed the disease.
The ants bring forth the medicine from the ocean;
it is the remedy for the wound, belonging to Atharvan.
The Atharvanic [Veda] is his place of healing.
This Asura of the gods rules over all;
for the cow is indeed the truth of King Varuṇa.
Then, exulting in the sacred word (*brahman*), I lead this man out from the fierce wrath [of Varuṇa].
Homage be to you, O King Varuṇa, and to your wrath!
For you, O God, perceive every injury;
I impel away hundreds and thousands of others,
so that this man may live through the autumns.
Whatever falsehood or much crookedness you have spoken with your tongue—
[I take it] from you before the King whose law is truth.
I release you from Varuṇa;
I have released you from Vaiśvānara and from the great ocean.
Speak out, O fierce one, against those of equal birth;
drive away our enemies with sacred prayer.
Varuṇa has spoken in favor of lead.
Fire protects lead;
Indra bestowed lead upon me as a dispeller of disease.
This [remedy] overcomes Viṣkandha;
this subdues the Atris.
By this [spell], may I overcome all those born of the Piśācī who [haunt] this new-moon night.
The Atris rose up, shining;
Agni, the fourth, is the slayer of the demon Yātu.
May he protect us from them: if you kill a horse,
if a cow, or if a man.
We pierce you with lead so that this arrow of ours shall not slay our heroes.
PS_1,10.4 (10) Anuvāka 2.
With the turning-amulet by which Indra was turned about,
with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, turn this one [about].
Turn [the wheel] toward dominion!
Turned against our rivals—
those who are hostile toward us!
Overcome him who attacks us, he who seeks to harm us;
overcome you, O divine Savitṛ!
Soma has turned toward you; may all beings turn toward you, so that you may be victorious.
Up has risen that sun;
up has risen my word,
so that I may laugh at my enemies.
Without rivals, the slayer of rivals;
the destroyer of rivals, the bull, the sovereign of the realm, the all-conquering.
So that I may shine among these heroes and among the people;
may he increase for you alone in his old age.
May no other deaths harm him;
like a mother her son, may he, well-disposed, hold him in his lap.
May Mitra protect him from distress caused by a friend.
And may Mitra and Varuṇa, O destroyers of enemies, acting in harmony, grant you death through old age.
Then Agni, the Hotṛ-priest who knows all ordinances, the god, proclaims all generations.
Bhaṭṭa [reads] *vivaktu*; cf. K [which reads] *vakti* (PS 1,12.2):
"May Heaven be your father and Earth your mother; grant me old age, death, and long life."
Just as living beings in the lap of Aditi are protected by out-breath and in-breath for a hundred winters,
so do you rule over the animals of the earth.
Those who have been born and those who are yet to be born—
let neither the out-breath nor the in-breath abandon him.
May neither friends nor enemies slay him;
given by Indra, instructed by Varuṇa, and sent forth as a formidable one by the Maruts, he has come to us.
I entrust this to you both, O Heaven and Earth;
may it not thirst for me, may it not hunger for me.
O full of vigor, bestow vigor upon him.
Bestow milk upon him, O ye two full of milk; Heaven and Earth have bestowed vigor upon him;
all the gods, the Maruts, and the waters [have bestowed] vigor.
May auspicious ones satisfy his heart; free from disease and rejoicing, let him move about here.
Let the two who dwell together drink this stirred drink.
Having assumed the form of the Aśvins through their creative power (māyā),
may their essence (purīṣa) attend him as his drink;
may this [essence], along with nourishment (ūrj) and the self-sustaining power (svadhā), attend him.
Indra created this at the beginning when he was pierced;
it is this undecaying nourishment and vital power of yours. With that, may you live for many autumns, full of luster.
Let him not leak away; his physicians have prepared him.
O All-Gods, protect him;
and you, O Ādityas, keep watch over him.
May neither this nor any other [weapon] reach me;
may the mortal weapon of man not strike me.
O gods, you who are fathers and you who are sons—
Listen with attentive hearts to these words of mine:
I entrust this child to you all;
may you lead him safely to old age.
O gods who dwell in heaven, who on earth, and who in the intermediate space, in the plants, and in the waters—
you grant him long life and old age.
May he ward off a hundred other deaths. Those gods who have both *prayāja* and *anuyāja* offerings as their share, whether they consume oblations or do not consume oblations—
Those five directions which have been apportioned to you— those I make for you here, O you who sit in session;
I take Bhaga away from you.
Like a garland upon the head,
like a mountain with deep roots,
may you dwell long among the ancestors.
"O King, this maiden, your daughter-in-law,
is being led away by Yama; let her be bound in the house of her mother."
"Whether from a brother or from a father—
O King, this [woman] is yours as a protector of your intent;
we entrust her to you."
May he dwell long among the ancestors, from the head down to the gathering of the limbs—
by the power of the Black Brahman.
Like the inner chambers of Kaśyapa and Gaya, I bind your vulva,
O sister.
Section 3.
O herb, you are born at night— Rāmā, Kṛṣṇā, and Asiknī.
O Dyer, dye this!
O Pṛṣat,
drive away and destroy from here both leprosy and grey hair.
May your own natural color reach you; cast away the white [complexions]. Black is your place of dissolution.
Your seat is black,
O herb; O black one, drive away the speckled spot from here.
That which was produced from bone, from kilāsa, and from the skin of the body,
having been defiled by Brahmā.
I have destroyed the white mark.
The first embryo-born, ruddy bull, thundering with rain, comes from the clouds of wind.
May he, who with his straight course breaks [all things], having fashioned the one power threefold, be gracious to our bodies—
he who has taken up his residence in every limb with his flame.
I worship with oblation him who seized his joint, the seizer of the joints;
him who dwells in the heart, who has produced [all things] with his mind, limb by limb and joint by joint.
I release him from headache and from cough; whatever has entered him joint by joint— whether that vital force (śuṣma) was born from the clouds or born from the wind.
May he attend upon the trees and the mountains.
May there be well-being for your upper limb;
may there be well-being for your lower limb.
May it be well for your back and your marrow; may it be well for your body.
May Mitra come hither, conforming himself to the seasons.
Causing the earth to be settled by means of the dawns—
may Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Agni bestow upon us that great kingdom to be settled.
May Dhātṛ, Mitra, Varuṇa, the god Agni, Indra, and Tvaṣṭṛ accept my speech;
I invoke the goddess Aditi, the mother of heroes.
May I be the one who stands in the midst of my kinsmen.
I invoke Soma and Savitṛ with prostrations,
and all the gods, so that I may prevail.
This fire has shone forth at daybreak, kindled by kinsmen who do not offer resistance;
stay right here, do not go before us.
May Aryaman, the protector and lord of prosperity,
drive you hither. For this desire of yours, O longing ones, come all you gods together toward the sky here.
May the Vasus place wealth in this [child]: Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni;
and may the Ādityas and all the gods [do so].
May the gods establish him in the highest light.
May the gods grant him light in every direction:
may it be the sun, or fire, or even gold.
Shine forth with superior power through the sacred word (*brahman*),
making your other rivals inferior—
by means of that [power] wherewith I have gathered the waters for Indra.
With that which is superior, O Jātavedas,
with that, O Agni, do thou cause this man here to prosper; bestow upon him an abundance of wealth and preeminence.
I bring their sacrifice and splendor,
O Agni, as well as abundance of wealth and possessions;
let our rivals be lower than we.
—Place this man in the highest light among the gods!
May those who pierce from afar not find us; may those who pierce from close by not find us.
O Indra, strike down the arrows far from us in all directions;
let the shafts fly away from us in every direction.
Those who are on both sides of her—
may the gods, humans, and seers pierce our enemies.
Bhaṭṭa [says]: "He who is common, he who is not common, the enemy who seeks to kill us. (PS 1.20.2)
May Rudra pierce those enemies of ours with his arrow, whether they be kinsmen or strangers.
Whoever seeks to harm me, O Indra—
may all the gods destroy him; may the sacred word (*brahman*) be my inner armor.
Section 4.
Neither non-existent nor perishing, falling away of its own accord— O Bhaṭṭa,
neither existent nor non-existent, more non-existent than the non-existent, and more sapless than sap.
More moist than salt,
fly away, you diminished ones,
like a bird from its dwelling.
May the Sun provide a remedy;
may the Moon shine away your [sickness].
One is tawny, one is white.
Kṛṣṇā is one, Rohiṇīs are two;
I have seized the name of them all:
"Go away, you who do not slay heroes!"
The woman who has not yet given birth shall fall away from the Rāmāyaṇa;
the consumption shall fall away from here.
He, as he goes, shall perish.
Indra and Pūṣan have taken note of those who are departing and wasting away.
Having gone away from his necks and from his feet,
let him depart from the quarters and from the guardians of the quarters.
To the four immortals,
the overseers of what has come to be, let us offer this oblation with our sacrificial gift.
O four gods who are the guardians of the quarters, you who are the protectors of the regions— may you deliver us from the snares of Nirṛti.
May he release us from distress, from distress.
May you, who are not lame, be won over by my oblation; I offer to you with ghee, O one who does not limp.
May he who is the guardian of hopes, the fourth god among the quarters, bring us well-being here;
may there be well-being for our mother and our father.
May there be well-being for the cattle and for men; may everything be auspicious for us and easy to find.
May we long behold the sun.
O people, this great sacred formulation (brahman) shall be proclaimed as a sacrificial session;
it is not upon the earth, nor is it in heaven.
From which the plants draw their breath;
it is like the vast abode in the intermediate space for those who are weary from their labors.
O people, that is the station of this wise Being, the Ordainer,
when the two worlds tremble.
The earth has been carved out [by you],
yet today it remains ever moist;
you abide like a fissure in a mountain of rock.
The one has encompassed the universe;
the universe rests upon the other, as well as upon Dyaus, the all-knowing.
And I have offered homage to the Earth.
May the rivers flow together;
may the winds from heaven also come together.
With all those outflows, we cause wealth to flow together for me.
Those outflows which flow together—
Of milk and of water—
with all these outpourings, we cause wealth to flow together for me.
With all those outpourings which flow from the rivers, the ever-unfailing springs— by means of them all, [may this be for me].
We cause wealth to flow together.
Come to these oblations, and to this flowing together as well.
Let every animal here come; may it increase his wealth.
Golden-hued, pure, and purifying...
In whom Kaśyapa was born, in whom Indra, those golden ones who have held Agni as their embryo—
may those waters be auspicious and pleasant for us.
In whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men...
Those whom the gods make their portion in heaven, those who exist manifoldly in the intermediate space,
those golden ones who have taken Agni as their embryo.
(…) Behold me with a gracious eye; touch my skin with a gracious body as you perform the ablution.
May those waters which drip with ghee, pure and purifying, be auspicious and pleasant for us. (PS 1.25.4,
Anuvāka 5)
The Suparṇa was born first; you were his bile. Then the Asurī was conquered in battle.
Rūpa made the trees;
Āsurī made the first—
this, indeed, is the remedy for kilāsa.
This, indeed, is the destroyer of leprosy;
it has destroyed the leprosy and made the skin uniform in color.
Your mother is named Sarūpā, your father is named Sarūpa;
you, O herb, are the maker of likeness.
Make this [body] uniform in form:
whatever leprosy you have produced, whether born from the body or born from fire, that which is variegated— [make it uniform].
Let that be for the skin of the body as we remove you from it;
Śyāmā is the maker of beautiful form.
Drawn forth from the earth,
accomplish this task well;
fashion the forms once again.
May Soma and Savitṛ grant us fearlessness; may both Heaven and Earth grant us fearlessness; may the Sun and the mid-air be free from fear for us.
Through the oblation to the Seven Seers, may there be safety for us.
May heaven and earth grant us safety here; with Agni, burn up our enemies who face us.
May they find neither a knower nor a support;
striking one another down, may they go unto death.
The five gods rule over fearlessness.
Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni— may this village ward off evil through its magic;
may the wrath of kings fall elsewhere.
May Savitṛ bestow strength and well-being upon this village from the four quarters;
may Indra make it free of enemies and secure from fear.
And may we abide in the midst of the people as doers of good.
May the heart-ache and the jaundice depart from you, following after the sun.
With that which is the color of the red bull,
with that we enclose you.
We enclose you with red colors.
We bestow [this] for the sake of long life;
so that you may be free from disease and likewise free from jaundice.
Those cows that belong to the Lord of Gods, which are ruddy, and those which are even more ruddy— may they,
form by form and age by age, [grant us prosperity].
With that we enclose you.
We place your yellowness in the parrots and in the thrushes.
And so we deposit your yellowness among the *hāridrava* birds.
Those which move about in the east—
Lower than the sun and even lower than the sky,
we address this host of Apsarases with a sacred prayer.
Those that creep from below, making crooked faces as they come— driven away,
let them go from here! Bhaṭṭa has struck them down.
May those [streams] that are gathering [the waters] perish from here—
those which are channel-streams, those which are forest-streams,
and those which are intoxicating.
All those [plants] he crushes with a stone like sesame seeds in a mortar— the conscious, stony, leafy [plant].
Homage to you, O flames!
Drive the consumption far away;
do not let it settle upon our person.
In the beginning, desire arose within that [Being], which was the first seed of the mind.
That desire, united with the great desire, was its womb.
Bestow an abundance of wealth upon the sacrificer!
O Kāma, you are established by power; you are all-pervading, radiant, a good friend to him who seeks your friendship.
O Bhaṭṭa, you who are fierce and victorious in battles, bestow power and vigor upon the sacrificer.
From afar,
they have listened to us from all directions for him who desires and bestows inexhaustible wealth.
Through desire, they generated heaven.
Bhaṭṭa [says]: "By desire I have begotten thee.
(PS 1.30.3) "O Desire, let desire come to me from heart to heart."
Whatever mind these [people] have here,
let that come unto me; O Kāma, whatever you desire, [let that be mine].
We prepare this oblation for you;
may all of that be fulfilled for us.
Now, partake of this oblation, Svāhā!
Who gave this to whom? Desire gave it to desire.
Desire is the giver; desire is the receiver;
desire has entered the ocean.
I accept you with desire; O Desire, this is yours. (PS 1.30.6, Anuvāka 6)
O Kuṣṭha, bring that man here to me; drive him away;
and make him free from disease for me.
Born in the north from the Himavat,
O Bhaṭṭa, you are led eastward toward the people;
there are the names of Kuṣṭha.
The best things have been distributed.
Your name is Uttama; your father’s name is Uttama.
From where you, O Kuṣṭha, are born,
from there come for our well-being—
to [ward off] the blow to the head and the fatal blow.
May Kuṣṭha protect our eyes, our bodies, and our skin from injury on every side; may it bestow upon us all divine virility.
Where Agni, having entered the waters, burned them,
and where those who uphold the cosmic order (dharmadhṛt) offered their salutations— there they say is your supreme place of birth.
Knowing us, O Takman, spare us!
Whether you are the fever of grief, or the fever of intense sorrow, or if you are the breath of Rudra, or if you belong to Varuṇa— spare us!
O god, you are named Huḍu, belonging to the green one; as one who knows us, avoid us, O Takman!
Whether you are the flame or whether you are the smoke.
Whether among the Śākalyas or in your place of birth,
O god, you are named Huḍu of the green one.
Knowing us, O Takman, spare us!
Homage to the cold Takman; homage to the burning one, we pay it to you.
Homage be to Takman, who manifests on alternate days, on both days, and every third day—
the tertian and the sub-tertian fever.
Destroy the fever that lasts six days or even a year, the fever of every autumn, the summer fever, and that of the rainy season.
I have moved along with the waters today; we have united with their essence.
O Agni, I have come full of milk.
Endow me with that splendor!
O Agni, endow me with splendor and with progeny; make me abundant.
May the gods know this of mine; may Indra know it together with the seers.
O Waters, carry this away!
Whatever is blameworthy and impure,
whatever is malicious and false, and whatever I have sworn falsely in anger— [may all that be removed].
Behold me with an auspicious eye; touch my skin with an auspicious body.
We invoke the auspicious fires that dwell within the waters.
O divine waters, bestow upon me sovereignty and splendor!
Whatever sexual union the waters practiced at night, or whatever ancient sin they committed through treachery; [may all that be removed].
Then may those golden-colored ones purify me;
may they release me from the noose of Varuṇa.
Agni, the progenitor, has given this wife to me.
Soma, the bestower of wealth, has given this wife to me.
Pūṣan, the knower of kinsmen, has given this wife to me.
Indra, the more powerful one, has given this wife to me. (34)
To Agni, the knower of people, svāhā!
To Soma, the finder of wealth, svāhā!
To Pūṣan, the knower of kinsmen, svāhā!
To Indra, the more powerful, svāhā!
PS_1,35.4a (35) Anuvāka 7.
Those who move about in front, or those who always follow behind— the Sadānvas— let them strike against the stone.
That which is beginningless in its own essence,
and those eternal [entities] that proceed from a substratum or from what is superior; these are the [objects of] constant pursuit.
Let those who move behind him strike against a stone— those who, though appearing sweet, are inedible.
Let the Sadānvas come from the front, striking the stone—
him who is pleasant to taste yet not to be eaten.
Let those who come from the north or from below, the ever-following ones, go toward the stone as they approach.
I have turned away those two kinds of approaches that were directed toward you, which were not to be indulged in for one's own pleasure.
One [set of arrows] is shot by the gods, many others [are on the earth], and yet others reach the sky.
Homage to you, O Rudra, as you draw your bow!
Homage to those who have been dispatched; homage to those being released;
homage to those who have fallen down.
My golden amniotic membranes are six thousand and six hundred;
with them we enclose ourselves.
May they protect us from all sides.
This other [world] is vast and spread out;
pierce through its desire at will!
Out of fear of you, this great celestial mansion made of iron has been fashioned for me; it is worthy of homage through my prostration.
Therefore we take refuge in them; may they protect us on all sides.
I make an iron armor;
I make an iron door;
I make iron stakes.
May they protect us from all sides.
This other [world] is vast and established;
pierce through its desire at will.
Of these three earths that exist, this ground is the highest; from their very skins, I [take].
I have gathered together the remedy. You are the best of herbs,
the most excellent of medicines.
Like Bhaga among the sacrifices on their journeys,
like Varuṇa among the gods—
may they be wealthy and unassailable.
Desiring to bestow, you bestow;
you are these that increase the hair, and you are those that strengthen the hair.
Strengthen the root, extend the tip, and restrain the middle, O herb!
This is the hair-increasing [charm] of Atharvan.
This *Keśadṛṃhaṇa* belongs to the Atharvans:
"O Agni, come to us with cattle; O Indu, be with us with wealth."
May Indra, the sustainer, be in our homes;
may Savitṛ, who possesses thousands,
take delight in our dwellings.
May prosperity come, may wealth come; may Tvaṣṭṛ, who is the bull and the youth,
take delight in our homes.
May Dhātṛ, the lord and master of the world, bestow upon us wealth by the hundreds and by the thousands.
May he grant us [our desires] in their fullness.
To me belong both Mitra and Varuṇa;
to me belong both Indra and Bṛhaspati.
Tvaṣṭṛ and Pūṣan are under my control, and Savitṛ likewise is under my control;
Viṣṇu and Soma are mine as well.
The Maruts shall be under my power alone;
and Sarasvatī, Bhaga,
and all the gods shall be under my control.
Both Heaven and Earth are mine, the intermediate space and the celestial light are mine; all these herbs are mine.
All waters are under my control.
Mine are the cows, mine the horses, and mine the goats and sheep.
Men are mine alone; all this world, endowed with self, moving, and breathing, is under my control.
Section 8.
O Agni, you who turn toward us, turn toward us with long life, with splendor, and with gain.
O Agni Jātavedas, may there be a hundred turnings for you through wisdom, progeny, and wealth.
A thousand have turned back to you; now,
as the lord of prosperity, bring wealth back to us again.
Return with wealth—
O Agni, swell with a stream that provides for all, from every side.
Turn back again with vigor, O Agni; turn back again with full life-span.
Protect us again from distress.
Those armies that are attacking, piercing, and consisting of fierce hosts— whether they be a thief or a robber.
O Agni, I place them within your mouth;

And those [curses] which corrupt speech with poison—
whatever is ground and whatever is ungrounded, whatever is smeared and whatever is to be smeared.
O gods, you who know all things,
make the poison tasteless!
[Protect us] from hereditary disease, from destruction, and from the curse of kin.
I release you from the noose of Varuṇa, from deceit; by means of this sacred prayer, I make you sinless.
May Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you.
May Agni be auspicious for you along with the waters; may the cows be auspicious along with the plants;
may the mid-air together with the wind be auspicious for you.
May the four quarters be auspicious for you.
Those divine quarters, the four whose husbands are the winds, which the sun surveys from all sides.
Into these [fingers] I place this old age; let consumption and destruction depart far away,
just as the sun [drives out] darkness from the grasp of the seizer.
The gods, releasing him, freed him from sin;
even so do I release you from *kṣetriya*, from destruction, from the curse of kin, from malice, and from the noose of Varuṇa.
I have been released from consumption, from misfortune, from reproach, and from the noose of malice; I have also been released from the grasp of the seizer.
Casting off distress, I have found a pleasant place.
O blessed one, has it come to pass in this world for the sake of well-done deeds—
that [you should attain] the fearless, bold, solitary, and invincible bowl that desires to devour?
And we shall destroy all the granddaughters of Caṇḍa, the Sadānvās,
or indeed those born of Kṣetriya.
Whether impelled by men,
or whether you were born from the Dasyus—
perish from here, O Sadānvās!
I have run around their stations like a swift horse to the goal;
I have won all your races.
May the persistent enemies perish from here!
We drive you out from the cow-pen, out from the womb, and out from the wagon.
O daughters of Magundī,
we drive you out from your houses to that lower dwelling.
May all the Arāyīs be present there; may evil and all the Yātudhānīs be cast down.
Heaven and Earth, the wide mid-air, the two wives of the field, the far-striding and wondrous; and the broad mid-air, whose guardian is the wind.
Let them indeed suffer while I am suffering!
O Indra, drinker of Soma, hear this which I call out to you with a grieving heart.
I cut down with a thunderbolt like a tree him who injures this mind of ours.
O gods, listen to this, and you who are worthy of sacrifice!
May Bharadvāja recite hymns for me;
may he who injures this mind of ours be bound in fetters and cast down into misfortune.
May the eighty-three Sāmagas, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aṅgirases protect the merit of our ancestors' sacrifices and charitable works.
I take this with divine power.
O Heaven and Earth, look upon me;
O All-Gods, hold me fast.
May the sin of the one who acts with hostility reach the performer of that act— the one who thinks too highly of himself, O Maruts, you who are the Soma-loving ancestors of Aṅgiras.
May burning pains be the lot of him who reviles the Brahman as it is being performed;
may the sky scorch that hater of the Veda.
I place your footprint in the kindled Jātavedas; may Agni pervade your body.
Let your life-breath go to Yama;
I sever those seven breaths and eight marrow-essences of yours with the sacred word (brahman).
Go to the abode of Yama, with Agni as your well-prepared messenger. (PS 2.5.8,
Anuvāka 1)
Vena beheld that supreme station where the universe becomes a single nest;
this cow, as she was being born, milked it forth.
The hosts of those who find the light have shouted their acclaim.
Let the Gandharva, knowing it as the immortal, proclaim that supreme abode which is hidden in the cave.
Three steps have been set down in his secret place; he who knows them shall be the father of the Father.
He is our kinsman, our progenitor, and our sustainer.
He knows the abodes and all the worlds,
where the gods, having attained immortality,
established themselves in a common dwelling.
I have gone around all beings; I have approached the first-born of Cosmic Order,
established among beings like speech in its speaker.
Truly, this Agni is about to suckle;
indeed, he has swiftly encompassed heaven and earth, so that we may behold the outspread thread of the Cosmic Order.
A god, guarding his divine nature, alone questioned his common kin:
"O Indra, take pleasure [in us]; come, O hero!"
Drink of the pressed honeyed juice, O you who desire it,
lovely for exhilaration.
O Indra, let the pressed juices enter you.
Fill your two flanks; drink, O Śakra!
Come to us with your wisdom.
Indra, fill your belly with the sweet [soma].
May Vāja be near you in the exhilarations of this son;
Indra, the subduer of the swift, has slain Vṛtra.
The wielder of the thunderbolt, in the exhilaration of Soma, has overcome his enemies in battles;
hear my call and take pleasure in my songs.
O Indra, exhilarate yourself with your own companions for intoxication, for great joy!
Upward indeed have the three stepped forth.
The tiger, the man, the wolf; apart from that is the light, the sun;
apart from that is the god, the lord of the forest.
May the enemies perish from afar;
let the wolf go by the highest path, and let the thief pass by the farthest way.
Then there is the supreme tiger:
"O tiger, we crush both your eyes and your jaws."
And from all twenty nails:
"That which has perished, that which is perishing,
that which will perish, and that which has not yet perished."
The teeth of the beast are crushed, and its ribs are shattered;
we [fear] the tiger among those with fangs.
First we crush him; then the thief, the serpent,
the sorcerer, and likewise the wolf.
Do not seize, do not enter the house;
do not harm our bipeds or quadrupeds.
Born of Indra, you are born of Soma.
This plant is born of honey;
for the sake of honey, we dig you up.
You are born from honey;
make us full of sweetness.
On the tip of my tongue is honey.
Madhūlaka at the root of the tongue:
"O lustful woman, just as you have come to me, so do you follow after me. (PS 2.9.2)
I have come around you with a surrounding stalk of sugarcane, so that we may be without enmity,
and that we two may not hate one another.
We shall never perish; speak thus to King Varuṇa:
[for the sake] of the horse and the man.
O wealthy one, bring a wife to me by a good path along my way.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, [bring] a wife to me.
May the goddess Sarasvatī grant me a wife;
may both the Aśvins, adorned with lotus garlands, bestow a wife upon me.
O ten-wooded tree, release him from distress and from the seizing grasp;
and so, O Lord of the Forest, [release] him.
Lead the living beings upward to the world!
He who made it has undone it; he alone is the most excellent physician.
He himself has prepared medicine for you and called you a physician; the gods have found a way for you.
Even the Brahmins and the plants have found for you today the highest manifestation upon the earth.
He has come; he has risen up;
he has entered the company of the living;
he has indeed become the father of his sons.
And among men, he is the most blessed;
he has ascended to the study of the Vedas,
and he has ascended above the cities of the living.
He who possesses a hundred plants and a thousand remedies.
PS_2.10.5 (10) Anuvāka 2.
For long life and for great joy,
remaining unharmed and always exerting ourselves,
[we wear] this amulet that destroys *viṣkandha*.
We carry the jaṅgiḍa plant.
The jaṅgiḍa [protects] from the seizing tooth, from the falling-apart, from the viṣkandha, and from the burning fever.
May the jewel of a thousand powers protect us on every side; it overcomes the *viṣkandha* demon.
This Jaṅgiḍa,
the all-healing, drives away the Rākṣasa; may it protect us from distress.
By means of the jewel Jaṅgiḍa, bestowed by the gods,
which brings delight, [drive away] Viṣkandha and all the Rākṣasas.
May we endure in our exertion.
And may both Śaṇa and Jaṅgiḍa release you from Viṣkandha.
One [kind of animal] is brought from the forest, another from the fields, and others from [various] juices;
may those animals that have departed come here.

May the cattle flow together into this pen;
may Bṛhaspati lead them here, knowing the way; may Sinīvālī bring them to the forefront.
May Anumati bestow favor upon those who have come. May cattle, horses, and men flow together in harmony.
Whatever abundance there is of grain,
that I offer with the flowing oblation;
I pour together the milk of the cows.
May strength and essence be united with the clarified butter;
may our heroes and our cows be united in me, their master.
I bring the milk of the cows; I have brought the grain and the juice;
I have brought our heroes.
Bring this eighth day as a wife.
May Aryaman unite you, may Pūṣan unite you, and may Bṛhaspati unite you.
May Indra, the winner of wealth, prosper whatever riches there are here;
right here, O cows, come hither!
—Thrive here like the Śakas; right here, moreover, procreate. May there be harmony among you in me.
O cows, be united with me, the lord of the herd; this is your stall, may it nourish you here. Becoming abundant through the increase of wealth, may you prosper.
May we sit near you, O living ones, as you live.
May we be united with your well-seated cow-pen, with wealth, and with excellent nourishment.
With the name of that which was born on this day,
we unite you;
being in agreement and unswerving.
In this cow-pen,
you who possess dung, bearing the Soma-offering,
come hither with easy access.
May the rising sun destroy the worms;
may the setting sun destroy them with his rays—
those worms that are within the cow.
The worm that is multiform, four-eyed, variegated, and white—
this worm is slain, its brother slain.
Their mother is slain, their sister is slain;
the king of the worms is slain,
and their chief architect is slain.
Slain are his attendants,
slain are his followers;
I sharpen your two horns.
With those two by which you cause yourself to swell,
I now shatter that jar in which your poison is stored.
Like Atri, I kill you, O worm; like Kaṇva, like Jamadagni, by the sacred word of Agastya.
All those worms have been slain—
the great stone of Indra,
which crushes every worm.
With that [pestle], I grind the worms together like grains of sesame with a millstone;
I have crushed what was seen and what was unseen.
And I have crushed the Kurūru;
all the Algaṇḍus and Śalūlas, the worms—
we crush them with our word.
I strike down the Algaṇḍus with a great slaughter; the afflicted have become unafflicted and tasteless.
I cast down the remaining ones, both those who are disciplined and those who are undisciplined, by means of my word.
Just as there is no remnant left for worms,
[so may I destroy] the worm in the intestines, that in the head, and also that in the back.
With our speech we crush the Avaskava, the Vyadvara, and the worms—
those worms that are in the mountains and those that are in the forests.
Those [worms] which are within the plants, within the cattle, and within the waters,
which have taken up residence in our bodies— may Indra slay them with his great weapon.
Section 3.
You who conquer enemies, you who are victorious and overpowering— slay those who oppose us.
O herb, make them tasteless!
The fair-winged bird found you; the boar dug you up with his snout.
Indra placed you in his arms to strike down the Asuras;
Indra devoured the *pāṭā* plant.
I have struck them down from among the Asuras;
with that [weapon] may I overcome my enemies,
just as Indra [overcame] the hyenas.
O Rudra, whose medicine is water,
blue-crested one, performer of deeds,
strike down the question of the malicious one.
"Whosoever assails us—
O Indra, strike down the question of him who seeks to harm us."
Speak over us with your powers;
make me superior.
Just as this [is] over the earth...
The wind stirs the grass;
even so do I stir your mind, so that you shall be in love with me.
Just as you have followed after me,
so have I come here, desiring a husband; I have come desiring a wife.
Like a neighing horse,
I have come here with good fortune;
O Aśvins, if you two lead me together.
Bring them together for the one who desires;
may your minds meet, your eyes meet, and your vows meet as well.
That which is internal is external, and that which is external is internal,
in the case of maidens of manifold forms.
Seize the mind, O herb!
[The one] with beautiful wings,
the one who does not cause [them] to fall from their wings.
Herein your mind is fixed,
like a thorn in a bud, as it were,
in a lion, a tiger, or a viper.
The splendor that is in Agni, in the Brahmin, and in the Sun—
that goddess who, being fortunate, has caused Indra to grow— may she come to us, in harmony with our luster.
The splendor that is in the elephant, in the leopard, in gold, in horses, in men, and in cattle...

The brilliance that is in the kṣatriya, in the drum when it is struck, in the army, in the thunder, and in the sound—
The goddesses who, being fortunate, have strengthened Indra in his chariot, in his axles, in the bull’s vigor, in Parjanya, in Vāta, and in Varuṇa’s impetuous force.
(…) That [power] which is in the Rudras, which is in the Vasus, in the Ādityas, and in the Maruts;
May that splendor which is among all the gods come to us, being in harmony with our luster.
Whether [we are] on firm ground or on the waters, may it come.
May the king be our friend on the far shore of the rivers;
O All-Gods, protect him so that he may promote the assembly while still alive.
Whether on this side or indeed on the other side,
or if the king is our friend in the desert; (…) whether in battle or in steadfastness.
If the king were our friend in the assembly...
may those who would attack our patron, the bountiful lord, fall down below and be brought low.
O All-Gods, protect him so that he may live to attend the assembly.
O Yama, O Death, do not harm him!
May he whom I have protected with heart and mind,
who nourishes me and whom I nourish, be rich in offspring, wealthy, and a patron.
Embark upon this boat— unpierced, leading to the further shore—
which dwells in the house of Narāśaṃsa.
And may the hundred-oared boat of Bhaga [bring us across].
Come near with bdellium;
may the cows be free from disease.
The arrows of Rudra and of King Bhava strike down the sorcerers;
the two Rudras rule over bipeds and quadrupeds.
May we be present at their proclamation;
adorning them with ripe and abundant offerings,
may we abide in the good favor of the gods.
Pratīcī is your mother by name,
and Śatavāra is your father; from them indeed were you born.
They shall not suffer harm, O Arundhatī;
you are indeed called "Mother," for you are as it were the mother of immortality.
O Arundhatī, you have placed all this living world within yourself. (PS 2.20.5,
Anuvāka 4)
O Agni, as a matchmaker, grant us your favor; bestow this maiden upon us along with good fortune— she who is beloved among suitors and charming in assemblies.
May she be united with her husband; may she be fortunate.
O Agni, may this woman find a husband; for King Soma shall make her blessed.
Giving birth to sons, she shall become a queen; having approached her husband, the fortunate woman shall shine forth.
Cherished by Soma, cherished by the sacred word (brahman),...
Bhaga is gathered together by Aryaman;
by the truth of the divine Dhātṛ, I effect the finding of a husband.
Just as this lovely ass of Maghavan has become a pleasant resting place for wild animals,
so may she be dear to Bhaga.
Being well-beloved by your husband and not causing him harm,
mount the full boat of Bhaga, which provides a continuous supply.
With those two, go forth to him who is the desirable husband. Here is the gold and the bdellium.
This is the bull, and this is Bhaga;
these have given you over to your husbands,
so that you may find one who desires you.
Harness the ploughs, stretch out the yokes;
sow the seed here in the prepared field.
May the abundance of Virāj be our provider.
The ploughshares draw near to the ripened barley. The seers yoke the ploughs and stretch out the yokes separately.
The wise among the gods are intent on favor;
those men who are oxen that pull the plough and the share— I anoint them with abundance for prosperity.
May the plowman follow his draft-animals with success;
may the plowshare go through the earth with success,
for him who shall worship Śuna and Sīra with an oblation.
May the plants bear good fruit for him.
May the men with the plough, Bhaga with the oxen, and the Lord of the Field with the Maruts bring us prosperity.
May Parjanya impel the seed;
may Śuna and Sīra cause this grain to grow here. May Indra hold fast the furrow.
May Pūṣan protect her;
may she, rich in milk, yield for us in each succeeding year.
Up has risen Savitṛ on his one-wheeled chariot, the winner of chariots, the winner of cattle, the winner of horses, the winner of gold, encompassed by pleasant truth.
Having reached the earth with portions of vigor, filling it,
he distributes the essence of cattle, the sap of houses, and the herbs— the foremost splendor and life-force.
Do not harm your parents as you grow; go from a state of well-being to an even better world.
Whether this food is shared or divided...
Whether it be the field of the gods or of the ancestors,
whether at sunrise or as among men,
may the earth and the sky be auspicious to us.
Your portion is vigor, the best upon the earth;
O divine doors, I sustain you with sacred prayer. May there be for us a propitious and helpful dwelling.
It was given by the gods, the ancestors, and by men.
Viśvāvasu’s dwelling-place, his home, the Gandharvas, the wise ones, have declared to me.
Do not harm that treasure which we give to you, this man, for a hundred winters.
O Rudras, we place [you] upon the imperishable seat;
there the gods, the ancestors, and human beings rejoice.
This is the portion and the lord of the portion; O gods, may we cross over many unassailable autumns.
Whatever consumption has entered this man—
May Agni, who awakens with clarified butter, cast far away from us that impelled divine power.
Whatever wasting disease has been sent by the gods, we drive that away from you. 1. Whatever wasting disease has been sent by the gods—
And he who is impelled by the ancestors—
therefore may all the gods release you from distress.
May those various [afflictions] cause the consumption to fall away from you...

with the *apaskanda* oblation.
We destroy your consumption;
this Agni has said, and Soma has said it, as have Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, and Indra.
Let those various forms of consumption fall far away from us; let it meet with something else— we drive it away for him.
Those who are foremost in fire, possessing the strength of Indra, the Ādityas who know battle—
they are established upon battle.
They offer oblations for victory;
for one who is engaged in a great enterprise and desires an ally in battle, [the sacrifice is performed].
May the victorious King Varuṇa first accept the oblations from those who fight and those who offer sacrifices.
With Rudra the conqueror, with Keśin,
with Bhava, with the victorious one, and with Parjanya the more powerful, he conquers.
With the great copper-hued Astra,
with Śarva as he fought with the Astra,
and with the radiant Gandharva.
In a chariot that is irresistible in battle,
Sinīvālī and Anumati are the draft-horses; they are armed with quivers.
May Jayanta, together with Indra, the ally, overcome our enemies. (PS 2.25.5,
Anuvāka 5)
Whatever you have committed in a dream, or whatever falsehood you have spoken— may Agni deliver you from that sin.
May Brahmā release you from distress—
whatever offense you have committed against the dice or against your friends.
May Soma, as the Brahman, release you from that sin, from that distress—
[the sin] which [you committed] among boys while being a boy yourself.
Or whatever you have suffered while making the *nīvi* among those who are more senior— may we make that free from disease and auspicious.
For you, O Apāmārga plant, have become one whose fruit turns back;
[ward off] all curses from me.
O Apāmārga, you are the most excellent; you drive away [evil].
O Apāmārga, among all plants, you alone are the sovereign lord.
By that we wipe away what has settled upon you; now, move about free from disease.
Śatavāra has destroyed it.
The amulet, which drives away those of evil name, ascends with its splendor and luster over consumption and the Rakṣasas.
With its two horns it drives away the Rakṣas;
with its root, the Yātudhānīs; with its middle, it repels Yakṣman.
No evil shall overcome him—
those wasting diseases which are small,
those which are great, and those which are noisy.
The jewel Śatavāra has destroyed all ill repute;
he has begotten a hundred heroes.
He has scattered away the consumptions;
having slain all those of evil name, he shakes off the *rakṣas* demons.
This golden-horned bull, Śātavāra, is this jewel;
having struck down all those of evil name—
He has overcome the Rākṣasas.
A hundred [are] of the ill-named ones,
a hundred of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.
With a hundredfold barrier, I ward off a hundred [attacks] accompanied by dogs;
I drive away everything, like the earth [drives away] its abundance.
I receive the food that comes and that which is brought;
may Agni Vaiśvānara, by the greatness of the Great One, make all of that free from disease.
Whatever food I eat in many forms—gold, horse, cow, goat, or sheep—of Vaiśvānara... [it is the offering]. (PS 2.28.2)

Whatever has been offered and whatever has not been offered has come to me; from whatever food I am driven mad in mind—
by the greatness of the mighty Vaiśvānara.
May Agni make all that free from disease.
May Jamadagni, Kaśyapa, and Bharadvāja make this food sweet and honeyed.
May Gotama, Vasiṣṭha, and Viśvāmitra, as recipients, extend our lifespan.
O Agni, you are the eye of the sacrifice.
We know this, how this shall come to pass; svāhā!
O Agni, ear of the sacrifice:
we know this, how this shall come to pass; svāhā!
O Agni, breath of the sacrifice!
We know this: how this shall come to pass, Svāhā!
O Agni, out-breath of the sacrifice!
We know this, how this shall be; svāhā!
O Agni, soul of the sacrifice, we know this, how this shall be; svāhā!
O Agni, head of the sacrifice, may we understand this so that it shall come to pass; svāhā!
May the auspicious favor of the upright gods be ours.
May the gift of the gods turn toward us;
we have sought the friendship of the gods.
May the gods extend our lifespan so that we may live.
We invoke them with the ancient invocation:
Bhaga, Mitra, Aditi, Dakṣa the infallible,
Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, and the two Aśvins.
May the auspicious Sarasvatī grant us bliss.
Let this homage be offered today to the ancestors— those who came before and those who followed after.
O Agni, let the arrows fall back upon those who are seated in the earthly dust, or those who are now among the well-fortified settlements.
Do not show mercy to the mortal enemy who has done or has not done [wrong]; bestow him, the flesh-eater and devourer,
into the lap of Destruction.
Whether from the reproach of one superior or from that of one inferior, whether from the reproach of a kinsman or from the reproach of a relative—
whatever sin has been committed by another without our instigation, [may Agni carry it away].
Therefore, O Jātavedas, release us from that. (PS 2.30.5, Anuvāka 6)
I step forth with these two feet from my home for well-being;
Indra is behind me, Indra is before me.
May Indra protect us from the midst.
May Indra drive away our fear, both from the Śūdra and from the Ārya.
Indra has rushed along the paths; the malevolent ones have been unsuccessful.
Indra shall strike the weapon of those who seek to kill.
Unloose for us the bonds like a snare. We have ascended this path, easy to traverse and carrying one safely.
By means of which he avoids all enemies,
finds wealth,
and goes home unharmed.
Let it go away, cutting the *avakā* grass as if blinking; let its keepers go in all directions.
The waylayers are scattered in every direction; the malevolent ones who fail in their purpose are dispersed everywhere.
I have looked toward well-being; I have looked back toward well-being; may there be well-being on the paths and in the desert wastes.
May there be well-being within the waters;
moving about, may you lead us to heaven.
You are the means of auspicious passage.
Blessings upon Bhāradvāja for his safe return;
he who is born from the north, the honey-dropper, from the honey-dropper above.
I know the remedy in that;
my tongue is honey-sweet.
Honey-sweet was your leaf.
O herb, you are honey-tipped and flower-bearing; you are honeyed, O mountain,
from which you are born.
You are the embryo of the plants,
and you are also the embryo of the waters;
furthermore, you are the brother of Soma.
O Madhugh, accept my word.
Auspiciously have I grasped the name of Madhugh’s father, as it were.
May he who makes me golden-hued and dear to men make me beloved among the gods.
Be dear among kings;
be dear to everyone who looks upon you,
whether they be a Śūdra or an Ārya.
O Forest, with your udder, with your heart, with your mouth, and with your tongue—
O Forest, you are swollen with milk.
Desire the feet, desire the skin, desire the two eyes, desire the two thighs;
may your mind follow after the calf.
May it flow downward like water;
may your body hairs stand erect,
and may your eyes dry up with desire.
Like a cow with her calf,
let this seal be joined like a woman;
these cows are kinsmen.
They have made a common calf for themselves;
uttering the sound "hiṅ," they flow down the streams with a loud neighing.
Adorned with horns as their ornaments, inviolable, clothed in skins,
cows are the mothers of clarified butter.
Let us lead away that vital power which is in maidens and that which is established in elephants.
Whatever splendor is in gold and in cattle, may I partake of that splendor;
and whatever splendor is in the royal chariot.
And whatever splendor is deposited in kings, and whatever splendor is in the gold necklace and the golden ornament—
may I partake of that splendor.
Whatever splendor is in the waters, in the tree, in the fire, and in the sun, [and] in the sacrifice and in the sacrificial fee— [may that be ours].
May I partake of his splendor.
May my face be radiant with splendor, and may my head also be radiant with splendor.
May I be full of luster, facing in every direction;
may my complexion be full of luster;
may my face be beautiful.
May my head be auspicious;
may I be auspicious in every direction;
may my complexion be auspicious.
Yonder sun has risen together with my bridal dowry;
I am yours, full of sweetness.
The honey-sweet ones, most intoxicated with sweetness—
whatever honey is in the hills, in the mountains, in the cows, and in the horses; [all that is here].
As sweetness is in the wine being poured, as it is in the nectar, so may that [sweetness] be in me— just as in wine, just as in honey.
As the dice are upon the gaming board,
as the mind of one who desires cattle [is drawn],
so may your mind be directed toward me.
I have sought your footprint with my own foot; I have sought your mind with my own mind;
I have seized you, turning toward me.
Like a horse by its halter.
For me, may Heaven and Earth;
for me, may the goddess Sarasvatī [grant you].
Let both ends of the earth cast you into my midst. (PS 2.35.5,
Anuvāka 7)
Those arrows which belong to the Viśvedevas,
those of the Vasus, those of Rudra, those of Soma, and those of Bhaga— O All-Gods, as many arrows as there are, [drive them away].
With that protection of yours through Agni, I pacify [them].
Whatever arrows belong to the Ādityas, whatever to the Vasus, whatever to Rudra and the Aśvins— whatever they may be.
O Viśvedevas, as many arrows as you possess, may the god Savitṛ pacify them for you. O Agni, those arrows of yours, and those of Vāta...
That which is in the waters, in Aditi, and among the Maruts—
may Sūrya with the *bṛhat* sāman pacify those [fevers] of yours, as do Indra and King Varuṇa.
May we not incur the wrath of the Ādityas, nor that of the Vasus, nor that of Rudra, nor Agni of the earth;
may we avoid the fury of Indra and the fury of Varuṇa.
May that divine Aditi pacify those [stings] of yours which are in the wind, in the wind blowing from all sides,

May Agni, the lord of wealth,
make all those things into healing remedies;
I worship consciousness with my mind.
O divine Jātavedas, you who increase the cosmic order, extend our intelligence with all your protections, O Agni.
Drive away our hostilities with this offering of barley;
O Trita, that portion of bad dreams which belongs to you— [drive that away].
We send him forth to you, to each of you,
just as they pay back a sixteenth part, an eighth part, or a debt.
In this way, we transfer all evil dreams onto that which is unpleasant.
O Araru, may I today enjoy a hundred cows!
A hundred goats, a hundred sheep, a hundred horses, and a hundred men—

I bind him in the noose of Death;

May those who curse us pass away; let us pass over them as one passes over trees that have been felled, prolonging our life for a longer duration.
May we abide in the good favor of the gods.
O Agni, be watchful against the one who performs sorcery; perceive the sight of his final end.
O God,

We entrust you back to him so that you may strike down the one who fashioned the *kṛtyā*. Back to the fashioner of the *kṛtyā* [we send] the *kṛtyā*.
Seizing him by the hand, lead him away; let her devour him again,

Let the magical spells go to the maker of the spell,

Just as well-rain falls upon the plants, so [be it with you]. Whether the pressing-stone, moved by the arms, has caused you to flow forth,

O King Soma, may that part of yours swell, may that part of yours be restored,
which they have cut off with the pressing-stone, O King Soma.
O dear limbs, many are your well-formed parts;
join them together with clarified butter and cause them to grow, so that we may always remain free from sin and dwell together in peace.
Whatever skin they have torn from you, whatever womb [they have entered], or if you have been displaced from your station, or even if you are pressed out—
O Soma, all this of ours has been prepared by you.
O King, call upon us for our good deeds!
O King Soma, come together with our out-breath and in-breath, together with our sight, and together with our hearing.
Whatever in you is injured, may that be united for you;
may it recognize us at the meeting of our paths.
The day meets with the body through the milk.
His color becomes manifold;
to him, O Indu, let us worship with an oblation.
May we be masters of riches.
The ladles flow toward you with clarified butter, increasing your limbs and joints;

—O King, call upon us for our good deeds!
Come here, O goddesses; let this be the path, this world be a fitting refuge for you.
Enjoying this oblation, rise up quickly, impelled by King Varuṇa. May King Varuṇa come here with his swift ones.
The god, being pleased by the oblation together with the goddesses,

We worship Agni as our protector, the slayer of the malevolent spirit, the destroyer of secret spells; may Agni take pleasure in the clarified butter.
The menihās, the valagahās, the protectors—may they protect us! Svāhā!
We worship Indra, the protector.

bestow the sacrificial fee upon the Brahmins,

O Bhaṭṭa, make his enemy devoid of luster.
Grant him a share in this village, in horses, and in cattle.
Favor him who has no enemy;
let this man be the king of the ruling powers.
O Indra, subject all enemies to him.
May Heaven and Earth yield for him abundant wealth, like two cows that yield warm milk;
may he become a dear king to Indra.
He is dear to the cows, to the plants, and also to the waters.
I harness for you Indra, the superior one,
by whom they conquer and are not conquered.
But he who has made you the sole bull among the people, O King, and the highest among men—
may you be superior and the others be inferior.
O King, whatever adversaries you have,
may you, the sole bull, the friend of Indra, victorious, trample down the greatness of those who act as enemies.
Born of the Aṅgirases, born of the gods, possessing horns and a mouth, the beholder, she has arisen from heaven and earth.
O thousand-eyed one, be with us!
O herb, you who are thousand-eyed, look upon that which seizes us.
May she, who always destroys and slays the Rākṣasas, be here a beholder for those who carry off this daughter of the Soma-presser.
And the abundance of milk, O herb—
those, do you, O thousand-eyed one of accomplished power, seize!
Those who subject the afflicted, the diseased, and the emaciated to their will—
subdue them for me, O thousand-eyed one!
Seize it, O you of performed valor!
Just as the four-eyed horse gazes across the night throughout the darkness.
Thus, O thousand-eyed one, may you look back upon us from afar with cattle, horses, and wealth.
O herb, you have been purchased;
with the eye of the dark horse,
look upon the Kimīdins.
Unite together; drink together;
may your honeyed food be shared;
may your entire vow be directed toward a single goal.
May your minds be in harmony. Agree with one another; may Indra be your guardian.
May this Agni appease your wrath.
Whatever act of hostility or terror there was, may all the gods wash it away.
May Bṛhaspati be for your well-being.
May both Heaven and Earth be auspicious; may the intermediate space and the Maruts be auspicious for you;
may Aditi, the mother of the gods, be auspicious for you.
May heaven and earth be favorable; may the waters and plants be favorable;
may all the fires be favorable.
For this preeminence, being of one vow,
I unite your hearts;
may your minds be united.
May your bodies be united; may your breath be united.
I unite your hearts with the hearts of the cattle.
I unite the minds of your sons and those of your daughters; I unite the minds of your wives with [yours],
and I unite the eyes of your husbands.
The eastern direction has Agni as its overlord, Asita as its protector, and the Ādityas as its arrows;
homage to them, the overlords; homage!
Homage to the protectors; homage be to you, O arrows!
Him who hates us and him whom we hate, we place within your jaws; may his life-breath abandon him.
The southern direction has Indra as its sovereign lord, Tiraścīrajī as its protector, and the Vasus as its arrows;
homage to them, the sovereign lords; homage!
Homage to the protectors; homage be to you, O arrows!
Him who hates us and him whom we hate, we place within your jaws; may his own life-breath abandon him.
The western direction has Varuṇa as its overlord, the viper as its guardian, and Mitra as its arrows;
homage to them, the overlords; homage!
Homage to the protectors; homage be to you, O arrows!
Him who hates us and him whom we hate, we place within your jaws; may his life-breath abandon him.
The northern direction has Soma as its overlord, Svaja as its protector, and the winds as its arrows;
homage to them, the overlords; homage!
Homage to the protectors; homage be to you, O arrows!
Him who hates us and him whom we hate, we place within your jaws; may his life-breath abandon him.
The fixed direction has Viṣṇu as its overlord;
Kalmāṣagrīva is its protector; plants are its arrows. Homage to them, the overlords; homage!
Homage to the protectors; homage be to you, O arrows!
Him who hates us and him whom we hate, we place within your jaws; may his own breath abandon him.
The zenith has Bṛhaspati as its overlord, Citra as its protector, and thunderbolts as its arrows.
Homage to them, the overlords; homage!
Homage to the protectors; homage be to you, O arrows!
Him who hates us and him whom we hate, we place within your jaws; may his life-breath abandon him!
The ox has supported the earth and that heaven;
the ox has supported the broad mid-air;
the ox has supported the six wide quarters of space.
The ox has entered into this entire world.
The ox milks out the world of the well-performed deed;
may Pavamāna swell him from the front.
Parjanya is his rain-showers, the Maruts his udder;
sacrifice is his milk, the sacrificial fee his milking.
Indra is the ox; he looks out for the cattle.
He measures out the paths in three strides;
milking the world that has been and that is to be, he moves about upholding all the ordinances of the gods.
He whose master is neither the lord of the sacrifice nor the sacrifice itself, whose giver has no power over him, nor does the receiver;
he who sustains all and is the architect of all.
"Tell us of the *gharma*, whichever of the four-footed it may be.
This Indra moves among men;
the *gharma* has been heated and travels along, glowing brightly.
May he have good offspring; let him not sit among the noble ones who, knowing [the truth], would not eat of the oxen,
by which the gods ascended to heaven.
Having left behind the body, may we go by that [path] to the abode of immortality, to the world of the well-done,
through the observance of the *gharma*, through glory, and through ascetic heat.
They say these twelve nights belong to Prajāpati as days of observance;
even there, it is the vow of Brahman.
In that regard, there is also the strength of oxen.
As for those twelve nights which they call the observance-nights of Prajāpati:
Even there, he who knows that Brahman— the strength of the ox—
milks the ox in the evening.
They milk it in the morning, they milk it by day; may we know those streams of his that flow together, following one another.
He who knows the seven milkings of the Vedas, which yield their fruit,
attains both progeny and the world.
Likewise, the Seven Seers know this:
"This is the middle of the ox, whereon this burden is placed."
So much is his eastern part as he is concentrated in the west,
treading upon the earth with his feet.
Digging up the earth with his shanks,
the ox reaches the sweet drink through his toil, and the plowman likewise reaches it.
"Indra is called 'the ox' among men;
let his hooves not be injured."
And all his joints:
"O Indra, you are the Supreme by your power, the Vratapati by your vow; as the cow is, so indeed is the Vaiśvadeva."
Whoever hates us, and whoever we hate—seize his vital breaths; tear apart his vital breaths! (PS 3.25.14, Anuvāka 5)
I go to my home with a joyful mind,
bearing strength, possessing wealth and wisdom,
with a non-terrible, friendly eye.
Beholding the houses, I cross over toward the milk.
These houses are blissful, full of vigor, and full of milk.
Standing full of desirable wealth,
may they, who know, recognize us who know.
May they be possessed of truth and blessed.
Possessing wealth, laughing with joy,
free from hunger and free from thirst—
O house, do not be afraid of us!
Those from whom we study while living abroad,
and in whom there is much goodwill— for them we call upon their homes.
May they know us from afar;
like cattle invited hither, so are goats and sheep invited hither.
And furthermore, the sweet essence of food is invited into our homes;
those possessing abundant wealth are invited.
May our friends be joyful in sweet delights;
may all our men be unharmed, and may our homes be secure at all times.
May he be invincible; may Indra, the victorious one who overcomes hostile armies, be our protector.
Prajāpati has bestowed vital power upon him.
With the great oblation, with the strengthening of the offering—
O Prajāpati, by means of the strengthening of the oblation,
you made Indra the slayer of the one who cannot be slain.
To him the tribes created by the gods bow down;
for he has become the slayer [of enemies] and the one to be invoked.
O Prajāpati, lead us toward greater prosperity.
Increasing the wide pasture,
O subduer of adversaries, you increase Indra for great delight.
With divine oblation that causes increase, O God,
so that you may conquer all hostile armies, and so that, overcoming your enemies, you may be victorious.
Just as he is a sovereign, a true sovereign,
so may Indra make you invincible;
let this hero strike down the enemies without opposition.
O All-Gods, make a seat for him;
let them not harm his offspring nor his heroes. May Indra make this man invincible.
Conquer the enemies; subject them to yourself—[read "prati"?]—Agni is your protector and Vasiṣṭha is your overlord; may King Varuṇa grant you shelter.
Thus may Indra make you invincible.
May you two touch one another with your bodies, with your faces, and with your very selves.
May Brahmaṇaspati and Soma unite you both; may he cause you to touch one another with this name through speech.
I hold him; he shall not be released.
By my power, I have seized him in his desire, like a black beast in its pen.
That love which was bestowed by the brown Soma upon the beloved—
listen to me concerning that.
His mind is placed upon me.
Whatever man you desire, or in whomsoever you seek fortune—
We shall instill grief in his heart so that it withers away after you,
so that his heart may wither.
Even while my limbs were being severed,
I beheld the terrifying eye of space; O Bhaṭṭa, even as I was being cut, I gazed upon that which is of the nature of space.
That which brings about what is most dear has been brought by Madhughu;
you indeed are the possessor of splendor.
Furthermore, you are Sumaṅgala;
furthermore, you are said to be the bringer of prosperity to all plants.
O herb, you turn toward Soma; you turn toward the Sun;
you turn toward all the gods.
Thus we speak to you with truth:
I dig up this herb,
the far-reaching one that has no end.
One who comes from afar is to be welcomed; one who departs for the far distance is to be bid farewell.
"I [bid farewell] to him as he departs."
I have seized the far-reaching mind; I have seized the mind that is in the hands,
and also the mind that is in the heart.
Your mind is placed in me, your heart in me, and your vow in me;
you shall also be in my ritual act.
Place it in my heart!
Let me speak, and not you; do not speak in the assembly.
You are mine alone;
do not mention the names of other women,
even if you are hidden from people.
Or even across the rivers—
this herb shall bring you down to me, as if bound with a cord.
"Just as a sixteenth part," thus one [verse].
"Together the kings have come, together the debts have come, together the kuṣṭhas have come, together the clans have come."
May we bestow good dreams upon ourselves, and cast the evil dream upon our enemy.
Bhaṭṭa: [This is] a bad dream;
it is the embryo of the wives of the gods, the instrument of Yama.
Whatever dream is auspicious, let that be mine; whatever is evil, we send forth to our enemy.
O Tṛṣṇāmā, you are the mouth of the black bird, the mouth of Nirṛti.
We know you thus,
O Sleep. As such, like a horse without a body, like a horse without a bridle, seize the one who hates us, the scorner of the gods.
Whatever evil dream is among us, whatever [evil dream] is among our cattle, and whatever is in our house— that which is not ours, let the hater of the gods, the one who hates, [take it away].
As if putting on a golden ornament,
may they fasten [it] around our bodies after measuring out nine cubits.
All bad dreams and all evil occurrences, we cast away upon our enemy. (PS 3.30.7,
Anuvāka 6)
O gods, Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, give us water; cleave open the ocean from the sky, from the earth, and from the vast intermediate space.

Agni, Indra, Sūrya—
