The gods, the fathers, the lowest ones, the Āyavas,
the Krāvyāpas—
O gods who sit in the waters, O son of the waters, Tanūnapāt, Narāśaṃsa—
give us water, cleave the ocean!
O divine Bṛhaspati, bestow the waters; split open the ocean. (…);
O divine Prajāpati, bestow the waters; split open the ocean.
(…) O God Parameṣṭhin, bestow the waters; break open the ocean;
[pour them] from heaven, from the earth, and from the wide intermediate space.
To this sovereignty, with this sacred word (*brahman*), for these subjects, for these plants— *svāhā*!
[To those] being born from Prajāpati.
And these offspring that have been born— make them known to him; may he,
the wise one, grant his approval.
Those animals over whom Paśupati is lord— whether they be four-footed or two-footed—
they go to the world, purchased as those worthy of sacrifice.
May the increase of wealth attend the sacrificer.
Releasing [the sacrificial horse], O gods, guardians of the world, grant a path for the sacrificer.
May that which has been brought forward, being purified, stand firm;
may it go to the dear path of the gods. Those who, meditating upon him as he is being bound...
They looked after them with their minds and their eyes;
may the god Agni, Prajāpati, in agreement with his offspring, release them first.
Those whose lives were bound together in a herd of cattle, as well as those of beasts and men—
Indra, the god, released them first.
Prajāpati, being in harmony with his offspring:
those wild animals that are multiform, and those that are multiform or even uniform.
May the god Vāyu release them first, and may Prajāpati, in harmony with his offspring,
[release them]; may the gods, knowing [them], accept them.
The vital breath that has departed from the limbs: go to heaven, find firm support through your bodies,
and proceed to the celestial realm by auspicious paths.
O Agni, may the seasons and the years increase you, along with the seers and those truths;
shine forth with splendor and with light.
Illumine all four quarters.
O Agni, be kindled and awaken this man;
rise up for great good fortune.
May those who sit near you not come to harm here;
may these Brahmins of yours be glorious, and no others.
O Agni, these Brahmins choose you.
O Agni, be auspicious and a furtherer for us; O Agni, be a slayer of rivals and a conqueror of adversaries. Shine in your own dwelling, never failing.
Right here, O Agni, bestow upon us a stream of wealth;
let not those who act with malice and harbor ancient grudges deceive you.
O Agni, may sovereign power be easy for you to govern.
May those who approach thee prosper; mayst thou be unassailable.
O Agni, take hold with thy own sovereign power;
O Agni, strive for the bond of friendship with Mitra.
O Agni, worthy of invocation among kings, shine here in the midst of your kinsmen;
overcome the deceivers and overcome the powers of destruction.
Beyond hostilities, beyond enmities— for you, O Agni, cross over all difficulties—
therefore grant us wealth together with heroic sons.
Invincible, Jātavedas, unsubdued, O Agni, shine here as a sovereign ruler with [your] powers;
driving away diseases from human beings.
Protect our household today with auspicious dwellings.
This is your seasonal womb, from which born you shone forth.
Knowing that, O Agni, ascend it,
and then increase our wealth for us. We invoke the giver.
To Agni, the fierce one for our protection, who is pure and the greatest slayer of Vṛtra;
O Agni, speak here to us.
Turn toward us with a gracious mind;
bestow upon us, O Lord of the People, for you are the giver of wealth to us.
May Aryaman grant us [wealth], may Bhaga, may Bṛhaspati,
may Pūṣan, and may Sūnṛtā grant it to us.
May the Goddess bestow wealth upon us.
Urge Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, and Indra to grant their gifts.
Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and the vigorous Savitṛ;
and King Soma for protection.
We invoke Agni with songs of praise,
Āditya, Viṣṇu, Sūrya,
and Bṛhaspati the Brahman.
We invoke Indra, Vāyu, and Bṛhaspati, who are easy to call, so that all this world may be ours.
May he be well-disposed toward our assembly.
O Agni, through your fires, increase our sacred word and our sacrifice.
O God, impel us to give wealth for our gift.
This has come into being at the impulse of strength.
And within him are all these worlds;
knowing [all], he causes even one who is unwilling to give to bestow.
May he grant us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
May the five directions yield for me; may the wide expanses yield according to my strength.
May I attain every intention.
With mind and with heart,
may I utter speech that wins cattle;
cover me with splendor.
May Vāyu restrain [the enemy] from every side;
may Tvaṣṭṛ be established for our prosperity. O Indra, from whatever we fear...
Therefore, grant us fearlessness;
O Maghavan, be gracious to us with your aids;
strike down our enemies and our adversaries.
We invoke Indra for success; may we prosper with our two-footed and four-footed creatures.
Let not hostile armies assail us.
O Indra, destroy the malevolent ones who strike from all sides.
May Indra, the protector, the slayer of Vṛtra, our supreme defender, be our excellent guardian.
May he be our protector from behind, may he be from the middle; may he be at our back and in front of us.
O Knower, lead us toward a wide world.
O Indra, sacrifice for heaven, for light, for fearlessness,
and for well-being! O Indra, we would dwell under the protection of your two mighty, firm, and great arms.
May the atmosphere grant us fearlessness; may both heaven and earth grant us fearlessness; may there be fearlessness from behind and fearlessness from before.
May there be safety for us from above and from below;
may there be safety from the friend, safety from the enemy, safety from our kinsmen, and safety before us.
May there be fearlessness for us by night and fearlessness by day; may all directions become my friends. (PS 3.35.6, Anuvāka 7)
Go forth to victory; do not falter;
tear asunder the wealth of the enemies.
Indra, the slayer of rivals, is terrible.
Saṃjaya has brought you together;
you are victorious, O Maghavan, never defeated in battle, whether small or great.
Even you, the fierce one, we sharpen for our protection; as such, O Indra, be gracious to us in our invocations.
Your arms are winners of cattle, possessing unequalled power in battle.
O you of a hundredfold aids, who make your own deeds effective;
Indra is beyond calculation, his might is incomparable.
As such, O Indra, be gracious to us in our invocations.
I know the beloved Indra, his treasure-store, that secret name of his which is in the encounter;
he, the bounteous one, shall surely conquer and be mine.
May our warrior come to our call in the invocation;
may we, supported by you, be victorious. In every battle, raise up our portion.
O Indra, grant us wide space and an easy path;
O Maghavan, shatter the manly strength of our enemies.
We invoke you as the first among the gods.
You have been the conqueror in battles;
O Indra, in this furtherance, make our singer Upamanyu a breaker-through and place his chariot in the lead.
Remember! You are Smara;
you have been given by the gods as Smara.
Remember the mind of such-and-such a person!
Just as I desire, so let it be:
O Desire, burn his heart;
let the fever of the limbs consume him; let him grieve within himself.
His intentions are stilled by his thoughts; this alone is his direction, while all other directions are joyless, bewildered, and deluding to the mind.
O forest-dwellers, you who cause destruction, you who possess the power of possession, you who cause trees to grow—
you who are here, I send you away with a sacred prayer.
Heart-cutters, season-givers, village-destroyers, dream-breakers, strikers, slayers, mind-bewilders, possessors,
those who cause flight, and those that cause growth.
These I send forth with a sacred prayer:
Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, and today both Heaven and Earth and Mātariśvan.
May the Aśvins, the god Savitṛ, and Bhaga strike your mind with exhaustion here;
may the thirty-three gods also strike you down.
Let the wealthy ones bring their hearts to you; may the hymns of Bharadvāja be master over you.
Like a ship released from its moorings, float away!
These wealthy women fall like lightning flashes during the rainy season;
become the recipient of their gifts.
Like cows in the cow-pen at evening, I cause your mental anxieties to settle down and fall away from your head. I make them enter into you [as a dwelling].
Let these women sit near you, pricking you and awakening you.
I send forth these yearnings of yours with a sacred prayer.
The Tṛprā demons, led by Aśrī,
shall wither you like a blade of grass; moreover, they shall make you weep bitterly.
For the unborn was born from the heat of Agni;
he beheld his progenitor in the beginning.
By him the gods attained godhood in the beginning.
By that, O Rohas, ascending, you have surpassed those more worthy of sacrifice. Step forward with the fires toward the firmament,
bearing the fire-pan in your hands.
Having gone to the back of heaven, the light-world, be united with the gods.
O Agni, go forward as the first of those who seek the gods.
The eye of gods and of mortals— may the sacrificers, desiring to sacrifice and being in harmony with the Bhr̥gus, go safely to the light of heaven.
Going to heaven, they look not back; may those who possess wealth ascend to the sky,
they who maintain the sacrifice on every side.
The very wise ones have spread it out.
I anoint the rice-mess with power and ghee,
the divine, vast ocean of milk.
By that, may we go to the world of the well-done, above the highest vault of heaven, where the lotuses bloom.
"Rising up from the earth... (PS 3.38.5).
"Those two wings of yours, the undecaying ones, belonging to you the bird, with which you drive away the *rakṣas* demons, O Rice."
Through these two, may we go to the world of the well-done, where the first-born seers of old abide,
standing upon the back of heaven.
O rice-offering, you have ascended into the sky;
the Brahmins, whose nature is truth, have followed along with the gift.
From the back of the earth I have ascended to the intermediate space; from the intermediate space I have ascended to heaven;
from the back of the firmament of heaven, I have gone to the light of the sun.
Unborn art thou; O Unborn, thou art heaven.
Knowing the world through thee, O Aṅgiras, may we attain that world.
By that path by which you carry a thousand, or by which you carry all one's possessions—
by that, carry this sacrifice of ours.
To go among the gods;
cook a goat and five portions of rice. Having cooked the goat and the five portions of rice, [offer it].
The gods have attained the worlds.
That offspring of yours which was formerly concealed, I bring it forth for you with the firm Aśvin.
Agni Vaiśvānara shall give that back to you from the highest heaven;
O Agni, you are a second, auspicious lord.
Grant her offspring that reaches old age; release her from the grasp of Grahī and Nirṛti, whatever binds her.
O Agni, bestow offspring upon her who desires offspring.
O Agni, this woman, longing for a son, bends her knee and worships you, the bull;
mount her with a benevolent mind.

Mount upon her, display your manly vigor; as a fierce bestower of seed, unite him with offspring from the mountain, from the womb of heaven.
From limb to limb,
the seed of every god is gathered;
I have placed it like a feather upon an arrow.

He who does not desire and does not grieve— [he is liberated].
He who supports you with a sharp point—
you are an ancient sharp point;

May that desire be of last year,
by which we desire her.

The Maruts bestowed abandonment upon me; all the gods bestowed abandonment upon me;

in the past, I abandoned those who were my enemies.
Before midday and before evening,
I have exerted myself;
for great strength lies in exertion.

"Let this desire of yours remain.

In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha came into being; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists.
He supported this earth and yonder heaven.
Let us worship that god with an oblation—
he who is the giver of vigor and the giver of strength, whose command all the gods revere.
To that God, whose shadow is immortality and whose [shadow] is death, let us offer worship with an oblation—
to Him who is the sustainer of all that breathes and all that blinks.
He has become the lord of the entire moving world— he who rules over its bipeds and its quadrupeds.
To that god let us do homage with an oblation.
By whom the fierce heaven and the firm earth were made stable, by whom the sun was supported and the firmament;
he who measured out the vast intermediate space.
Let us worship that god with an oblation—
he who, by his protection, supported and held firm these two trembling worlds, heaven and earth.
To that god upon whom the sun rises spread out, let us worship with an oblation;
he whose greatness all the snowy mountains acknowledge.
To him whose essence they say is the ocean,
whose [five] directions are the goddesses,
to that god we shall pay worship with an oblation.
In whom the waters, bestowing all life, generated the embryo as mothers—

the waters, generating the embryo,
sent forth the calf at the beginning.
As he was being born,
his amniotic membrane was golden;
his amniotic membrane was indeed golden.
A young calf was born;
the great Diti beheld him within her two quivering wombs.
Being among beings, he bestows milk;
he has become the sovereign lord of beings.

May that king approve of this kingdom:

"Mount [it], O increaser of friends;
the gods have spoken in favor of you.

great is that name of the bull-like Asura— he,
possessing all forms, has taken his stand upon the immortal realms.
Embracing this tiger, they urge on the lion for great good fortune,
like a well-favored buffalo standing firm.

stride forth through the great quarters of space.
May all the people come to you;
may the celestial waters, rich in milk, come to you—
those waters which rejoice in the celestial realm with their milk.

that which is yours, O Kaśyapa, the moon-like, radiant, well-composed, abundant, and of wondrous luster.

may the gods grant me wealth through sacrifice; may my prayer be fulfilled, and may my invocation of the gods be successful.
May the divine Hotṛs win this for us; may we be unharmed in body and rich in heroic sons.
O six divine expanses, grant us wide space!
O All-Gods, rejoice here!
May we not be abandoned by our offspring nor by our wealth; may we not fall into the power of the enemy, O King Soma.
May the far-reaching buffalo, invoked by many, rich in food, grant us protection in this contest;
O Lord of the tawny steeds, be gracious to our progeny.
—O Indra, do not harm us; do not abandon us!
Dhātṛ, the Ordainer, the Sustainer, who is the Lord of the world, the divine Savitṛ, the overcomer of adversaries.
May Bṛhaspati, Indra, Agni, both Aśvins,
and the gods protect the sacrificer from destruction. Summon hither the one who comes toward us.
May Indra be ours alone for victory and for conquering;
may he display his heroic power from here.
From over there we call Indra hitherward—
he who wins cattle, wins wealth, and wins horses; enjoy this sacrifice of ours at our invocation.
O Lord of the Bay Steeds, make you our ally.
Indra the protector, Indra the helper, the hero Indra who is easily invoked at every call— [we invoke him].
May we invoke Śakra, Indra invoked by many;
may the bountiful Indra protect us with well-being.
May the three goddesses grant me great protection.
Whatever is nourished for my progeny and for my body,
may the subjects, being of one mind, favor me;
may they recognize us as their own ancestral domain.
O Śakra, whoever as an enemy of Indra seeks to slay us with his arrogance—
O slayer of Vṛtra, do you destroy him!
Bring us wealth!
May those who curse us be far away;
with Indra and Agni we drive them off.
The Ādityas and Rudras, reaching toward the heights, have made me a fierce guardian and sovereign lord.
The Cow, the Earth, conceived Agni as her embryo.
Protect this earth; it is subject to you.
To her, to you, obeisance! To him, to you, svāhā!
The cow is the intermediate space; Vāyu is its embryo... (see 1abc) PS_5,5.2
The Cow is the sky; she has the sun as her embryo.
The Cow is the *ṛc*; she has the *sāman* as her embryo.
The Cow is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*); she has the sacrifice as her embryo.
The cow is excrement; she [bears] a Kṣatriya as her embryo.
Speech is the cow; she [bears] a Parameṣṭhin as her embryo. The cow is the cow; she [bears] a Rājanya as her embryo.
She is the equal, the barren cow; she bore the embryo for a year.
Protect this [embryo] for her; let there be what is to be performed for her; obeisance to her; to her, svāhā!
Section 1.
Seven suns have entered the sky;
the giver of sacrificial fees follows them along the path.
They all heat clarified butter for him.
Milking out vigor, not recoiling,
he burns down the lowly diseases of servitude while heating them thoroughly.
The sun rises with wings outspread, following the great [heavens];
we know the ancestors who have been heated by it.
We have subdued the Dasyus;
those others who, like suns, move according to their own nature in secret caves.
The sky accompanies the later generations; five other peoples dwell beyond the sky.
Into that vast sky has the sacred word (brahman) entered.
He who knows them thoroughly shall cross over;
he who gives, he who causes to give, or he who, full of faith, lays up treasures.
May Yama, the son of Vivasvat,
protect all treasures;
may those who wander about find them not.
Yama the King leads all those who rob the sacrificial gift (dakṣiṇā) once given along the path of misfortune.
May Agni, who knows the way, lead us by that path along which Yama, the son of Vivasvat, has gone from here as king.
Vaiśvānara, the maker of paths, the all-pervading one; a great light placed among mortals,
by which the gods overcame their enemies.
Thus may we all cross over this bridge, Vaiśvānara, the light that removes disease, O gods; we rise up from out of the darkness.
Beholding the higher light,
we have gone to Sūrya, the god among gods, the supreme light.
Āroka, Bhrāja, Paṭara, Pataṅga, Svarṇara, Jyotiṣīmant, and Vibhāsa—
all these heat the clarified butter for him.
Milking forth vigor, without faltering,
let the cloud-bearing quarters of the sky spring up;
let the clouds, driven by the wind, come together.
May the waters, lowing like the bellowing great bull of the wind,
satisfy the earth. The wind from all sides causes the clouds to look upon one another.
Let the torrents of water spring up in various directions;
let the outpourings of rain glorify the earth;
let herbs of every form be born everywhere.
Roar out, thunder, and strike the ocean;
O Parjanya, drench the earth with your milk! Through you, let abundant rain come forth, released.
May the one who seeks with longing, though thin and heavy, go to his setting.
O Maruts, raise yourselves up from the ocean;
let your brilliant rays cause the clouds to fly upward.
The powerful, bounteous ones cause the rain to fall;
may the plants be united with the essences of the waters.
Let the hosts of Maruts sing to you.
Let the separate streams of rain, sounding like thunderclouds as they pour down,
release their showers upon the earth.
May the bounteous ones protect us—
the springs, the serpents,
and the winds that send down the rain.
May they blow forth along the earth;
may the wind, the lightning, the cloud, and the rain—
those of liberal gifts— protect us all.
Swell forth, overflow;
unite the earth with milk.
Agni, in harmony with the bodies of the waters—
May he who has become the lord of the plants, Jātavedas, win rain for us—
the immortal breath from heaven for our offspring.
Let lightning flash in every direction, let the winds blow from every quarter, and let the clouds be driven forth by the Maruts.
May they rain down upon the earth.
Prajāpati, driving forth the waters from the primeval flood and from the ocean,
causes the sea to swell.
May the seed of the potent stallion swell;
come hither with this thundering,
pouring down the waters, O Asura, our father.
Let the water-vessels roar;
release the waters downward; let those with speckled arms speak out.
Like frogs from a dry pond,
the Brahmins who observe their vows have remained dormant for a year.
May their speech be quickened by Parjanya;
the frogs have begun to croak. O female frog, speak forth!
O Tādurī, speak forth the rain; float in the middle of the lake,
having spread out your four feet.
Pour forth the great treasure; let him be sprinkled with the lightning. Let the wind blow;
let the sacrifice, released in many ways, spread out.
May the plants be delightful!
As far as heaven and earth extend in breadth, or as far as the seven rivers have spread out.
I have expelled from here that speech which corrupts poison;
may the fair-winged Garuḍa take you away.
The poison first entered him; indeed,
it was not from his father that this affliction came upon him.
Did you read it? PS_5,8.2: You whom the five-fingered one drew from the curved bow;
From the two arms of Apaskambha,
I have spoken the poison away;
from the barb, I have spoken the poison away.
From the collyrium, from the leaf-container,
from the handle, from the horn, and from the tortoise-shell,
I have spoken the poison away.
Tasteless is the shaft of that arrow, and likewise tasteless is its poison; even so is the tree of which it comes.
The bow is for you, the essence of essences.
Those who have crushed, those who have ground, those who have cast forth, and those who have released— [all these are yours].
May they all be emasculated;
the poison-mountain has been made emasculated,
and emasculated be those who dug it.
You are castrated, O herb;
castrated is that mountain, the peak, from which this poison was born.
This water, brought from the protection of Varuṇa, wards off [evil]; therein is poured the nectar of immortality.
He made that poison tasteless with *khadira* water and then with *kaṅkata* tooth-wood.
Moreover, with that which is the poison of poison,
with the hundred-jointed spell, I have destroyed the evils.
With the thousand-eyed hide and with sharp spades,
we drive out the Sadānvās.
O powerful one, you are full of power; from here the Kaṇvas have driven away the enemies who have now arrived.
Those graspers (*grahaṇī*) which were here before—
neither they nor those here have entered me;
like a cauldron, the head is [separated] by the horns.
O Brahmanaspati,
come hither like a sharp-horned bull;
your churning-sticks have indeed been set in motion.
Your milking vessel has been split;
today the cow has given to you, O Kaṇva. Go forth, I shall crush the one who is lower.
Those that dwell in the reasoning, those in the surface,
those that swing upon the swing and those that are indeed terrible, and those that seize the embryos— [may they be appeased].
I have destroyed all evil things—
those which wear a garment,
and those which are dark, tawny, or even red.
I have destroyed all those wicked ones who touch the fetuses,
whether they are tearing them out or crushing them.
Bind up his breath as well!
O all you women of ill-repute, having come together,
let not even a trace of that man's leavings remain.
This [soma], struck by the pestle and ground upon the stone, is pressed with poison; it is a glowing fire, a glowing heaven.
Become heat within the sun!
O *tokman*, those who caused the poison to grow said to you: "Flow like poison into the jar!"
Poison is your seat, O goddess;
poison is placed in your hand; be you possessed of poison as your weapon.
Let rice be your lion; let the porridge be your tiger;
let the *nagnahu* plant be your viper.
Flow together into the heart of the wolf! This [goddess],
who was poured into the vessel,
wearing a garland of young grass and sounding aloud—
Varāhamanyu, O Ajani,
afflict Uttānapāda; you are the one who causes swelling and the one who causes falling away.
Tawny with dust, crying out in distress,
with anger uprooted— you were born;
what was behind, place that in front!
O Viṣṇu, let poison be in your wind;
O Śakra, let blood be in your vessel. Let them churn one another.
From you come the quivers, from you the bow;
these gods, the drinkers of poison and drinkers of blood, are the mortals who drink for the sake of power.
Some are slain while others fight;
praise that greatness of the Surā.
Those plants flow forth with power.
—Fly up! Intoxicate him for the sake of battle!
Let him, with his jewel-bands shattered and his head split open, encounter his own blood;
let the drunkard, his garment ruined and streaming, meet his end.
Drink this poison-mixed liquor with joy,
blended with fat and mixed with blood;
with his hand severed, he wanders within the village.
Bartering away many acts of hostility,
I lead forth [the waters] from the hundredfold [source], accompanied by swords and arrows.
Intoxicate them, intoxicate them completely; make them swell like a serpent,
so that not one of them remains for the other.
Section 2.
May Agni grant his consent to you; may Varuṇa grant his consent to you. From that, may a son be born to you.
May he, clad in armor, fight for the cattle.
O Vāyu, recognize this; O Indra and Bṛhaspati, recognize this!
We prepare the collyrium that brings the knowledge of a son; we perform the rite for the birth of a male child,
by which this [embryo] is firmly established.
Since you do not obtain a son,
O Indra and Agni, may you two protect us from that sin day by day.
May the Atharvans, the Aṅgirases, and all the gods who increase the cosmic order hear my invocation today.
For this son to find [the way],
may Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, Sinīvālī, and Aditi [be his protectors].
May Varutri, the fierce mistress of wives,
point out a son to you today; O Mitra and Varuna, grant a son to you.
May the goddess Sarasvatī grant you a son;
may both the Aśvins, adorned with lotus garlands, grant you a son.
And those whose names I have grasped, and those whose I have not remembered—
all those gods, having assembled together, [acted].
Bestowing upon you a son who grants long life,
fashion him from your own self;
let him be born from you.
You are the seed; like a fertile field, you bear it in the womb together with the earth and the sacrifices.
May the Sun together with the constellations,
and the Wind together with the winged birds,
designate a son for you today.
The bull, the giver of joy, was born from these honeyed [waters];
he has lain upon your womb.
Becoming a man full of skill,
go to the womb; O Madhavan,
become a man within the womb.
Then again,
with his head turned back, he pushed down his hips like an arrow from a quiver.
Making it dear to his parents as if [making] his own,
he did not harm the two hips within,
as he was being born in the tenth month.
At the end of the year, he turns back again,
so that you may live with prosperity.
May he support you in great prosperity. I have fashioned your womb with auspiciousness for the sake of good progeny.
Pour therein your unimpaired virility for the ten-month-old [child];
let the embryo lie within your womb.
The embryo lies within the chorion;
the youth lies within the amnion.
Fashioned by Tvaṣṭṛ according to its joints;
O King Madhavan, just as you cause the seed to sprout.
Thus, O Madhavas, having placed the embryo, split this womb apart from the boy.
May the divine Bṛhaspati [bestow] the embryo;
may Indra and Agni [bestow] the embryo for you;
may Dhātṛ bestow the embryo upon you.
O Śiva, Jātavedas, go together with the auspicious ones and with your own body; bestowing treasure, be well-disposed toward us from the front.
I winnow you from the houses for the sake of splendor.
O Gharma, you are supported on the earth, established in the intermediate space, and resting in heaven.
May the sky protect him on all sides— he who cooks this rice for you.
Those who sent forth the ocean and those who sent forth the river;
Those gods who travel through the atmosphere, the earth, and the sky, or those who go in a chariot with the wind—
the cooking of the rice porridge reaches them here.
By the *ṛc* the pot is placed upon the fire;
by the *sāman* the rice is cooked.
I consider this to be a stalk of Soma.
This oblation is for the Viśvedevas:
whatever has been attached to the mortar, the pestle, the winnowing basket, the ground, or the cooking pot.
Whatever drops and whatever washings there are—all that I fill for you with the sacred word (brahman).
Go upward; do not falter.
Having transcended the intermediate space of this world and having overcome all the *rakṣas* demons,
you have now ascended to heaven.
Be swift for us, do not be weary;
may he be established with our prayers,
united with the earth and with Agni.
Together with the rays of the sun,
together with the activity of the gods,
he has driven away his enemies to the world of the well-done.
In the third firmament, in the luminous realm of heaven,
go now along after having effaced the track of death by means of this effacement of the track. PS_5,13.8 (13)
You are the face of prosperity, the ray of truth; you of high renown, go to heaven.
May you two, the preparers of the oblation, rise up.
"Excellent! Worship the gods;
remove the *ṛjīṣa*. O divine waters, you who perform the sacrifice..."
The goddesses are variegated, prepared with oblations;
the rice cooked in a single vessel is commensurate with the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
O Gāyatrī, you are the bearer of oblations;
you are kindled as the divine Agni in the world of well-performed deeds, which flows with a thousand streams.
The two immortals, whose backs are anointed with ghee,
ate austerity and truth as their rice-meat, O Supreme Lords.
From those two, indeed, the light was brought;
therefore you are called the Overlord,
O wide-striding one.
Measured by the breath of the wind,
strike away my adversaries;
may I be released from distress.
Drive away the Rākṣasas with your splendor;
offer the oblation to the gods through song.
You are expansive and far-reaching.
Let the fair-winged one fly high up to heaven;
do not make him dear to the gods, but deliver me over to the seers.
Consume the semen with semen;
let the doers of good deeds drink the honey.
The two kinds of gods have come to our sacrifice.
May the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases, whom this rice pleases and who have been questioned, partake of this heavenly food,
having sat down according to the seasons.
We collect this first portion of nectar, of milk, of clarified butter, and of food;
we send forth this share to those who have not yet been offered oblations.
May the gods accept this our oblation; the divine ones,
some eaters of what is offered and others eaters of what is unoffered, both together partake of the Vaiśvadeva oblation.
May they, being well-disposed, rejoice here; exhilarate yourself with nourishment and vigor for the sacrificer.
May Bhava not slay these, nor may Śarva slay the cattle.
Let not the *klomaśva* find our calves;
those born and those still within the womb,
may they, unharmed, O Agni, seize the breast.
May these cows be prolific and rich in offspring;
may they be of one mind with the women.
May the gods bestow abundance upon them.
I unite their calves with long life and with fatness.
Let the cows and the women go forth;
Viṣṇu prepares the womb.
Receiving the seed of the bull,
the ox follows the female;
he does not harm anything that is offered before him.
Prepare the sweet Soma-drink according to your desire; may the non-eaters of oblations lead the sacrifice successfully;
may riches and prosperity attend the sacrificer.
Let not your footsteps sink into the earth, nor into the rivers; let the plants rise up, let the refreshing waters flow forth;
O Maruts, strike the ocean upon the ridges of Parjanya.
May the grain ripen in abundance; may the world rejoice.
There are seven seers, seven seats for them, ten fingers belonging to the Aśvins, and five strengths.
May Prāṇa, Vyāna, Mind, Intention, and the Goddess Speech,
knowing [the way], carry the oblation to the gods—
those who are seen and those who are unseen.
The worms and those that are kikṛśa—
their heads I cut off with a sword;
then I unite their calves with life-force and fat.
Section 3.
May Heaven and Earth together milk forth this sacrifice;
may Mātariśvan and Pavamāna from the east, and Tvaṣṭṛ and Vāyu along with Soma and Vāta [do the same].
May they milk this [cow] for us without faltering.
I heat the Gharma with a stream of immortality;
I offer the oblation to the gods and to Savitṛ.
O gods, eat the clarified butter, the cooked oblation, which we have offered with the ladle into the womb of immortality.
We have caused it to rise from the fire; we have prepared the cooked oblation.
Ascend the back, the seat of immortality!
O trees, spread the sacrificial grass; prepare it all around with honey and ghee.
The wasting disease that is in the waters, I pacify that for you; with vigor, I anoint this pasture for you. I make your milk from the breast free from poison.
Even while sucking this life-breath, they come to the herd.
May the sons of Iḍā and those of Mitra,
not being hostile, suckle their milk.
May the crops be well-ordered by the seasons;
may the watchful guardian Vāyu protect these.
Drink the clarified butter; this is yours in many ways.
That which was placed in the cave and deposited among men,
and all the gods and Vaiśvadeva in the fire— rejoice in your respective portions of the oblation.
You who are the best among the gods, Rudra, the bull who moves along the threads—
may our heroes be unharmed.
Let this be your oblation:
"I make [him] full, possessing cattle,
possessing hundreds, and possessing thousands."
O Agni, together with all the gods,
ascend this cow-pen for him who has been driven mad by divine offense.
From hereditary disease and from curses—
may the gods release you from that,
from madness, and from the *rakṣas*.
O Agni, as we move around you, the silent sage, may you drive away the shrieking demons;
therefore, O powerful one, protect us from there.
May I be exhilarated by Indra for great delight,
just as the wise divine Ṛbhus, O Agni,
released the mad sage from his sin.
Thus may Śakra grant you fearlessness; be released from sin, and I drive away the demon.
Just as cattle [return] to the earth...
And men who dwell in their own homes—
may the earth take back the mind of you, O sage, who are thus like one insane.
The earth supports the sage; the sky protects the sage;
indeed, all beings support the sage.
Indra has supported the sage; I drive the demon far away from you.
O Agni, release this man for me.
He who, being possessed by the Grāhis, prattles on—
on his account you should provide a portion [of the remedy], so that he may become free from madness and free from disease.
May Agni pacify that which is stirred up in your mind as it is being carried forth.
I offer the oblation to you, O wise one, so that you may remain undemented. (See Lubotsky 2002, 90) PS_5,17.7
May the Apsarases restore you; may Vāta restore you; may the quarters of space restore you;
may Yama restore you; and may the messengers of Yama restore you.
May they release you from distress,
so that you may live and not die, and for your safety.
O gods, lift up again that which has been cast down;
O gods, [lift up] even one who is about to die.
O divine ones, you have made [this] for me to live. I have come to you with healing remedies— yes, with healing remedies—
and furthermore, with means for safety.
I have brought you what is skillful and auspicious; I drive away that which causes illness. These two winds blow.
From the ocean or from afar,
may one wind bring you strength, and may the other blow away whatever is harmful.
O Vāta, blow hither healing; O Vāta, blow away whatever is disease, for you are the possessor of all remedies.
You go as the messenger of the gods.
May the gods protect him;
may the Maruts with their hosts protect him.
May all beings protect [him], so that this may be free from disease;
with clarified butter, [I honor] Heaven and Earth.
Sprinkle the waters with ghee;
through ghee, free yourself from the sin which you have committed against yourself.
This hand of mine is the Blessed One; this [hand] of mine is the even more blessed one;
this [hand] of mine is the universal medicine.
That which is the auspicious touch;
with his two ten-fingered hands,
the tongue is the forerunner of speech.
With those two which are healing and auspicious,
we touch you.
Water indeed is a remedy.
The waters drive away disease; the waters are the remedy for everything.
May they provide a remedy for you.
I create for you a state of shared heart, harmony, and freedom from enmity;
love one another.
Like a cow toward her newborn calf,
let the son be devoted to his father and of one accord with his mother.
May the wife speak honeyed and peaceful words to her husband;
may the brother not hate his brother.
Do not [speak ill] of your sister, nor of a sister;
being united and of one vow, utter speech with auspiciousness.
That by which the gods do not depart nor hate one another—
that *brahman* we establish in your home.
May there be mutual recognition among men;
may you, who are superior, wise, and harmonious, not fall apart,
but move together in concord, striving for success.
Speaking pleasantly to one another,
come together as a united group;
your water-drink is common, and your share of food is shared.
With a single yoke I bind you together;
united, worship Agni as spokes surround the nave.
With that oblation by which the worshipful gods struck away evil,
wrath, anger, falsehood, and fury—
We cast far away the evil speech that causes grief and consumption;
I make you all turn toward one another with a common mind.
With one finger, may we be united in heart through this conciliation;
like the gods guarding immortality,
may your assembly be well-ordered both evening and morning.
Go away, go far away; move away, move far away; depart further still, with the rush of fire and wind.
I drive you away!
This is the path of water;
this is the breaking-place of the wind.
This is the path of the smoke of fire; there is no crossing over for you here. May the one with the black track pass around you.
Agni [is known] by smoke and flame;
therefore, O cutter, go forth as a cutter— cut another plant than the barley.
Those arrows sent by the Asuras and those sent by the gods—
all of them we [ward off] with the sacred word (brahman).
We crush the locusts.
Of the male locust, the female locust, the grasshopper, and the winged one—
Perhaps we might even bind the mouth of the winged thunderbolt, or of the rushing wind. (PS 5.20.5) following Bhaṭṭa.
This is the medicine that is in the cow, gathered together from every form— from the mole, the wood-boring beetle, and the boring insect.
Even with their sinews they are bound.
You have been seen by your scent—
you are the medicinal herb that crushes wood-worms.
Crush with your splendor those things born of the wood-boring worm; let it consume the cotton, the wood, and the grass.
The rat is the root, driven by thought;
likewise, let the woodworms eat the pith of the tree, not the grain.
Section 4.
May Heaven be our father and Earth our mother,
and may Agni, the watcher of men, Jātavedas,
drive the fever downward and away from us.
May the ten days drive far away from us the fever,
O Takman, whose portion of the earth’s surface I have assigned to you in its eastern half.
Having passed over that, you then strike us;
indeed, the seizing one with the leprous head will seize you, O Takman. These are the mountains.
The Himavant mountains have Soma upon their backs; they have made the wind our messenger and physician.
Let it destroy these Maruts.
Neither women nor any men at all desire you; here there is no longing for feverish passion.
The small one weeps, not the great one.
Do not harm us from the great; do not harm us from the greater than the great. You [are] the great.
O tawny one, do not harm the boys;
do not harm our girls—
[you] who cause them to fly up together.
The phlegm and the cough arising from water—
O Takman, your weapons are terrible;
with them, avoid us!
The immortal thousand-eyed one does not delight in another's field; Takman has indeed become an object of longing.
He indeed will show us mercy.
O Takman, neither horses nor cows are yours here, nor are your homes here.
The slayer of Muṣṭiha of Śakambhara; go again to the Mahāvṛṣas,
you two who put winter to sleep by your might.
— We choose the benevolent favor of Bhava and Rudra, who are either on this side of the gods or beyond the sky;
let their poison of evil pass away from us.
To him who, being born from his own vital power, stretches out the sky and supports the mid-region—
to that Rudra, let us do honor with an oblation.
—let the poison of our sin pass away elsewhere.
the refrain (2d, 3d, …, 8e, 9e)
It is written in KPS 5.22.2:
"For the destruction of whom nothing whatsoever occurs— neither among the gods nor among humans."
With oblation let us worship those two Rudras;
may the poison of evil depart from us.
They who rule over the animals of the earth...
Whether they be four-footed or those that are two-footed— to those two Rudras we shall offer oblation;
let the poison of evil pass away from us.
To him, at whose command both the wild animals and the domestic animals enter their dwellings—
to that Rudra we shall offer worship with an oblation.
—Let the poison of our sin depart elsewhere! From whom all plants proceed when they are being gathered, and from whom all trees do not depart; [from him let it go].
Before whom all creatures move in fear—
to that Rudra let us pay worship with an oblation; may his deadly poison pass away from us.
To him who, being most wise, fashioned the mountains, who ordains all beings with full knowledge— to that Rudra we shall offer worship with an oblation.
— let the poison of our sin depart elsewhere.
As far as these two lords range over his bipeds and quadrupeds, [so far let it go].
To those two fierce Rudras, who possess swift bows, let us pay worship with an oblation;
may their poison of evil pass away from us.
Again give us sight, again breath, again life, O Jātavedas;
O Rudra, you whose medicine is cooling.
May we, as the wise, worship you with this oblation; may the poison of evil depart from us.
You are the lord of healing remedies.
We choose thee for victory;
Sarasvān has placed within the wheel a thousandfold power— O herb, [we choose] thee!
I have called upon all the plants— those that conquer truth, those that protect through oath, those that endure, and those that bring back life.
"Do not cross over from here!"—
thus she who cursed with a curse, or she who indeed laid a snare.
Or that which was undertaken for the consumption of the sap— may it devour the offspring;
for you indeed have backward-fruited.
O Apāmārga,
you have come into being; drive away all curses from me to a greater distance.

All that is beneath our feet.
That which they prepared for you in an unbaked vessel, or that which they placed in a thread, blue and red;
With that *kṛtyā* which they have fashioned against raw flesh, destroy the practitioners of magic;

The demonic power, the Arāyī-demons,
the evil speakers, and all that is ill-omened— we cause all that to perish from here.
O Apāmārga, through you may we [overcome] the death of hunger, the death of thirst, childlessness, and lack of offspring.
All that we wipe away.

From the ignorant Hara, may he return and fall back into his home, like a lowing calf toward its mother. PS_5,24.2
He who, having attributed his own evil to another, seeks to strike him down with it—

O you of a thousand abodes,

Bring back the spell that was performed against the one who performed it,

She has pressed her foot and her toe;
she has brought us fortune,
she who was without fortune, from those who possess fortune.
By means of this herb, I have neutralized all sorceries—
those which they have performed against my field and those against my cattle.

Drive away the female sorceresses,
drive away all the *arāyyas*,
having wiped away the sorcerers.
Drive away all Arāyyas;
O Apāmārga, be with us for the sake of progeny and wealth.

Cut him down like autumnal reeds;
you have been summoned by the Brahmin Kaṇva Nārṣada.
O herb, you who seek out armies and possess splendor, there is no fear where you reach.

you are also the protector of the simple-minded.
And you shall be the slayer of the Rākṣasas.

Therefore, O herb, you were born as Apāmārga,
splitting [the obstacles] with your hundred branches.
Vibhindu by name is your father; split him asunder who assails us.
From the non-existent ground it arose; that lofty word ascends to heaven;
from there it sends forth smoke.
Let it reach the doer face-to-face;
for you have come forth facing [us], you whose fruit is directed toward us.
Having turned back the sorceries, strike down that one who fashioned the sorcery.
Protect me with a hundredfold!
Protect me with a thousandfold!
O Indra, lord of plants, the fierce one has bestowed his vigor upon you.
Section 5.
O Heaven and Earth, cut away the root of Arāti, and likewise her head; having severed her ribs in the middle, let her be split asunder.
Make her fall beneath your feet!
O Jātavedas, hear these words of mine from that woman.
O Aśvins, [drive away] the entire head of Arāti; [ask] the great question regarding her who wanders in sleep.
Having become a cow among the people,
O Indra, do you strike down the enemy; let Agni burn him with his heat.
May King Varuṇa, the most excellent for me, come to my invocation with truth; having struck down hostility, may he fulfill our desire.
May the fierce goddess protect us;
may she who is the guide, Sinīvālī, and the seven Śrotyās [protect us].
May all beings slay the enemy, as one slays a female slave for her offense; King Soma, together with the plants.
May both the Sun and the Moon,
all the Gandharvas, and the Apsarases destroy every enemy.
Bhava is the king; Bhava and Āśarva, Indra, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Pūṣan are my overseers.
May those gods who roam upon the earth and those who dwell in heaven always destroy our enemies.
Those who rule over the intermediate space,
may they, being of one accord, destroy the enemy.
And those who are impelled by the Asuras...
And that which is sent forth by the gods,
and that which is born of wrath— I slay that malice with a sacred prayer.
That indeed has now appeared to me: a great spirit, a vast form, when Nirṛti, with all the gods as her constant allies, [assailed me].
He is born here from death;
though he was once immortal, he spread himself out and consumed the serpent who roared with power.
Crush even Kutsa Atithigva’s life-force;
destroy Nikilbida with your might,
as far as heaven and earth extend in breadth.
As far as the seven rivers extend in their greatness, so far reaches Nirṛti, the possessor of all boons,
she who knows of everything that is being born.
For you, O Goddess, have become the mistress of prosperity for all that is born and all that thrives;
homage be to you, Nirṛti; do not harm us.
Do not strike another with your superior arm;
considering Nirṛti to be a goddess, I shall follow her with my words as a father follows his son.
She who knows every head of the being that is born,
following after each head like the sun—
seek out him who does not press the soma and does not sacrifice.
Follow the track of the thief, the robber;
seek him while he sleeps.
O Nirṛti, homage be to you; I pay you reverence.
Seeking to devour those who do not offer oblations, Nirṛti—
whose father is not known, nor her mother—
has struck down everything from the midst of her sisters.
The divine power of the gods did not reach that which was born as the bright light on the further shore of darkness.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, may you, the guardian of the world, help us cross over our enemies with your splendor as we are being released.
May the sacrificial animal here come to its share for us;
may Agni, the god who knows, carry the threefold, seven-threaded sacrifice—the oblation to the gods—to the deities. PS_5,28.1
Those two fangs of yours, well-biting and eager to wound,
which are bared and look about toward the south—
may our fathers make that harmless for us.
We have released the food that was bound to the sacrificial post; undecayed and unsoiled, go forth— you,

May the wise seers cleanse you thoroughly; exhilarate yourself with nourishment and strength for the sake of the sacrificer. With the seven seers, including Atri, may I [purify] you.
I receive this pleasant offering in the world;
may Jamadagni, Kaśyapa, and Bharadvāja make this food sweet and honeyed.
May Gotama, Vasiṣṭha,
and Viśvāmitra grant protection to the giver who has brought to us the first portion of the oblation.
— whether it be a vessel of food or of clarified butter; or whatever wealth has come to those two who carry it— read *prattam*?— [that too].
May Agni, the Hotṛ, make that a well-offered oblation:
the clarified butter which he accepted, and the rice grains which he ate together with the goat and the moon.
May Bṛhaspati, the distributor of our oblation, and the goat, the horse, and the barren cow, not harm us; may Agni,
the wise one, accept this from us.
May Bṛhaspati return, knowing the way;
may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, make this well-offered; may it be free from consumption and free from disease for you.
Whatever imperishable wealth they gave us— a boar, or a bed together with a pillow—
whatever [gift] along with a herd, together with virile power, [is ours].
May Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, make that a well-offered oblation:
whatever they have given us— this house providing all enjoyments, or a dwelling together with the yoke-halter and the sorcery.
Or rather, O Hara, bring it with an upper garment;
may Agni, the Hotṛ, make that a well-offered oblation.
As for what I have heard regarding "splendor in the sun"—PS_5,28.9 (28) ... I have heard this.

The Maruts bestowed splendor upon the sacrifice;
Vāyu released the cattle together with Bhaga;
[this occurred] in the waters of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.
In me (…) [as in 1d] // In the sacrifice is splendor, and in the sacrificer is splendor;
and whatever splendor there is in a king consecrated with water.
In the south is splendor;
that which is upon the chariot and upon the chariot-yoke is splendor.
Splendor is in the quiver and splendor is in the armor;
splendor is in the horses, which is upon [the chariot].
Splendor in the assembly, splendor in the council, splendor in the brides, and splendor in the bridegrooms—
splendor that is also in the surā.
(…) Splendor is in the lion, and splendor in the tiger;
splendor is in the wolf and splendor in the honey-stealer.
Whatever splendor belonged to the falcon among those that fly,
[that splendor] is golden-hued and likewise elephantine-hued.
They say that the splendor of those who have given birth to battle lies in the battle; in agriculture, the seers won over the people in the field.
The gods who uphold the kingdom have performed that for me:
in me be splendor, in me renown, in me glory, in me brilliance.
May those who attack me fall beneath my feet; may I be the highest. May the plants be full of sap.
May my speech be full of milk;
thus, I bring forth milk by the thousands from those things that are full of milk.
I know how he who is the god named Saṃbhṛtya made much grain out of water.
We worship him in the house of every non-sacrificer,
just as [we worship] Heaven and Earth.
They stood for the sake of support.
Thus do I bestow abundance upon the enemies and upon the wicked.
Just as a well with a hundred streams or a thousand streams is inexhaustible,
even so may my grain be.
The inexhaustible one with a thousand streams—
O hundred-handed one, gather it; O thousand-handed one, scatter it!
Just as here there is the expansion of what has been done and of the task to be performed;
these are the five directions.
The five human tribes—
may they all be auspicious and bringers of joy,
like rivers after the rain have released their flow.
— bringing abundance here;
here is the abundance of herbs and the assembly of the gods.
Right here let the two Aśvins be;
let the Dvāparāśva mount [the chariot]. Three measures belong to the Gandharvas.
There are four wives of the householder;
with that which among them is the most prosperous and excellent, we touch you.
With the hands of Jyeṣṭha Āṅgirasa, we take hold of you,
so that there may be abundant grain.
Free from disease, with many men.
(PS 5.30.9) [Anuvāka 6]
The first one has come forward, about to be milked, she who bears all sacrifices and belongs to all the gods;
the lowing cow lets loose her calf.
She has released it with a gracious mind; she makes it sound "hiṃ.
Bind the calf, place him near the cow that is eating; sit down, O milk-maid, and milk her.
May Iḍā, swelling for him with milk-rice, with sweet drink, ghee, and exhilarating food-portion—
may she, together with her calf, run to the realm of King Yama.
Given here on the first path of the well-performed,
given by the one who is not thirsty, she has come here first;
unite the cow of all forms with her calf.
In the beginning this came; in the beginning she gave it. In whatever world he gives it to you immediately, as the first milch-cow you shall carry him across.
Given with faith in the highest heaven;
know this, O cow, in the refined state: he who gives you, the first of his own possessions, [becomes] the lord of cattle.
For those who have performed good deeds there go first;
then this one comes after them, beyond old age, having passed over the cow and the ox.
One age has passed away;
the bull has bellowed toward his father among the calves.

O luminous one, go well-performed; in the sun may pleasant masters be for you, O cow.
May seven suns warm you; run toward Yama, do not go too far away.
Read *parācaiḥ* with K? (cf. PS 5.37.5c). PS 5.31.7:
"Yielding for me in the hereafter, enjoying both worlds, stride out!"
Clothed in nourishment and vigor, we receive the stream of Bhaga for our protection, the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*).
She possesses a thousand limbs and a hundred lights.
The fulfiller of the sacrifice, immortal, leading to heaven—
may that sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), multiform, come to us; we receive her back without causing harm.
Those snares of yours, O Varuṇa, seventy-seven in number, which stand divided threefold and gleaming—
let them all bind him who speaks untruth.
They release him who speaks the truth.
Here his spies move about; with their thousand eyes, they survey the earth.
Whoever violates his vow, no matter who he may be, is not released from the noose of Varuṇa;
and this earth here is likewise his counterpart.
And this vast heaven with its distant limits, and the ocean within the belly of Varuṇa—
yet even in that small amount of water he is not released.
He who stands with his mind, he who deceives, he who moves in concealment,
and he who moves in open view— if two sit together and speak, [they may both be like him].
King Varuṇa knows that as the third;
King Varuṇa beholds all that which is between the two worlds and that which is beyond.
The twinklings of his eyes are counted by men; like a gambler with the dice, he measures out the worlds.
You alone, O King Varuṇa, [are the ruler].
You are the upholder of the gods, possessing all forms.
May he be skinless, base, and tawny— whosoever destroys true speech with falsehood.
That Varuṇa who is within the home,
he who is abroad, he who is in the vicinity, he who is in a distant land; that Varuṇa who is divine and he who is human.
But I release them all here;
O Varuṇa, bind him with a hundred nooses— he who speaks untruth before you, O watcher of men— so that he may not be released by you.
"Let the rogue remain, having let his belly hang down like a sheath being cut away;
moreover, he causes [the enemy] to fall away from you."
From thee indeed he binds us;
from thee indeed King Varuṇa goes forth, having made [the world] his own.
Varuṇa cuts him down,
as one cuts a reed for a mat;
he cuts off his very root.
Whoever seeks to measure him—
[he is the one] who bound this girdle upon me as a god, who fastened it together, and who yoked me [to it].
By the command of whichever god I move, may he desire the further shore; may he indeed release me.
You are invoked; you are invoked over.
Thou art the weapon of the seers;
partaking of the first portion of the vow,
O girdle, be a slayer of my enemies.
I am a celibate student of Death, who,
extracting from living beings the man destined for Yama,
[binds] him with sacred knowledge, austerity, and exertion.
—With this girdle I bind him.
May this vajra satisfy him with his vow;
may it strike down his kingdom while he yet lives.
May he split the aggregates and crush the hair-tufts;
hidden by the earth, may he not escape, [overcome] by that which is above and below through that which is above and below.
Strike down those who lie prostrate with the thunderbolt!
Seek out him who conquers; strike down him who conquers him.
O Vajra-arrow, from the Conqueror, cause [the enemy] to fall following the parting of the hair.
Whatever I eat, may it produce strength.
"Take up the thunderbolt!"—
thus [he spoke], felling the aggregates of that person, just as the Lord of Might (Indra) struck down Vṛtra.
What I drink, I drink up; like the ocean, I drink it all up—
drinking up the vital breaths of that person.
I drink it up, I drink;
what I swallow, I swallow down completely,
like the ocean that swallows all.
Swallowing his vital breaths, I swallow his speech;
she is the daughter of Faith, born from austerity.
She became the sister of the seers, the makers of beings.
O girdle, bestow upon us thought and wisdom; furthermore, grant us ascetic heat and sensory power.
You whom the ancient seers, the creators of beings, encompassed—
do you now embrace me.
O girdle, grant me long life!
May your mother-in-law speak auspiciously for you, and may your father-in-law speak even more auspiciously.
O gods, let this incantation of yours, which causes burning pain and creates enmity,
be brought forth; make it roar and cause it to tremble!
Utter an unpleasant word;
seek to seize the head with your two hands;
let your hair be scorched.
Those hairs of yours, those two side-locks, that crest, that headband,
and also those locks which are yours.
All those [sorceries] shall cause you grief;
I drive away your terror from your clothing and I render you mad.
Moreover, whatever garment is yours, all that shall be your funeral shroud;
eat the *arka* plant and fly away from here!
I make you the eye of the sages;
furthermore, for the sake of the dogs that seek wealth,
make yourself a target for them.
Arise, O enemy, flee away;
become the footprint of the rays of light.
And then, perform what must be done.
I have drawn forth hope from between the testicles.
"Hoot at him and shake him; blow upon him like the wind upon a tuft of cotton."
Biting with your teeth at the bones of the chest and the arms,
sing toward Murava’s son Śābaleya.
Praise the well-pulling horse of Śauṇeya;
urge on the dappled steed of Kālmāṣeya from afar.
May the gods bring together for you that chariot which has the tail of a deer, the tail of a dog, the speed of the wind, and the swiftness of thought.
Therefore, you wander about, desiring a husband. To Agni they bowed down; to him, the Earth, they bowed down, just as they had bowed down to Agni and the Earth.
So may all my obeisances be directed toward them;
[may they grant me] gain, prosperity, nourishment, cattle, sacred knowledge, and the spiritual luster of Brahmins.
You are the submissive ones; be submissive to me, svāhā!
To Vāyu they were submissive; they were submissive with the intermediate space.
Just as they were submissive to Vāyu with the intermediate space, so [be submissive].
(…) they bowed down together to Sūrya; they bowed down together to him by day,
just as they had bowed down together to Sūrya by day.
(…) they bowed down to the moon; they bowed down together with the constellations,
just as [they] bowed down to the moon together with the constellations.

(…) they bowed down to the ocean; with the rivers they bowed down to it,
just as [they] bowed down to the ocean with the rivers.

(…) they bowed down to Indra; by his heroic power they bowed down to him,
just as they had bowed down to Indra by his heroic power.
(…) they bowed down to the gods; they bowed down with immortality to them,
just as they had bowed down to the gods with immortality.
(…) They concurred with Prajāpati; they concurred with him through his offspring. Just as they concurred with Prajāpati through his offspring...
In this way, let all my inclinations be directed toward me:
toward wealth, prosperity, nourishment, cattle, sacred knowledge, and the spiritual luster of the Brahmins.
You are the submissive ones; be submissive to me, svāhā!
There are seven submissive ones, and the eighth is the Dhītisādhanī.
Make the paths easy for those who desire;
may there be mutual recognition among you in the contest for wealth.
The snares belonging to Varuṇa and those belonging to Nirṛti, the snares of the forest trees and of the plants, and those which have arisen from the earth upon the earth— [all these I loosen].
May they not harm you; may there be auspiciousness for you.
Those snares in the intermediate space and in heaven, and those that are spread out in food and bind in many ways—[may they release you].
Those who have arisen from the animals—may they not harm you; may there be auspiciousness for you.
That which humans curse as "human"—Bhaṭṭa [notes].

Whether you have stepped into the waters or into the sacrificial food, whether you have touched the fire or the kindled flame—

Whether they prepare the well-fashioned arrow with its shaft, or whether they seize the hand of the Brahmin.

that with which they press the stalks of Soma,

That offspring of yours which was concealed and perished—may it be restored.

may a heroic son be born to her,

with that oblation I offer for her,

may the Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, grant their approval.

Exalted by our state of silence, we have come to the winds;
you [abide] within our bodies.
O mortals, look upon him!

dwells in both oceans simultaneously—
the eastern and the western.

May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman lead us safely across our enemies.
