O Agni, sprinkle me with splendor in the assembly;
sprinkle me with the prosperity of the gods;
[sprinkle me] with Sūryā...
May Savitṛ unite me with splendor, may Agni and Sūrya sprinkle me with nourishment;
may Candra [unite me] with... // PS_6,19.6
O Agni, may cattle unite me with splendor;
may sacrifice unite me with nourishment; may the sacrificial fee unite me with... // PS_6,19.7
May wealth pour upon me; may power pour upon me;
may splendor pour upon me.
May splendors pour upon me;
may prosperities pour upon me;
may truth pour upon us.
With progeny and with wealth,
may she make me long-lived.
O Night, [come] from the earthly realm.
The father has been satisfied through his domains;
the vast [light] spreads to the seats of heaven, and the shimmering darkness rolls away.
O wide and dark one, may you be safe for us— you whose further shore is not seen, nor is it perceived even by one who hastens; in whom all that moves comes to rest.
May we reach the further shore of the night; may we reach the further shore, O auspicious one!
O Night, you who have the eyes of a man...
There are ninety-nine seers;
there are eighty-eight,
and indeed they are seventy-seven.
Sixty and six, O Revatī;
fifty and five, O Sumnayī;
forty and four.
And thirty-three, O swift one;
and twenty-two— these are the nights, eleven of which are the shortest.
With those protections of yours, O Daughter of Heaven, guard us this day;
protect us so that no malevolent speaker may have power over us.
May the evil-minded one have no power over us;
may neither the thief of our cattle nor the wolf of our sheep have power over us today.
O auspicious one, let there be no thief of horses nor sorceress of men on these highest paths.
Let the thief run, let the robber run; let the rope with its teeth pass by, and let the malicious one flee away.
Make the blind snake, standing in the smoke-filled night, headless;
crush the jaws of the wolf.
—Strike the thief down upon the wooden post.
O Night, we dwell with you; we shall sleep; keep watch for us.
Grant protection to our cattle, to our horses, and to our men;
and also to those whom we cherish.
And whatever is within the enclosure,
that we entrust to you.
O Night, our mother, deliver us to the Dawn.
May Uṣas entrust us to the day, and may the day entrust us to you, O radiant one—
whatever here is flying about.
Whatever here is crawling,
and whatever is footed or seated—
from that, O Night, protect us.
Protect us from behind, protect us from the front,
and from above as well as from below;
guard us, O radiant one!
We here are your praisers—
those who observe the night and those who remain awake among living beings.
Those who protect all cattle, may they be watchful over our own selves; may they be watchful over our cattle.
O Night, I truly know your name;
you are indeed named Ghṛtācī. As such, Bharadvāja knows you.
As such, watch over our wealth.
The *brahman* is its head; the *bṛhat* is its back; the *vāmadevya* is the belly of this rice-mess.
The Vedic hymns are his wings, truth is his mouth;
the sacrifice, spread out, was born from austerity.
Boneless, pure, and purified by the wind.
The pure go to the pure worlds;
for those who cook the spreading rice-offering,
the fire does not burn their penis.
The fire does not burn their penis;
in the heavenly world, there is much company of women for them.
Yama does not steal away their semen.
He sits; he approaches the gods;
he rejoices with the Gandharvas over the Soma-offerings—those who cook the far-spreading rice-porridge.
No misfortune from any quarter shall attend them.
Having become a charioteer, he travels in a chariot;
having even become a bird, he goes to heaven.
This sacrifice, most extensive and wide-spread, being prepared, has sat upon heaven;
he bestows four jars in four ways.
May these streams, filled with milk, water, and curds, flow toward you from every side,
swelling with the *svadhā* offering in the heavenly world.
May these channels— pools of ghee, lined with honey, filled with Soma-water, milk, and curds—
approach you from every side forever.
Rejoicing with the ancestral offering (*svadhā*) in the heavenly world,
the white lotus, the water-lily, the lotus-fiber, the lotus-root, the *śaphaka*, and the *mulālī* spread forth.
May the well-anointed lotus-pools, swelling with the *svadhā* offering in the heavenly world, attend upon me.
This rice-mess which I cook with faith—
May that heaven, which is expansive and has conquered the worlds,
never fail me as it is being enjoyed; may it be for me a cow of plenty, yielding all forms.
The bull who, together with Sūnṛtā,
yields immortality in the heavenly world—
those who are my sons and those who are my fathers.
May they all sit down around you,
O wide-striding one— those who have fashioned these sacrifices, for whom these worlds are anointed with their own inherent power.
Those who are my grandsons and those who are my grandfathers— from them,
O Dispenser, milk forth the immortal nectars. Whether on earth or in the intermediate space.
If you have gone to heaven or to the gods— if my great-grandsons and my great-grandfathers are there—
may they recognize you here as you spread out.
In the heavenly world, the Apsarases lie beside them as wives—
those who cook the spreading rice-offering.
In this world, she who is adorned with sacrificial gifts—
drive her out, drive her away from her own dwelling-place.
We cause her downfall; may that man fall away from his houses. We make her husband turn away.
Lead the woman downward; pass beyond these ten mountains,
beyond these ten navigable rivers.
Downward,
downward, and likewise toward the unpropitious direction—
there we bring about her downfall.
Therefore we burn her away;
drive her out from the opening, from the hole, and send her to the forest.
From forest to forest, drive the people away; let them flee after the wild beasts;
make them like a crest of wind.
We place her heart upon the tip of the wind, her mind upon the storm; we bring about her total disorientation.
Let everything that is intent on destruction and self-restraint float away between both heaven and earth.
Just as a tuft of grass is carried away by the wind above, so may the wind blow unceasingly upon her.
May the sun burn him;
moreover, whatever food he eats,
let that be most poisonous for him.
"May there be a lion for your eye"—this is one verse.
"This Agni is between you two; may he drive them apart in all directions."
So that they may not prevail over you both, even in the life hereafter— O Śimidāvatī, cause them to fall away!
Strike them down, O Śimidāvatī! Tear these two, husband and wife,
apart like cooked meat with a knife.
May she take pleasure in this husband; may she find delight in this bed of her own;
let her cast off her own garment.
Like a snake casting off its worn-out skin;
as both the dead and the living are but dwellers in this world.
Thus may this couple be dwellers together in this world.
Suparṇa found you;
the boar dug you up with its snout.
O herb that destroys the malicious, burn against the one who seeks to harm and the performer of sorcery; burn the sorcerers!
Burn the one who performs witchcraft;
moreover, O herb, slay him who seeks to harm us.
O Agni, victor in battle, overcome the hostile armies!
We turn back the sorcery upon the sorcerer by means of this counter-sorcery.
May the straightest arrow fly from heaven and earth;
may it pierce him like a deer.
May the magic spell be turned upon the one who performed the magic;
may evil befall the evildoer, and curses upon the one who utters curses.
We send it back against him who did it; let it reach him who performed it. "One verse beginning with *yas tvā kṛtyā*."
Again, seize the sorcery by the hand, O sorcerer, and lead it away to another;
we place it before this man.
As one destroys a spell that has been cast, so may you strike down [the enemy]. Go like a son to his father;
like a dog, attack and bite him ten times.
Go forth, weaving like a thread,
having performed the ritual act against the performer of the ritual act;
rise up like a doe toward the water!
Like a doe springing upon a predator,
let the *kṛtyā* seize its maker;
like the hunter’s snare for a deer.
Having measured around the skins,
fasten the spell upon the necks of the one who has committed malice against us.
Whatever [curse] you are that has been made by the gods or whatever is born of men,
that very thing we send back against you.
By means of the backward-turning sacred formulation (brahman),
whether it be a woman or a man who has performed a malevolent spell (kṛtyā) for evil—
We shall lead her to him, as one leads a horse with a halter;
Heaven and Earth have spoken my word.
May the goddess Sarasvatī be propitious;
may Indra and Agni both be propitious to me;
may they crush this worm.
O Indra, O Lord of Wealth, destroy the worm of this youth;
all enemies are slain.
By this word of mine:
"He who creeps around the eyes, he who creeps around the nostrils."
We crush that worm which goes into the middle of what has been given;
there are two deformed ones and two of like form.
Two black ones, two red ones,
Babhru and Babhrukarna—
those vultures and cranes have been slain.
Those worms that have white collars, those that are black with white forelegs,
and whatever others there are of variegated forms—
We crush those worms:
the two-headed, four-eyed worm, the speckled and the white.
I crush his ribs and split his head;
yonder sun has risen.
The all-seeing destroyer of the unseen, striking down both the seen and the unseen,
he crushes all worms.
The *yevāṣas*, the *kṣakaṣās*, the *dhrukṣṇas*, and the *śipavitnavas*—
let the worm be seen and destroyed.
And let the unseen one be struck down as well:
Yevāṣa is slain, Śipavi is slain, and Gaṅgaṇivān is also slain.
All enemies are struck down by my fierce word,
as are all worms.
And of all worms,
I split the head with a stone;
I burn their mouths with fire.
O divine Agni, with your fierce flames and your bright radiance, drive away those who eat the raw.
O Agni, with your glow and your flame, burn away those who intend us evil, making them another's mouth.
Let us two establish friendship; may you and I both be free from disease and attain well-being. We drive the disease away.
Drive away from our houses the flesh-eaters;
O divine Agni, let those who are called grain-eaters not deceive you.
Those who created offspring as their share— both the raw-flesh eaters, the meat-eaters, and the grain-eaters, together with both kinds.
We drive them away from here—
those who took pleasure in raw things and did not dare to consume cooked food.
Let all those who are malevolent toward us here, who are sinners and doers of evil, go away together elsewhere.
May those gods worthy of sacrifice, by whom they were brought here, lead them back again from where they have committed their sin.
Wash away the dust, wash away the dirt, wipe off the grime from our hands;
may Dhātṛ lead us with auspiciousness.
May he protect our progeny.
I make heaven and earth my armor;
may we be under the impulse of Savitṛ.
May our mother Earth and the blessed Heaven protect us from distress on the day of the Asuras.
Do not approach us as sinners;
may these divine waters purify me with the milk of the gods.
O Father of the Maruts, I come to your favor;
do not deprive us of the sight of the sun.
May the Hero be gracious toward our horses.
May we procreate, O Rudra, with offspring— [we who pray:
"He who kills the unborn, he who [kills] within the womb, he who kills the man already born and him yet to be born."
Therefore, may I succeed today with this oblation;
may he grant us offspring that reach old age.
The two arms of Indra are firm and virile.
These two bulls, variegated and capable of carrying across, I shall yoke first when the time for action has come—
the two by whom the light of the Asuras was won.
Swift, sharpening his weapons like a terrifying bull, the striker, the agitator of the people,
the roaring one, the unblinking, the sole hero.
May Indra, together with his hundred armies, be victorious— [he who is] the roaring, the unblinking, the ever-conquering, the invincible,
the unshakable, and the bold.
Conquer with that Indra,
overcome it, O men of battle, with the Bull who holds arrows in his hand.
He is the controller, accompanied by those who hold arrows in their hands and those who carry quivers.
Indra, the striker in battle with his host,
the conqueror of those who have joined together, the drinker of Soma, strong of arm, with bow raised, is the archer who shoots with well-aimed arrows.
Prapāṭhaka 7.4.4:
He who is known for his strength, the steadfast, the pre-eminent hero, the victorious, the prize-winner, the subduer, the fierce one.
O Indra, supreme hero, subduer of enemies, conqueror by might, mount your victorious chariot that wins cattle!
Rejoice in this fierce hero!
O warriors, rally after Indra—
the conqueror of hosts, the winner of cattle, the thunderbolt-armed,
who triumphs in the race and crushes the enemy with his might.
Piercing through the clans with might,
Indra is fierce, possessing a hundredfold wrath; he is difficult to overthrow, the conqueror of armies, and invincible.
May our army prevail in the battles;
O Bṛhaspati, fly around with your chariot, slaying the Rākṣasas and driving away our enemies.
Shattering the enemies and crushing the adversaries,
be the protector of our bodies;
O Indra, Bṛhaspati is the leader of these.
May the sacrificial fee and Soma go before the sacrifice;
may the Maruts march in the midst of the divine armies as they shatter and conquer.
The fierce host of Indra the bull, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts—
of those high-minded ones who cause the worlds to tremble.
The shout of the victorious gods has arisen:
"May Indra be ours when the banners meet; may our arrows be the ones that conquer!"
May our heroes be superior;
may the gods protect us in our invocations.
From Vaiśvānara it shone forth.
A golden jewel was born;
Bṛhaspati and Kaśyapa brought it forth for the sake of heroic power.
Bṛhaspati made him into this amulet, the Vaiśvānara, for the sake of power;
the Seven Seers [made it] for the sake of strength.
The Viśve Devas and the Saptarṣis have bestowed upon you vital strength. They have all united your power.
The golden jewel was born from Agni Vaiśvānara;
the Aśvattha tree was born first.
The most beloved body of Agni,
Vaiśvānara; by the power of this creation,
the amulet has been made a destroyer of witchcraft.
I have found you as a destroyer of witchcraft; I carry you as a destroyer of witchcraft; I make you a destroyer of witchcraft.
The winged bird, powerful, the defiler of witchcraft,
the slayer of rivals, the bestower of vigor.
The *nitatni* amulet, the universal healer, the fierce protector—
may your winged one [grant] strength.
The golden amulet, born for your healing,
may it drive away the malevolent spirits.
The divine jewel is the slayer of rivals, the destroyer of demons, the dispeller of disease;
it has a golden womb and is radiant with light.
Kaśyapa brought forth the conquering power; they say that Vaiśvānara is the sole sharpening point,
born from the womb of Agni together with the Moon.
Increasing the cattle-pasture, furthering us, bestowing vigor, the destroyer of magic spells, the slayer of secret charms, he is formidable—
he upon whose [power] this [world] rests upon the earth.
A footprint has been left in the dust;
as you wipe away the bodily affliction,
bathe yourself in that very body.
O you who are to be corrupted, we bring you to death at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, for the sake of our own life.
For my safety and well-being—
this amulet is the cutter, the severer, and the burner of those who hate us.
Śatruñjaya, the slayer of rivals, shall drive away the one who hates us. (PS 7.5.12,
Anuvāka 1)
The pillar of truth has supported the earth;
by the cosmic order, the gods found immortality.
With this firm oblation, I sustain you.
May Heaven and Earth approve of that,
by means of those oblations through which Viśvakarman has supported this earth, our mother.
With these oblations I sustain you here;
may the oblations follow after the cosmic order and truth.
Stay here upon the supporting ground of the earth.
In the lap of the longing, fortunate Mother, rejoicing with great splendor,
may you be well-progenitive in this dwelling place for all future generations.
Possessing noble offspring, rejoicing in greatness,
take your place upon the height of the earth;
may the gods grant protection to this dwelling.
May the earth nourish her with streams;
may we, with our heroes unharmed, enter this dwelling, the most excellent of riches.
May they be firm for her;
may the heroes, the attendants, be steadfast.
May Savitṛ, Vāyu, and Indra [protect] this hall.
May Bṛhaspati, knowing [the way], establish it;
may the Maruts sprinkle it with water and with ghee; may King Bhaga bestow the cultivation upon us.
O wife of Māna, enjoy the oblation— this sharp-edged offering with its abundant middle portion; let the infant cry out to you, let the youth cry out to you.
Let the cows, always accompanied by their calves, low toward you.
May your pillars be firm upon the earth; O Goddess Śālā, may your wings be firm.
O firm hero, be without enemies; grant protection to us, to our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
The divine hall has been fashioned for the household fire.
Clad in grass, most gracious to the world, you whose limbs are firm and whose people are firm— O mistress of the dwelling,
may we, as heroes, approach you who are steadfast.
O Lord of the Dwelling, acknowledge us; be one who grants easy access and freedom from disease to us.
Whatever we entreat of you, graciously accept that from us.
May the four-footed and the two-footed enter here.
Darbha was born at the head of the plants, possessing a hundred stalks.
May he, possessing a thousandfold vigor,
protect us on every side, just as Darbha grass when it grows.
He pierces the skin of the earth;
even so let that person be pierced who seeks to do evil against us.
We drive away misfortune, we drive away witchcraft, we drive away the Rakṣas and the Sadānvās; we cause diseases to perish.
And all the Yātudhānīs [are here].
Indeed, there is a hollow and a height; not everything is submerged.
You are the destroyer of him who seeks to do us harm;
[ward it off] in the evening and ward it off in the morning.
Around midday,
may Darbha, who destroys with his golden hand,
protect us from every side.
Born on the mountain, you have ascended with the brown Soma;
do not leave behind those who commit evil deeds.
May the simple man not come to harm.
The root of heaven is stretched out;
it is woven across and established upon the earth.
May the darbha grass of a thousand powers protect us on every side;
it has a thousand stalks and is mighty.
With sharp shoots and invincible,
we burn away all demons and diseases with the darbha grass.
Burnt away is the evil dream; burnt away are the enemies,
and all the sorceresses.
Let not the sorcerers harm you,
nor the red bird as it flies;
Darbha is the king of the ocean.
May he protect us on every side from him who, with evil speech, utters a curse or speaks ill of us.
May that which curses us from afar, even before reaching us,
go away from us in every direction— whatever an enemy or a rival may curse us with.
Whether it be my mother-in-law or my father-in-law who curses us—
we ward off those curses of our superiors with barley.
Those oaths which they swear, whether verbal, patient, or seasonal—
bearing barley in your two arms, [you fulfill them].
O East, crush them down!
Yava with straight hair, tawny,
the bountiful one, who is to be rejoiced in by us.
May Hiraṇyadhanvan enter into the curses!
Having drunk you, Indra Śakra Vāsava slew Vṛtra.
Like a bull, overcome the curses, O barley;
let the curses go far away from here, separated from us.
May all tongues be rendered tasteless;
[may they be stilled] by the seizing of names, by the wrath of speech, and by the gaze of the one with the terrible eye.
We make your dwelling a shield for you.
Let the curses go away, cast by the evil-minded person.
May he who seeks to harm us protect me from the curse, while we ourselves live blameless by our own nature.
From falsehood and from misfortune,
and from the censure of one superior to me— may Yava protect me; may I not come to harm.
I fasten upon you this broad armor, free from stinginess and invulnerable to curses, as a barley-grain.
May the curses return again to the one who uttered them, just as winged birds enter their nests.
Direct us; do not stand in our way, O Arāti;
do not obstruct our sacrificial gift as we beg for it. May Savitṛ, the giver, bestow it upon us.
Homage to Vīrtsā and to Asamṛddhi; we offer this to them:
the man whom you, O Arāti, set before you as one who is full of lamentation.
Homage to him we pay; do not frustrate my desire for gain, which we employ this very day.
O Arāti, do not, with your mind or your heart, obstruct him who wishes to give to us, O you who revile others!
May our god-ordained prosperity succeed by day and by night; may we never follow after hostility.
Homage be to Arāti!
And you, becoming naked,
accompany the person in their sleep.
O Arāti, you seek to destroy the mind and the intention of the man;
go away, O unsuccessful one!
We lead away your weapon; pursue him whom we hate.
Having become a maiden, adorned with a garland and gold ornaments, appear for all to see.
Homage be to you, O unprospering one;
do not place me in front.
I know you as one who closes her eyes.
O Arāti, do not thrust away from mortals those who revile us; do not strike down our gain, nor our speech. Do not obstruct us.
May the formidable Indra and Agni grant us wealth; today, all of you, desiring to give,
take pleasure in repelling the stingy one.
Going forth, we invoke Savitṛ, Anumati, and Bhaga;
may I speak words that are pleasing and honey-sweet.
Among the gods' invocations to the gods,
I entreat that which is [granted] by Nakulī,
whose tongue has her lips as a covering.
May faith find him today,
bestowed by the tawny Soma;
may the protecting god come.
Kuṣṭha, from the Himalayas,
destroying every fever and all sorceresses.
O Kuṣṭha, you have three names: Naghamāra, Naghāriṣa, and Naghāyuṣa; may this man not come to harm.
To whomsoever I address you, evening and morning as well as by day—
Jīvalā is the name of your mother.
"Your father is indeed named Jīvanta,
and your sister is named Māriṣā. (…) // PS_7,10.3
You are the best among herbs,
as the ox is among moving creatures,
and as the tiger is among beasts of prey.
This man shall not come to harm,
for whom I proclaim you at evening, at dawn, and likewise by day.
Thrice from the waters, thrice from the mountains, thrice from the Ādityas,
and thrice born from the Viśvedevas.
That Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma,
destroying every kind of fever.
And all the Yātudhānīs;
the Aśvattha tree is the abode of the gods in the third heaven from here.
There, from the sight of the nectar, Kuṣṭha was born;
A golden ship with golden moorings moved in the sky,
where there is no falling of ships.
Where the head of the Himavat is, there is the manifestation of immortality;
from that, Kuṣṭha was born.
That Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma,
destroying every fever.
And all the *yātudhānī*s—
O Kuṣṭha, whom the ancient king of the Ikṣvākus knew, or whom the king of the Kaśis knew.
Since you belong to Śāva and to Mātsya, you are the universal healer of the headache that recurs every third day.
O you who possess all-pervading power, drive away the fever that lasts six months and that which lasts a year,
casting it downward.
Section 2.
The mountains whose backs are the Soma,
the waters flowing on their surface,
the wind, Parjanya, and Agni— these are the protectors.
They quelled the flesh-eater who strikes down that which moves and that which is stationary,
and the crawling creature as it rises up.
If the Apsarases kill the ten-month-old embryo, we cause that very one to perish from here.
The Gandharvas, the householders,
and the flesh-eaters who play with dice in folly—
these we cause to perish from here.
He who mounts upon your thighs for the sake of licking your blood— the raw-eaters, the flesh-eaters, the enemies— [may they be destroyed].
We cause those to perish from here.
That which makes your hips tremble and lies between the husband and wife— [we cause that to perish].
We cause him who lurks within the womb to perish from here. You who [afflict] you with sleep and darkness...
Having deluded him, he lies in wait;
he who seeks to devour your offspring—[him...
But he who, having become a lover corresponding to your husband, lies with you—
[drive away] that Arāya, Kaṇva, the evil one.
We cause him to perish from here:
Hā! Hai! O dwarf, O bald one, O Naigūrakarṇa, O pot-bellied one!
Indra’s sharp weapon—
with that we cause you to perish.
Homage to Taṇḍa, homage to Kusuma!
Homage to her who protects, homage to her who is established in her own nature!
Homage to you, O Nirṛti, possessor of all boons; O you of every form, cause this person to suckle [you].
As far as heaven, as far as earth, as far as the sun revolves— so far, O fierce Gulgulu, do you [prevail].
Protect this [earth] on every side—
she who has one king, one vow, one station, and one lord.
We invoke Pāṭā, the dispeller of rivals, for victory—
she who is sovereign and observes a single vow.
O you who are united and have a single lord,
no rival wife— neither one of the same lineage nor one from outside— has ever overcome you.
I am superior to those who are superior; may I rise above those who are inferior. May my rival wife be cast down below.
Lower than the lowest;
the sun does not wither the skin of the sindhu-flower.
O Pāṭā, from you who are not withered, I take splendor from my rival wife. Truly, O Pāṭā, you are not a mere Pāṭā.
You are the maker of good fortune;
bestow upon us the fortune of the vulva,
and furthermore, make me a queen.
That which, upon the leaf or upon the tree, you, O great one, fly like the wind—
victorious and firmly established.
Or you are named Saṃjayā;
[I praise] the one with upturned leaves, the fortunate,
the overcoming, the powerful.
Speak clearly, speak the great word, the *pāṭā* that drives away rivals;
Indra has consumed the *pāṭā*.
As Indra slew the Asuras with it,
so may I overcome my rival wife,
just as Mahendra overcame the Dānavas.
The pāṭā plant bears a golden hook with a handle;
by means of it, [take] the splendor from my co-wife.
"I destroy that which is not mine.
I dig up this herb,
the most powerful of all plants.
By means of which she overcomes her co-wife and makes the husband hers alone—
those of whom we proclaim the sound from afar.
Like the wind blowing in different directions,
Indra cut off the heads of those who possessed dogs.
Those that move in front together with the rays of the sun, (...
those that follow after the wind; (PS 7.13.2)
In the intermediate space, below heaven...
Those whose swing, bound in heaven, is golden in the intermediate space...
Those who dance along golden couches in the intermediate space,
those that fly with the wind as their chariot.
Lying on their backs, striking with their feet (…) those that crawl around the tree,
with sidelong glances, making a cracking sound (…) // PS_7,13.6–7 //
Those *vikumbā* women who dwell in the villages and gather at the crossroads,
and those who [gather] at the sand-pits...

Of those many hundreds who go about, desiring person after person,

Indra too has made his head.
Agni is long-lived; he is long-lived along with the lords of the forest.
May that venerable one make the venerable one long-lived! May Vāyu, the venerable one, [make him] long-lived through the intermediate space! [...]
The sun is long-lived; it is long-lived by day. (…) The moon is long-lived.
The Venerable One is long-lived by means of the constellations;
Soma is long-lived,
he is long-lived by means of the herbs.
The sacrifice is long-lived; it is long-lived through its sacrificial gifts. (…) The ocean is long-lived.
May he, the venerable one, [be] with the rivers; may that venerable one make the venerable one long-lived.
O Brahmā, [make him] long-lived!
May that [be] for the students of sacred knowledge, O long-lived one!
May that make you, O long-lived one, long-lived!
Indra is long-lived.
May he, through his vigor, become long-lived;
may he make the venerable one long-lived.
O gods, you who are long-lived!
They are long-lived through the nectar of immortality;
may they, being long-lived, make [me] long-lived.
Prajāpati is long-lived.
May he, long-lived through his offspring,
make me long-lived.
May the sacrificial fee protect me from the right.
May the sacrificial fee protect me from the left;
may it protect me from behind against being pierced;
may it protect me from every malevolent intent.
O Paśupati, having given me a two-footed animal and a four-footed one, grant me a living sacrificial fee.
Having given life, cause [others] to live.
Whatever sacrificial fee you give with faith for the sake of a Brahmin, [that shall be yours].
May she deliver you from consumption, from the heat of Agni, and from divine anguish.
You have given this sacrificial fee; may it not cause you harm.
We root out those wasting diseases from you; having struck down the ear-ache and hostilities,
may all wasting diseases depart together.
Through food one wins vital breath;
through clothing one wards off disease;
by giving gold, a horse, and a cow.
He makes the sacrificial fee his armor;
he makes the turban for the pain of the head,
and the garment for the disease of the body.
May the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), given from the ear, protect the bright, shining semen from blindness and deafness.
May the amulets protect you from neck diseases, from consumption, and from the flesh-eating tooth;
may the ointment protect you from disease of the limbs.
"Food [protects] you from disease.
From beneath the feet, from the foot-disease, the two shoes [protect].
May the staff, given by you, protect you from the serpent from the south, being offered with the right hand.
[May it grant] good-mindedness, the sacrificial fee, and skill.
Clothed in nourishment, strength, and the sacrificial fee,
we approach the stream of Bhaga for protection.
She possesses a thousand limbs and a hundred lights.
The fulfiller of the sacrifice, immortal, leading to heaven—
may the multiform Dakṣiṇā come to us;
we receive her back without causing her harm.

May the waters rich in herbs protect me from this direction.

may it protect me, may it guard me;
to it I entrust myself. Svāhā!

may they encounter Vāyu, the possessor of the intermediate space.

those who would harm me from the southern direction.

let them encounter Sūrya accompanied by Heaven and Earth.
May those who seek to harm us from the western direction encounter water rich in herbs;
may those who seek to harm us from this direction encounter water rich in herbs.
May those who are malevolent toward me from the northern direction encounter Viśvakarman accompanied by the seven seers;
may they encounter Indra accompanied by the Maruts.
May those who seek to harm us from this direction encounter Prajāpati,

Carry the clarified butter to the gods;

let them all come to my invocation.
O Indra, come to my invocation;

These are the *atisarā* offerings for Indra.
May my intentions be brought into harmony;
through them, O Jātavedas, master of your own body, may we be able to perform heroic deeds.
Whatever that godless one intends to accomplish against us from there, O gods—
may Agni not carry his oblation!
O gods, protect me; come to my very invocation.
O you who run beyond and overtake others, run past [my enemies].
Mistresses of all through their vigor,

Those things which you have done and those which you will do— O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra,

Just as one strikes down that person,

I deliver you, who are under the feet of Indra, unto death;

I make him lower than this for all future years;

Drive away the *rakṣas* demons;
drive away those who revile us—

Subdue those who worship foolish gods—
those who say that a family is ruined by fruit that is parched, bitter, and hidden.
To her, the golden-haired Arāti,
we pay homage—
she who is great and of vast measure.

we pay homage to that Hiraṇyakeśī, the female spirit of ill-will.

the egg-eater, the defiler of the fetus, the *arāya* who has reached the son— [may he be destroyed].

All your auspicious names— by means of them, protect us from distress.
[The hymn] that slays the Rakṣas, that slays Vṛtra...
The *pīlu* tree, which crushes the piśācas and was born at the beginning of all trees—
that I bind upon you for the sake of long life.

for you indeed, O Varuṇa, self-dependent one, O leader of the host, know all generations.
What is beyond this world-space?

There is but one [world] beyond this world-space.
One thing is easy to perceive, while another is difficult to see;
that I declare to you, O Varuṇa, as one who knows: let the Paṇis remain with their faces cast downward.

Equal is our kinship, O Varuṇa; equal is our birth.
Truly I know that which is our common birth;
I give to you what remains as yet ungiven.
The god, the bestower of strength to the praising god,

Moreover, you are the lord of immortality; moreover, you are the nourishment of food and the protection for men.

you stand as the protection for the swift horses.
Protect me; protect our beloved; protect whatever wealth we have;

Neither a curse, nor a magical rite, nor a burning grief shall reach him.
The *viṣkandha* does not seize him who wears you, O ointment,

[and] the highest of mountains.

That which has been and that which is to be:
just as the four-eyed dog [is the best] among dogs,

manifest your forms;

look back upon those who come toward you—

May the waters fashion all that [fault] away,
like a carpenter removing a splinter from a wagon-pole;
may heart unite with heart.
With the *opaśa* [let] the *opaśa* be united;
with water, release the *apasmita*;
may the *pārṣṇidyota* come together with me.
The divine waters, flowing from the mountains for the sake of the gods— those which have reached this person today.
That man shall not come to harm.
May the waters from the Himalayas be auspicious for you, and may those from the springs be auspicious for you.
May the flowing waters be auspicious for you,
and may the waters of the rain be auspicious for you; may the waters of the desert be auspicious for you.
May the waters of the marshes be auspicious for you;
may the waters from dug-out wells be auspicious for you, and those brought in jars be auspicious.
The cloudless ones, digging in the deep, are the wise ones, the skillful workers;
they are more skilled healers than the physicians.
We speak clearly to the waters:
to the divine waters and to the waters flowing in streams.
At the washing away of the waters, you become swift horses;
those are auspicious waters.
The waters are the makers of healing;
just as there is refreshment for one who is thirsty, so may they be your medicine for the removal of disease.
The heroic powers were gathered with Brahmā as the eldest; at the beginning, Brahmā stretched out the highest heaven.
Furthermore, Brahmā was born first among all beings.
Who, therefore, is worthy to rival the Brahman? This Brahman is these two, heaven and earth;
this Brahman is these seven rivers.
Brahman is all these Ādityas;
the gods worship Brahman;
the Brāhmaṇa speaks of Brahman.
The night of Brahmā enters;
the Brahman born of Savitṛ shines forth through the Brahman, and Agni blazes with the Brahman.
The sacred herbs abide in Brahman;
the rains rain down as Brahman; this entire world is Brahman, endowed with the Self.
As far as the sun shines:
the Brahman is the Hotṛ, the Brahman is the sacrifice;
by the Brahman the sacrificial posts were measured.
The Adhvaryu priest, born from the Brahman,
offers the oblation through the Brahman;
the Brahman is the ladles filled with clarified butter.
The sacrificial altar was raised by Brahmā; the Brahman is the thread of the sacrifice,
as are the officiating priests who prepare the oblations.
Brahman is the bull, possessing auspicious seed; the cows are the Brahman, the preparers of the oblation;
the Brahman belongs to the divine chariot.
That which moves,
self-fashioned, the chariot is drawn by the Brahman; by the Brahman it is yoked.
A person born of Brahman, moving as a biped,
is not shaken;
the sages are born of Brahman.
The kṣatriyas are born from Brahman; this world is Brahman, born from Brahman;
from Brahman comes the food for consumption.
The Brahman is the Śūdra of the Rājanyas; the Brahman is their distributor of food. The Brahman is their auspicious dwelling place.
Brahman is their assembly;
Brahman are their attendants, Brahman are their servants, and these gamblers are also Brahman.
Woman and man were born from Brahman; woman is Brahman, and indeed so is man.
Brahman is the high ground, the low ground, and the surrounding enclosure.
The trees are the mountains; the plants are the sacred formulation (*brahman*). This *brahman* has extended across all this—between both heaven and earth.
O Jātavedas, may the supreme Brahman become [his protection];
may the thunderbolt of Indra strike down the great Yātudhāna; and may Bhava and Śarva hurl their scorching weapon at him.
May these two, impelled by me, release [the poison] for his destruction—
whatever has been poured into the plants by the Ashvins, who wear lotus-garlands.
The plants bear honey;
with that, I sprinkle the head of this noble woman.
O Aśvins, that honey which is collected from the flower by the bees,
and that honey which is in salted food— [may it be mine].
Therefore (... [as in PS 8.10.2]:
"O Aśvins, that honey which has been gathered from the *gulgunī* plant and from ointment..."
That sweetness which is in this honey-giver...
(see PS_8,10.3) that sweetness which is in the axle of the Aśvins.
Whatever sweetness is in the cows and in the horses, whatever sweetness is in the flowing surā-liquor and in the thickened extract;
By that [... (see PS_8,10.4):
O Aśvins, [bestow] that which has the luster of cattle, the luster of gold, and the luster of elephants, O Aśvins.
With that, I sprinkle the head of this noble woman,
for her delight and her joy.
I bestow pride upon you;
may the two Aśvins, garlanded with lotuses, bring fortune to you.
O fortunate one, let splendor be in your teeth;
let honey-sweetness be on your tongue; let there be collyrium for your eyes.
The most honey-sweet token!
Come to us like two palms,
like a tree without a rival for its lord.
You have seized the men, as a hawk seizes other winged birds; for I have drawn forth your water.
The waters are for consecration;
that splendor of yours which has departed from the face, from the act of looking— [may it return].
May the two Aśvins, adorned with lotus garlands, bestow that splendor upon you once again; I have sprinkled you with luster.
Together with divine milk,
may you be most honey-sweet for your brothers-in-law, like a woman who has a husband.
May Bhaga be yours, O Mitra and Varuṇa;
may Bhaga be yours, O Goddess Sarasvatī; may Bhaga be yours, O both Aśvins.
—may the two lotus-garlanded ones bestow [it].
May King Varuṇa be your husband;
may the divine Bṛhaspati be your husband.
May Indra and Agni, and may Dhātṛ, bestow a husband upon you. (PS 8.10.12,
Anuvāka 2)
You indeed have four corners, and I am the middle of the sieve;
I shall praise your four streams.
The altar that increases mankind—
seize it, full of vigor; purify yourselves, full of prosperity.
Indra is the one who brings the seed; may Bhaga come as the leader before us,
for the two oxen belong to Bhaga.
Yoke your two draft-animals,
O Aśvins; then bring here the liquid of the earth.
Surrounded and clothed in grain, the all-pervading Lord, the master,
was born as the sustainer of mankind.
The chaff was the clarified butter of the gods; the winnowing baskets were the offering-spoons,
and the winnowing-fans were the enclosing-sticks.
The plowmen were the Hotṛ-priests;
the sower of seed was the lord of the oblation.
O Indra, loosen your fists here.
May the Saumanasa spirits here be fulfilled;
and may those Gandharvas who consume oblations bring abundance here.
O far-seeing one, O gatherer, O seeker, bring us what is ripened; the Gandharvas are the lords of the world.
May all bring prosperity to this threshing floor,
and may they bring here abundance and truth—
from behind and from before.
From above and from below,
O Indra, lord of wealth,
bring hither abundance to this threshing floor.
May Indra bestow abundance here upon the threshing floor; may Prāṇa fill it full; may all the gods grant me abundance.
May Soma and Bhaga grant me prosperity;
may there be prosperity in my hands, and prosperity wherever I take hold.
O you who are a hundred cubits long, fill this up from the midst of the ocean;
bring more of it here for me.
Just as I desire,
so may this swell up like water,
like three elephants together.
O sweet one, may Mitra and Varuṇa [accept] you; O goddess Sarasvatī, [accept] you, the sweet one;
O Aśvins, [accept] you, the sweet one, as the Soma.
Let them, wearing lotus garlands, fashion it—
those whom all the gods, the Marut hosts, and the sons of Sudhanvan poured out.
May that *surā* which the Aśvins poured out flow forth abundantly;
may it become sweeter than the sweet.
Be sweeter than honey;
as this female deer is to the male, so may you be, O fortunate one.
Born from the cloud, born from the rain,
and also born from the sky;
and also born from the ocean.
Therefore, become a churner of Sura;
you are by name Nāḍī,
so become a churner of Sura.
For that auspicious friend of yours was the *vikaṅkata* tree, sweet of fruit;
but the Asura was Aurdhvanabhasa.
The first among the gods acted thus;
however, in the house of the servant Sure,
they made his head blind.
From the Kaśīkā bird I have extracted the flower,
and from the flowing stream the Sura; come forth, O thou who art rich in steeds!
What do you desire among the Aṅgiras?
These kinsmen of yours sit here—
profound and bold.
O sure goddess, go forth,
gladdening every person,
you whose vessel they take up with a platter.
Cows, horses, grain, and wealth—
let that Sura flow forth abundantly,
coming down from the mountains.
Dug out by those who are cloudless,
whose resting place is in the ocean and whose dwelling is nowhere.
May they grant you a bubble;
O Udaṅka, drink this liquor which we desire with our heart.
May Bhaga grant that to me; may the Aśvins grant that to me; may Sarasvatī grant that to me.
This god Mayūlaśa—
Bestowing the delight of the gods,
he has been brought hither from the streams, the springs, and the mountains.
In the midst of the hundred, let the *maṣṭiṣka* urinate like a bull;
from the ocean, the honeyed wave has risen up.
In a whisper he attained immortality;
that which is the secret name of ghee is the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality.
Let us indeed proclaim our names; let us uphold this sacrifice with oblations of clarified butter and with reverent salutations.
May the Brahman priest hear the hymn being recited.
The four-horned bull has bellowed this:
he has four horns, three feet,
two heads, and seven hands.
Bound in three ways, the bull bellows loudly;
the great god has entered into mortals. Placed in three ways, it is hidden by the Paṇis.
The gods found the clarified butter in the cow;
Indra produced one part, Sūrya produced one, and from Vena they fashioned one by their own inherent power.
These flow from the ocean of the heart, moving in a hundred channels, unseen by the enemy; I behold the streams of clarified butter.
The golden reed is in their midst;
the streams flow together like rivers,
purified within by the heart and the mind.
These waves of clarified butter flow forth like deer fleeing from a swift hunter,
as rapid as those on the course of a river.
The mighty winds blow forth;
the streams of clarified butter fall like a ruddy steed, bursting through the barriers and swelling with waves.
Like beautiful women smiling as they go to a gathering, the streams of clarified butter have approached Agni as kindling-sticks.
Jātavedas, being pleased, desires them.
Like maidens going to the wedding procession, I gaze upon the ointments as they are being applied.
Where Soma is pressed, where the sacrifice is performed— there the streams of clarified butter flow toward it.
Flow toward our excellent praise, toward the prize of cattle.
Bestow upon us auspicious riches;
lead this sacrifice of ours to the gods.
The streams of clarified butter flow, sweet with honey.
Upon your abode the entire world is supported; within the ocean, within the heart, and within life.
He who was brought forth from the assembly of the waters’ front.
May we attain that honeyed wave of yours.
Two of different forms move toward their own goal; one after the other, they suckle the calf.
The self-powerful Hari is in one [form],
while the bright and radiant Śukra is seen in another;
the ten [fingers] brought forth this embryo of Tvaṣṭṛ.
The tireless maidens lead him around— the one who is carried hither and thither, whose face is sharp, who is self-glorious among men, and who shines resplendent.
Three he knows; they adorn him:
one in the ocean, one in heaven, and one in the waters, according to the eastern quarter of the earthly realms.
Directing the seasons, he has established them in due order.
Who among you has perceived this hidden one?
The calf has brought forth his mothers by means of their inherent powers.
The embryo of many, the great seer, moves forth from the lap of the active waters, self-sustained;
beautiful and worthy of being sought, he grows within them.
Standing upright in the lap of those who are bent and supine,
both [worlds] were afraid of Tvaṣṭṛ as he was being born;
turning toward him, they wait upon the lion with delight.
Both auspicious ones delight him like two women;
like lowing cows they have approached him in their own ways. He has become the lord of the skillful, the master of skill.
Him whom they anoint from the right with oblations—
he, the terrible one, reaching forward, stretches out both his side-ropes like Savitṛ stretching out his arms.
He produces for himself a bright garment; he leaves behind his old raiment for his mothers.
He assumes a brilliant form that is most excellent.
Mingling with the seat of cows and waters,
the sage, as inspired thought, polishes its foundation; it has become the assembly at the gathering of the gods.
Your wide expanse encompasses the foundation,
the radiant abode of the Mighty One;
O Agni, kindled with all your own inherent splendors.
Protect us with unfailing guardians!
He makes the desert a stream, a path, and a wave; with his bright waves he reaches the earth.
He holds all ancient things within his bellies;
he moves within the new-born plants.
Thus, O Agni, increasing by our fuel—
O purifier, shine forth with glorious renown!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
He who is a descendant of Jamadagni here, the Kauśika, he who is the Ātreya or the Kāśyapa;
those who are Bharadvājas, the Gautamas, and the Vasiṣṭhas— [all these are present].
To them we shall proclaim our transgressions here:
the Agastyas, the Kaṇvas, the Kutsas, the Prasravaṇas, the Virūpas, the Gargas, the Mudgalas, the Yaskas, and the Śūnakas.
We shall here proclaim our offenses against those Brahmins who are well-disposed and have not wronged us—
against that one who would not rise when a Brahmin is in need.
Whether through arrogance born of sloth or through pride in his fortitude,
may all the gods be his witnesses; let them collect the poison and the guilt within him.
Whatever offenses against a Brāhmaṇa he plants, and whatever sins and manifold misdeeds he commits—
performing them, he deposits that which is called "self" within himself.
Thus the gods cause him to enter that state:
he should not eat, nor drink, nor lie down, nor kiss his wife, nor even [kiss] his son.
When the sin against Brahman has been proclaimed, one should indeed stand firm; that is the path of Truth. The great seers who are the authors of the Śatarcins and those of the middle [Maṇḍalas]—
Whatever [faults] belong to the authors of the minor hymns, or those among their offspring here, and whatever births of the seers we know—
of these we declare our transgressions here.
Of the fifteen hundred brothers,
thirty-three gods remained; when one was pierced, all were rendered formless.
They found that guilt in the Brāhmaṇa:
he would be treacherous toward him who does not bring this [gift], who does not rise for it, or who does not speak of it in this [assembly].
"O Brahmins, arise and speak together concerning this Brahmin who is afflicted by sin and desires kinship among the Brahmins."
We beg for what has been won; may it all come back again!
O Indra and Agni, O All-Gods, may you cause that which was won by me to return once more.
He makes his life long and provides for his progeny—
he who is a true Brahmin to a Brahmin.
When summoned, he follows after his transgression.
Neither Śarva slays his progeny,
nor does Rudra slay them, nor does the thunderbolt.
The draught of Soma delights that brahmin who, being a true brahmin, speaks the truth even regarding sin.
The observer of men, together with the pressing-stones—
he who has torn away the darkness from the heart of the Brahmin, as the sun [dispels it].
He who, having risen, pours out sin upon the food of a Brāhmaṇa—
may both Heaven and Earth burn him up.
Now, come [back] to the path of one who has not departed.

And those ninety-nine swellings that have spread along the flanks—
may they all perish from here!
I have understood these seventy-seven subtle channels that have ascended along the flanks.
May all those fifty-five [obstacles] vanish from here, driven away by me, the Knower of the Truth.
May all those who have mounted upon the Vakṣaṇā follow after; driven away by me, the knower of the *puttha*, may they all perish from here.
From your thighs, from your knees,
from your heels, and from your buttocks—
like a lover of a woman.
We crush the Putrajñī;
we crush the Anusṛptā, the Dhrukṣṇā, the Pāpī, and the Śimidvatī, who dwells in the thickets.
Burn up this female slave of the Dasyus, O Cukākaṇi,
she who is the abode of sons for women.
She approaches the fishermen;
burn up that female slave of the Dasyus, O Cukākaṇi!
Fly forth, O well-winged one, like Kuṣītaka from a good reed-thicket;
I shall swiftly burn you with my jaws.
You shall perish, O Putthagi,
when its furrow is scorched and when its head is consumed by fire.
Then this daughter of the Dasyus shall be destroyed in her own dwelling;
she has remained there for a year.
The *prataṅkinī* [is for] the Asuras;
where there is a foul odor of the field, that is this *nyañcana* for you.
This is not for your mother to stand upon, nor is this a place of concealment for you;
this belongs to our heroes.
The gods performed the procreation;
on the mountain Himavat, they produced for you a son of stone and water.
There, having plunged in, dance among the herds of goats like a bull; may you [be endowed] with cattle and horses.
Prosper further with offspring;
may he whom you sent there live happily where those who live dwell.
Mitra has stepped forth from the earth;
I lead you toward that stronghold.
Enter it, enter into it!
May she grant you both protection and armor.

Prajāpati ascended with his subjects;
I lead you forward to that stronghold.
Enter it, enter it fully!
May she grant you both protection and armor.
O gods, that which you have uttered while uniting and drawing [the bowstrings] together— may that be yours.
O Indra, fulfill this true blessing for them;
may the oxen be truthful in their speech.
May he make my speech effective;
wherever Parjanya rains for your benefit, let that be for your welfare.
May the divine waters, the Śakvarīs, flow for you into the deep;
may they be full of vigor, rich in clarity, and abounding in milk.
Be visible; do not remain hidden.
Arise, O you who possess abundance, full-vessel, and radiant!
Milking [the earth] and protected by Pūṣan, fulfill their desire;
may this furrow be fruitful.
May she grow with a hundred shoots; may she have a thousand enjoyments.
May Indra protect her.
May the Aśvins prepare the ploughshare;
may Bṛhaspati protect it,
so that there may be abundant grain.
Free from disease and with many men—
O gods, that which you have sprinkled around here, so that there may be more.
Here we invoke that goddess Utpr̥ṇā, [saying]:
"May she bestow this upon me."
"May he bestow abundance upon me," means "may he increase my heap.
The maker of abundance is the maker of much.
This one with full, blooming lips is imperishable; he is the chaff, the eldest, the all-pervading, and the sovereign lord. In him, grain is sown.
Barley, rice, and likewise sesame—
having examined what has been done, take four hundred of that.
Like a field of sugar-cane, like the cry of peacocks—
O Bhaṭṭa, like a wheel-turner— and furthermore, whatever is in the bull, that indeed approaches as expansion.
Everything indeed exceeds [it].
It is said by Bhaṭṭa:
"O Great Ointment, destroy the enemy; crush those who possess a thousandfold nourishment."
O herb, become abundant for us,
like the flowing stream of the ocean.
From clarified butter, the goat was produced.
These porridges came from the regions;
Bṛhaspati saw them,
and he indeed became the Five-Porridge.
O Bṛhaspati, you have prepared these fourfold rice-offerings; you were born from the clarified butter.
He became their fifth.
By means of smoke he reaches the sky, and by means of heat, the intermediate space.
The unborn one attains the quarters with his eye; the five-fold rice-offering is the libation.
She who is your mother, he who is your father—
And those who are your own brothers—
having cooked the five-fold rice-offering for the Unborn (Aja), all of you subsist upon it.
To those who have departed before and those other ancestors who came after—
let a stream of clarified butter flow for them.
Flowing with a hundred streams,
she pours forth for those who always give and those who cook the rice-meat.
They indeed dwell in the world beyond the kingdom of Yama;
one does not reach it by means of the Atirātra sacrifice.
Neither the Ukthya sacrifice nor the Agniṣṭoma attains him; neither does the five-rice-oblation Sava attain the Unborn.
It is commensurate with the ten-night rite;
it is calculated as the twelve-day rite; it is commensurate with the long sacrificial session.
The *pañcaudana* sacrifice is the *sava*.
Of those [five], everything that is lost and everything that dies belongs to the *barhiṣya*.
And that which the thief steals away, and those whose sacrifice consists of the five-fold rice-offering; she who,
having found a former husband—
Then, when he finds another, a different one,
they two cook the fivefold rice-mess for the goat and do not part from it.
He becomes one who shares the same world as his future rebirth, another lord; [he attains] the unborn, the fivefold oblation.
Bestowing the light of the south,
may Sūrya sprinkle me with splendor;
may both Aśvins sprinkle me.
May the Sun, rising upwards, anoint me with splendor;
may Agni, the father, [anoint] me with splendor.
May Bṛhaspati [endow] me with splendor;
may [he endow] me with the splendor of the thickened residue of the surā being poured out.
May both the Aśvins, adorned with lotus garlands, sprinkle me with that;
may my face be radiant.
Shining and invincible,
I make him golden-hued, beloved by all who behold him.
I am sweeter than honey,
the source of honey, more full of sweetness;
may splendor enter into me.
Like a bull bellowing for his mate,
I have applied this collyrium which bestows splendor, while it itself roars aloud.
Just as one who is bellowing should move with splendor and fortune,
so do they bestow splendor upon Agni.
The sun rises with splendor;
as much splendor as belongs to a cow or gold, so much splendor may there be for me.
O Lord Sun, as far as you look upon with your vision when rising,
so far do you look upon me with your splendor.
Having become full from the womb, I have mounted the chariot of splendor;
may it carry me forever.
— [I address] the Venerable Suvarcas:
"I am encompassed by fortune,
by splendor, and by wealth."
Just as the sun, ever-shining, moves through its courses,
so may fortune come to me.
Thus may splendor come to me; thus may radiance come to me;
thus may glory come to me.
The house of Bhaga is covered with a golden wheel;
that I uncover with a sacred prayer.
It was given to me by the Aśvins;
it was given to me by Puṣkarasraj. (PS 8.20.11, Anuvāka 4)
Kāṇḍa 9:
His fuel-sticks rise upward;
the bright flames of Agni rise upward.
The most radiant one, the son of Supratīka,
Tanūnapāt, the Asura, the all-knowing,
the god among gods.
He anoints the path with honey and ghee;
being gratified, Narāśaṃsa, the god who performs good deeds, approaches the sacrifice with honey.
Savitṛ, the possessor of all boons,
approaches this [place] with power and ghee;
I praise Agni, the bearer, with reverence.
May he worship the greatness of this Agni at the sacrifices when the ladles are extended;
may he [worship] when the delightful offerings are presented.
And [he is] the most wise among the Vasus and the best bestower of wealth.
The divine doors, all the ordinances of Agni, grant food.
Widely-expansive, ruling by their own power,
those celestial bulls now [dwell] in his womb;
Dawn and Night [protect] this sacrifice.
Protect our sacrifice!
O divine Hotṛs, with the tongue of Agni, graciously accept this sacrifice of ours.
Make our sacrifice well-offered!
May the three goddesses— Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī— sit upon this sacred grass.
May the Goddess of Speech, being praised,
grant us that wonderful seed, rich in food, and may Tvaṣṭṛ bestow upon us heroic vigor and the increase of wealth.
Untie the knot for us.
O Lord of the Forest, being gracious, release [the offering] yourself to the gods.
May Agni, the preparer, prepare the oblation.
O Agni Jātavedas, utter *svāhā* for Indra’s portion.
May all the gods enjoy this oblation!
May Agni, the wise one, join you here with the sacrificial formulas as fuel at the sacrifice— svāhā!
May the god Savitṛ, knowing all, yoke the well-yoked [steeds] for this sacrifice; Svāhā!
Indra [accepts] the hymns and the songs of praise at this sacrifice.
May the wise one yoke the well-yoked [steeds], Svāhā! May the Maruts, through the meters, carry the sacrifice here like a mother her son, being well-yoked, Svāhā!
The *praiṣas*, the *nivid*s, the *āprī*s, and the remaining *yajus* verses are harnessed here by the wives;
come, O Agni, with the sacrificial grass and the sprinkling waters.
Aditi, performing the sacrifice— svāhā!
May Viṣṇu yoke his many heats in this sacrifice, well-yoked— svāhā!
May Tvaṣṭṛ now yoke many forms in this sacrifice;
may Indra yoke many heroic powers.

O Aśvins, come hither with the sacred word (*brahman*), increasing the sacrifice with the *vaṣaṭ*-call; *svāhā*!
O Bṛhaspati, come hither with the sacred word.
This is the sacrifice; bestow this light upon the sacrificer, svāhā!
May the waters purify, may Varuṇa purify, and may he who purifies at all times purify this [person].
Sacrifice is Bhaga, the advocate, and the distributor;
may both Agni and Sūrya purify us.
The ten-headed one, the ten-tongued.
The heroic physician has taken hold;
may your digger not be harmed, nor he for whom we dig you up.
The ten nights indeed know the remedy for leprosy through this plant;
dig that up from here with a spade.
I destroy your white leprosy.
One part grows in the water; the other stands upon the dry land.
He has destroyed leprosy and other [diseases]; may he sprinkle others with splendor,
with clarified butter and ghee.
I offer this remedy for vitiligo;
in the presence of the fire and the plants,
vitiligo shall no longer be found.
He becomes tawny-colored, or variegated in appearance; O leprosy,
perish from here forever!
I shall burn you with a plant,
those [seeds] which spring up separately,
appearing like stars in the sky.
Destroying every kind of leprosy,
I approach like a flood with my plant-essence,
whether impelled by men or otherwise.
The white leprosy has departed.
We pay homage; we bow down to the gods.
May the doer meet with his own retribution.
From your head, from your shoulders, from your forehead, and around your ears—
with the herb that hastens the rain.
I destroy your leprosy;
your own healthy color returns to you through this herb, which is free from malice and victorious.
From your necks, from your uṣṇihās, from your vertebrae, and from your spine...

From your two shoulders, from your two forearms,
from your two upper arms, and from around your two hands...
From your back, from your two sides, from your two hips, and from your buttocks...
(see 9cdef) PS_9,3.12.
From your two thighs,
from your two knees, from your two heels, and from your two forefeet— with the herb that hastens with the rain.
I destroy your leucoderma;
your own healthy color returns to you, O herb that is free from malice and victorious.
May your hearts be together, may your understanding be together; may Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, bring this about for you.
May the god Bṛhaspati be with you;
may your heart be one, and likewise may your mind be one.
Agni, the god, is common to you; together with him, enter the kingdom. Be of one mind and of one heart.
May you all be of one mind;
your anger is destroyed and your envy has withered away.
Live together with auspiciousness.
Just as a son speaks pleasant words to his parents,
so do you speak to one another.
Speak kindly with your tongue;
may your grains be together and your cattle be common to you all.
May the plants on the earth be with you, may the herbs be with you; may the consecration and the sacrifice be with you.
May your marriage be with one who is powerful;
may they dance together with vigor,
and may the women sit together with you.
Together with your heroic powers,
together with others, subdue [them]; together with the winged arrow.
Do not hurl a weapon at anyone else.
I unite this assembly with honey; I have anointed my speech.
Let others hear you when you speak in the assembly;
let friends choose you.
Even all people seek kinship with you; like mortals [seeking] immortality, they long for you. (PS 9.4.9)
May your minds be gathered together as one, like herds of cattle brought together by their gatherer. May your intention be common.
They have followed after the supreme knowledge.
That which is their heart,
let that abide in their hearts.
Moreover, that which is their heart is situated within your hearts; may your mind be one and the same.
He has followed after their supreme consciousness—
this which is their mind and those which are their minds.
O Indra, place those together like two feet set upon a chariot;
for the Puruṣa has a thousand arms.
He, the thousand-eyed, the thousand-footed,
having encompassed the earth on all sides,
stands beyond it by the measure of ten fingers.
With three steps he ascended to heaven; one step of his was here again.
Thus he strode out in all directions.
In eating and in not eating;
such are his glories, and the Puruṣa is even greater than that.
One foot of him is all beings; three feet of him are the immortal in heaven.
Puruṣa alone is all this.
Whatever has been and whatever is to be,
and even that which is the Lord of immortality, he became one with it through food.
When they fashioned Puruṣa, into how many parts did they divide him? What was his mouth, and what were his arms?
Why are the thighs called "feet"? [The verse says:
"The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth; the Rājanya became his arms."
The Vaiśya was his middle, and from his feet the Śūdra was born. In the beginning, the Virāj came into being.
From Virāj was born Puruṣa;
once born, he extended beyond the earth behind as well as before.
When the gods performed the sacrifice with man as the oblation,
spring was its clarified butter.
The summer was the fuel, the autumn the oblation;
they sprinkled that sacrifice with the rainy season—
the Puruṣa born in the beginning.
By that, the gods, the Sādhyas, and the Vasus performed sacrifice;
from it, horses were born.
And whatever animals have two rows of teeth were born from that; from that were born goats and sheep.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered,
the Ṛg-verses and the Sāman-chants were born; from it, indeed, the meters were born.
From that, the *yajus* was born.
From that sacrifice, in which everything was offered, the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) was gathered.
He made those animals— both wild and domestic— the victims for Vāyu;
there were seven enclosing-sticks for his mouth.
When the gods, performing the sacrifice, bound Puruṣa as the victim, thrice seven fuel-sticks were prepared.
From the head of the great god,
seventy-seven rays were born from King Soma.
From the Puruṣa who was born,
the moon was born from his mind;
the sun was born from his eye.
From the ear arose wind and breath;
from the mouth, fire was born. From the navel came the intermediate space.
From his head the sky evolved;
from his feet the earth and the quarters from his ears; thus they fashioned the worlds.

I dig up this herb, the unseen slayer;
it bestows the life of a horse upon you.
O Vairūpa, O possessor of steeds!
Your tongues are not seen, nor are there teeth upon your jaws.
Neither your middle nor your head shall remain;
you who were enemies of Indra have been slain by Indra.
There is no stumbling here;
may Indra, the powerful slayer of Vṛtra, trample all of you together.
The mules with iron hooves upon which Indra stands— by means of them I shall bind you fast.
The faces of those who slither through the belly are unseen,
like the mouth and feet of a leather bag.
Or has his tongue been torn out,
or are his teeth knocked out from between his jaws? I have struck down the blood-drinker.
I licked them from my lap;
I broke the eggs of all those kings who were unseen.
The *riśya* grasses, the *pauruṣa* grasses, the *darbha* grasses, and the *vairiṇa* grasses;
the unseen *mauñja* grasses and the *sairya* grasses.
Drive them all away together!
Seven births of the unseen have been crushed;
the great earth has not trembled.
Indra Śakra drove them all away with his two arms—
those of you who were born as seven.
Those who devour men, unseen— like the stalks of Soma by a pressing-stone—
we crush them all.
Those that are born from the self, those born from the bladder, those that are wrathful, and those that are piercing—
to them I dig up this herb.
From whom the killing of Bimbī was committed—
from those unseen ones, from the young, the middle-aged, and the old.
I have brought the potent herb for which the execution of Bimbī was carried out—
for those who have been seen and those who have not been seen.
The *titīlas* and those *śalunas*—
O Agni, burn them all up;
strike down these motionless worms.
"Let the cool waters [be]—let the cool winds blow upon us! Agni is covered with frost; Agni is surrounded by frost. (PS 9.7.1)
When the gods obstructed you, you caused the ocean to flow; the cold has slain the one born of the cow.
The axle is snow, the covering is snow.
From the snow we set forth; today, in the snow, is our release.
The pit that you dug for Saptavadhri, which had a hundred openings— you have filled it; let the *avakā* plant grow there.
Thine own is the cavity within thee;
O Agni, thy first radiance is the glowing coals, and thy latter is the flame.
With the sacred word (*brahman*), I seize your name, limb by limb, joint by joint; *Śītikā* is the name of your mother.
Jalāṣa is the name of your father;
remain here within this space,
and let whatever blemish there was belong to the Bāhīka.
Born from the snow, brought here from the Sindhu river when its waters had risen,
with that [name] I have grasped yours.
Like a horse by its halter,
O herb, "Āmā" is your name; I have grasped that name of yours.
O sons of Agastya,
do not consume my men.
O Agni, [do not consume] our bodies.
Do not damage our garments,
O you who are born from the ocean, whom we have mounted for our well-being.
From heaven the stars fell down;
from the stream came the waters of the ocean;
[there was] the golden jar, the green one.
Surrounded by Vakās,
we thereby pacify the fire;
I pacify the flame of Agni.
May Śiva burn me; may he not consume me.
Heaven and Earth are seized;
the earthly realm is seized.
Whatever water is in the muñja grass, whatever is within the reeds,
that which is in the ocean and that which is in the river—
With that we pacify the fire:
with reed, with *avakā* grass, with *naḍa* reed, and with *vīraṇa* grass.
I bring forth the fire-quelling [remedy] from the rohītaka tree; O women who fetch water,
come hither!
May they carry away whatever blemish is yours;
going forth to the far distance,
may they carry away whatever blemish is yours.
O Agni, we envelop you with the afterbirth of the cold; O cool one, make it indeed cool!
He makes snow with the cold;
with the plow that has eyes,
with the footed one that flies.
O Aśvins, seizing it by the tail, they dragged it like barley with a wolf;
the gods drew this barley mixed with honey.
Upon the Sarasvatī they ploughed with the plough;
Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, was the master of the furrow; the Maruts, the bounteous givers, were the drivers.
O bounteous Aśvins, [bring] the golden jar, fashioned by the celestial bee, filled with barley.
Therefore, you two have made that honey.
O Aśvins, even when emaciated, you two conquered this honey of the bees.
Then barley sprang up;
it became a destroyer of poison,
as young as the honey-bee.
Having squeezed it out, he brought the honey.
(…) When [he saw] the wolf, the drinker of honey...
You two, O Aśvins, have caused [it] to flow away.
(…) [The lake] named Kairaṇḍā.
From the vomit of a wolf, barley grew forth;
it became a destroyer of poison.
When Bharatha cut the honey from him, even as the bees were there, you two immediately took that from the horse.
O Aśvins, restore [him] again!
He who, pierced by a poisoned arrow or bitten by a snake, approached the barley.
O Aśvins, lift up that Bharata who is sinking like a sinner in the water, whom eight teams of horses carry.
The sixfold yoke with four oxen— may that drive away your poison,
like a fierce [bull] standing in the middle.
From whatever part of your body, limb by limb, joint by joint, the *yava* spreads,
from that [place] drive away the *yakṣma*.
Fierce like one who strikes the middle,
may no other plants grow upon your fragment of grain.
May barley ward off the poison from the cow,
the horse, and the man;
barley is the king, barley is the physician.
Great is the majesty of barley;
having drunk the churned drink of barley,
Indra performed his heroic deed.
Bring the nectar, bring the flower of clarified butter; O herb, you who have been dug up without injury!
Corrupt this poison which comes from those who have been pierced by poisoned arrows—

May all those who have been seen by my eye go back again, free from disease, for the sake of life and not for death.
We seize your head;
we have found no essence of the poison, like one who has eaten the foam of water.
From the middle of the earth, from the middle of the sky,
from the edge of the earth, and also from the sky— from the midst of the earth, whatever poison [there is].
That poison we neutralize with our speech.
The poison placed in the *aśvattha* tree,
the poison placed in the skull— [we neutralize it].
From a stone was born Taimāta, the first destroyer of poison;
I am the [remover] of the poison of Vaindaka.
Of the *dārvya* poison and of the *svaitna* poison,
I have seized the common voice.
This they say, both the seekers and the Śūdras, as well as the Āryas:
of the horn that removes all afflictions.
Poison is entirely devoid of flavor;
yet harsh speech, though its ears are like nectar,
conveys poison first.
Just as one would not apply that [poison] to a non-poisonous snake,
so too, O gods, is this sapless poison for you who subsist upon it.

there, having sprinkled nectar, they rendered that poison tasteless.

The Śārī birds have flown away over the difficult places, like [other] birds.

May we, with you as our physicians, overcome old age;
the sky has stood firm, the earth has stood firm.
This entire world has stood firm;
the draft-oxen of the poison have stood still like emaciated beasts.
As long as the sun shines and as far as one can see,
by that [extent] I am [known] as Indradatta.
I render the poison sapless; that poison is sapless,
the poison in the lower part is sapless.
Mātariśvan brought it together; Dhātṛ joined the joint; Indra and Agni protected it.
Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the navel;
Bhava has mounted upon you, and Rudra brought you the stalk.
Night protected you;
thus you were born among beings.
May Heaven protect your life.
The atmosphere is your life-breath;
may Pṛthivī, the mother of what has been and what is to be, protect you.
You whom the gods joined together, being truly possessed of a thousand men—
you, O Goddess, are this [earth] here.
Drive away, drive off the poison!
Those female [creatures] that flow forth from the front, by day and by night— drive them away, drive off the poison!
The waters flow in many streams; they indeed are the destroyers of poison for you. Heat was your rain.
Agni became the shadow, austerity was the womb;
the cloud was your amnion—
thus you were born among the beings.
The Gandharvas were your root;
the Apsarases were your branches;
the Marīcis were your leaves.
Sinīvālī is your lineage;
the undecaying gods have bestowed immortality upon mortals.
I take that foremost portion from him; it is indeed your poison-destroyer,
for him who digs in a cloudless sky.
The wise man [is] in the deep water;
the physician [is] for the eye, the physician for the wound— this indeed is your poison-destroyer.
Those which stand spread out in front like cows about to depart,
or like [the rays] of this immortal one.
And then Arundhatī was his;
he who, having tasted the honey of the bee, brought forth the honey.
From that, barley was produced;
it became a destroyer of poison.
This is the [mantra] for the straw of barley.
Of wheat and sesame,
of rice and barley— with the divine [power], I render the poison sapless.

they discovered it.
The gods brought her forth from the ocean, even as she sat hidden there; having brought her up from the ocean, they raised her aloft.

you are the eye of this divine earth, belonging to the atmosphere, the destroyer of poison.
Section 2.
The gods, increasing through austerity, encompass the common goal, assuming form after form;
when they enter into the Āditya.
That one form of theirs is immortality.
May the great guest, the father, come to us with the gods through the gods.
He goes toward Jātavedas,
becoming one in form while dwelling in the secret cave;
he has indeed descended as the guest-fire (Ātithya).
In harmony with both classes of ancestors, the great mortal has indeed come to the portion of food. (See Kim 2014, 305; Bhatt. reads *martyo nāgan*.)
Having grasped the Ādityas,
the bearer has entered them;
they enter the man who lies asleep.
The vital breaths, having entered him, do not desert him; they, being well-disposed toward us, protect us by night and by day, without showing any malice.
O Lord of Cattle, be gracious to us and our cattle; drive away all [evil] from us. Do not harm our vital breaths.
Vāyu is established upon truth,
protecting the out-breath and the in-breath;
he has set these creatures in motion.
The gods, being vigilant, and the Ādityas submitted themselves to Prajāpati;
Pūṣan extended himself within the rays of light.
The Sun is Viṣṇu in his stride; he ascends to the height in heaven.
From progeny come the gods at the impulse of Savitṛ.
May Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms;
anointing the milk with honey, come unweariedly, O Aśvins!
O All-Gods, O Ādityas, come forth in unison from the front and from behind for our well-being!
May Bṛhaspati, the Brahman-armor, protect our gathering; may the god, placed at the head by the gods, guard us.
O Maruts, whose laws are true, come to us with rain for our protection;
quicken us in the afternoons.
Indra, the king, the lord of heaven, stands measuring out the day;
may he arrange these quarters for us.
From afar you have come to us; from afar you have come to us. Be right here; do not go away.
Do not follow the ancestors who have gone before;
I bind your life-force firmly.
Whatever man has practiced sorcery against you—
Therefore, whatever the reddish person is—
both the releasing and the complete releasing— I declare those to you with my speech.
Whatever offense you have committed through thoughtlessness against a woman or a man, or whatever you have reviled— through thoughtlessness.
(…) Whatever sin remains from that committed by your mother, or even from that committed by your father; (PS_9,13.3) [see 2cd]…
Unloosing and releasing— both these I declare to you with my speech:
that which belongs to your mother and that which belongs to your father.
The sister and the brother together have produced this medicine from the west;
I make you one who reaches old age.
Come, come again, come with your whole mind;
do not go to the messengers of Yama.
Ascend to the cities of the living;
summoned back,
come again as one who knows the upward path.
Ascending, advancing,
the journey of both the living and the dead:
do not fear, you shall not die.
"You shall become one who has overcome old age.
I have driven away the consumption from your limbs, the fever of your body."
The disease of the head, the disease of the limbs,
and that malady of the heart— consumption has swooped down like a hawk.
Driven far away by speech—
[the two] seers, Bodha and Pratibodha, he who is sleepless and he who is watchful.
May those various guardians of your vital breath remain awake by day and by night.
This fire has been approached for worship.
May the sun rise here for you; arise from the deep death,
even from the most difficult darkness.
Homage to Yama; homage be to Death; homage to the Fathers and to those who lead [the dead];
and to him who knows the crossing over.
I place that fire before me.
Let breath come, let mind come, let sight and likewise strength come.
May his body be restored; may it stand firm upon its two feet.

May the chariot of desire, burning [me], crush me like a blade of grass with its wind.
Just as Bṛhaspati subdued the Asuras for Indra,

Bring these here for me...

Together with the earth belonging to Iḍā,
may the gods, humans, and gandharvas subject you to me.

Thus, let him never sleep with desire for me;

The Maruts heat the *kuṣṭha* plant,

Just as no one would go toward a precipice out of their own accord,

Kāṇḍa 10:
Alas, mother! O cow with sharp horns and hanging teats!
That which you desire is not known by those who know; that which is called wealth, you do not consume it—
[this is] your son, O Pṛśnibāhu.
Make him your own through the *sāman*; likewise [make] your daughter and your granddaughter;
and so, be in harmony with him.
O Asāmī, O Kuramā, O Sī, O Naigūḥ, sister of Naigūra— O Arāti, O Nirṛti!
O you who are hostile and venomous!

Bhaṭṭa:
From that [state], however, his sons and brothers are taken away;
from that, his cattle-pen is scattered.
He who speaks of what exists as non-existent, and he who has no sacrificial vessel— go to those who have such evil names.
In that [hymn], there are all [the verses] beginning with "paretana";
one verse beginning with "pari dhāmāni"; and [the verses] beginning with "antaścarām" and "kośecarām."
And likewise those that roam the cow-pens,
and those which we see in dreams—
