The Ayovasu people distinguish [the one] who comes to us— you, O Radiant One—
and then you approach others.
Entrust us to Uṣas; O Night, grant that we all be sinless.
May Uṣas bestow upon us the day.
Salutation to you, O Radiant One!
PS_14,9.7 (9) Anuvāka 3 // (14) Kāṇḍa 15
He purifies himself from all directions; he who possesses the light of heaven comes together from there.
May Mādhava protect us from this sweetness.
Agni, the god of invincible power, is unassailable.
May this Kṣatra protect and guard us;
may the Rathantara Sāman with its various forms protect us by means of the Gāyatrī metre.
May the twelve-fold hymn-form, the ocean of speech, fulfill this day with its strength;
may the fierce one, the conqueror of the quarters, the bestower of vitality, [protect us].
Pure on the bright day, in power;
may Indra, the sovereign lord, nourish us from here, and may he maintain this sovereignty for me in every respect.
A vast kingdom, upholding sovereignty, with increased virility; the Triṣṭubh meter, with vigor, adorned with fierce heroes;
Indra, with hymns and the fifteenfold chant, with splendor.
May this be protected by Vāta together with Sagara. The eastern direction among the quarters is glorious and renowned; may all the gods, together with the rainy season, protect it as the radiant day.
May this ruling power be invincible, an unassailable force, powerful and full of might.
May I be able to accomplish that in the Vairūpa Sāman.
Upon the earth, I cause this to enter into the people;
O All-Gods, by means of the seventeenfold [stoma], may this formidable ruling power, possessed of the waters, be established today.
May the supporter of the quarters uphold this sovereign power; may the strength of those seeking the lap [of the earth] be like that of Mitra.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who are wise through the autumn days!
Grant great protection to this sovereign power!
Upon the Vairāja Sāman rests my inspired thought; through the Anuṣṭubh, valor and might have been gathered together.
This ruling power, friendly and giving with moist bounty— O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect it in your sovereign authority!
The universal monarch of the quarters is powerful and full of might.
May the winter season, through its appointed time, carry us across.
May the great Śakvarī and the Oṣajātā, dripping with clarity,
protect this sacrifice of ours.
May the divine goddess of the quarters, rich in sound, easy to milk, full of milk, and dripping with clarified butter, protect us; may you be our guardian, both from the front and from behind.
O Bṛhaspati, yoke the voice toward the south;
O Stoma of twenty-one verses, O Mistress of the World,
O Vivasvat, O Vāta, sing for us!
May there be a ghee-rich and milk-filled delight for us under the sovereignty of Savitṛ;
may the upward direction be the delight of the quarters and of the plants.
May Savitṛ with the year and with the day,
with the *revat* chant among the chants, and with the *paṅkti* meter among the meters— may he who has no enemy be gracious to us.
The support of heaven, the foundation of earth,
mistress of this moving world, the consort of Viṣṇu, all-pervading, bestowing nourishment, and the one of excellent oblation.
May she be pleasant for us in the lap of Aditi;
may she be the firm quarter of the directions, the wife of Viṣṇu, who is not terrible, the sovereign mistress, and the mental inspirer of strength.
May Bṛhaspati, Mātariśvan, and Vāyu, and the winds that bring harmony, sing our praise;
he who is our father, our progenitor, and our sustainer.
He who has brought us forth from being—
desiring wealth through his prayer—
he, the first coverer, has entered into the chosen place.
Turn toward us, O Earth,
with the sacrifice and with milk;
let Agni, impelled by the waters, descend here.
O Agni, that which is radiant, that which is purified, that which is bright, and that which is worthy of sacrifice—
all that we bring for the gods.
From here, from the womb of the sacrifice, from the abode of the buffalo, I take nourishment and vigor; may it enter into our cattle, our clans, and our progeny.
I abandon exhaustion, emaciation, and disease.
You are the prolonger of life;
you are called the wise physician.
Therefore, O collyrium, you are a bringer of peace;
you have been made a source of well-being for one who suffers from jaundice and discoloration of the skin.
May the ointment drive out from all your limbs the consumption that causes the breaking of the body and the spreading poison.
May the collyrium born from the earth, auspicious and sustaining for men, make [the eyes] free from decay.
O Prāṇa, protect the breath, the sinless impetus of the chariot; be gracious to this life-force for the sake of its vitality.
O Nirṛti, release us from the nooses of Nirṛti!
You are the embryo of the river.
Lightning is its flower;
the wind is its breath, the sun its eye, and the milk of heaven its sap.
O divine collyrium from the three-peaked mountain, protect me on every side;
no plants can overcome you.
Whether they be outsiders or mountaineers,
he has cast this [remedy] into the midst, the destroyer of demons and the dispeller of disease.
Driving away all maladies and destroying all oppressions from here,
O King Varuṇa, this [is] much indeed.
A man has spoken falsehood;
therefore, O thou of a thousand powers, release us from this distress.
Whatever we have said regarding the waters as "the inviolable ones" or "O Varuṇa," from that [arises] your thousandfold power.
Release us from distress on every side,
O Āñjana; may both Mitra and Varuṇa follow after you.
Having followed you for a long distance, let those two rise again for the sake of enjoyment;
lead them together like debt from one debt.
The sorcery of the sorcerer goes to his own house;
may it shatter even the ribs of the evil-hearted one against whom the mantra is directed.
Whatever evil dream is among us, whatever is among our cattle, and whatever is in our house—
let the one of evil heart go away raw and uncooked.
May they release [it] for the beloved one—
[the drop] grown from the strength and vigor of the waters, born from Agni Jātavedas.
The mountain collyrium with its four heroes shall make the quarters and intermediate directions auspicious for you;
this four-hero collyrium is bound for you.
May all directions be free from fear for you;
may you stand firm like Savitṛ over what is desirable;
may these subjects bring tribute to you.
Wash one jewel; make one for yourself;
bathe with one; drink from one of these—[these four] which possess four heroes, [intended] for the four Nirṛtis.
May she protect us from all bonds.
May Agni protect me for the sake of out-breath, in-breath, and long life.
For luster, for vigor, for splendor, for well-being, for prosperity, svāhā!
May Indra protect me with his Indra-power.
For out-breath and in-breath, for life, for splendor, for vigor, for brilliance, for well-being, for prosperity— svāhā!
May Soma protect me with Soma for out-breath, in-breath, and life-span;
for luster, vigor, and splendor.
For well-being and prosperity, Svāhā!
May Bhaga protect me with fortune for the sake of out-breath, in-breath, and long life.
For luster, for vigor, for splendor, for well-being, for prosperity, svāhā!
May the Maruts protect me with their hosts.
For out-breath and in-breath, for life-span, for luster, for vigor, for splendor, for well-being, for prosperity— svāhā!
Section 1.
O God Agni, bestowing long life, filling us with old age, with a face of ghee and a back of ghee,
drinking the ghee— the lovely nectar of the cow— [protect us].
Like a father leading his son to old age, lead this man to long life. O Jātavedas, bestow life upon him; O Tvaṣṭṛ, grant him offspring and protection.
O Savitṛ, impel for him an increase of wealth;
may he live a hundred autumns through you.
O Agni, bestow upon this man long life and luster.
O Varuṇa, O Mitra, O King, [grant] dear seed;
O Aditi, like a mother, grant him protection,
so that all the gods may reach old age.
May Agni grant you a longer life;
may Soma bestow upon you increased prosperity;
may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, speak in your favor.
May Aditi, together with the Ādityas, grant you protection.
May the Revatīs fashion you as a wide-eyed one; may the Kṛttikās fashion you.
The Bhaṭṭas performed their labors for you; they stretched out their prayers and, having fashioned them, they sprinkled the songs of praise with ghee.
A thousand women have been given as a boundary on all sides— eighty in the middle, providing security— the divine maidens for the sake of the god Savitṛ, as a surrounding enclosure.
Great indeed is that majesty of yours, O Maghavan.
Ascend this stone;
like a stone, may you be firm.
Crush those who desire to harm; overcome those who attack in battle—
with that [mantra] by which one [worships] the god Savitṛ.
The gods have established it all around;
with that, O Brahmaṇaspati,
bestow this [power] upon us for the sake of sovereignty.
Bestow this Indra upon long life and great sovereignty,
so that you may lead him to old age.
May he remain awake long over his dominion.
Prepare this Soma for long life and for great hearing.
So that you may lead him to old age,
let him remain long awake in his hearing.
Clothe him, clothe him with splendor!
Ward off old age and death; grant long life.
Bṛhaspati has bestowed this garment upon King Soma that he may put it on.
Go well into old age; put on your garment;
become the one who wards off the curse of the young cows;
live for a hundred autumns with radiant luster.
Clothe yourself in the increase of wealth.
Put on this garment for well-being;
you have become the protector of waters and the guardian against curses.
May you live for a hundred long autumns;
living, may you, O handsome one, distribute wealth.
In every endeavor, may you be the best at ascetic heat.
In every battle we invoke our friend Indra for his aid;
he is golden-hued, undecaying, and possessed of excellent heroes.
Enter into union with offspring, O Old Age and Death!
This Agni has said, and Soma has said this; Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, and Indra have said this.
When you weave that most excellent thread, like a garment of many forms and beautiful appearance, it becomes auspicious in aspect, ageless, and full of heroic sons.
By that may the gods prolong our life.
When Brahmins seize the hem of one's garment, loosening the lower robe, they prolong his life.
May the gods favor his invocation; may he always abide in well-being.
Put on another garment, wrap yourself in it.
I peel away this caul from you; may the seers wrap you up for old age;
may Sūrya and Bhaga extend your life.
O you whose first garment I take up, may all the gods protect you;
may your brothers, increasing you, cause you to grow.
May many be born after this well-born one.
Be unharmed by the unharmed;
be firm with the firm.
Crush those who seek to harm;
overcome those who attack us.
Mitra is the overseer of the earth.
May he protect me in this sacred knowledge,
in this rite, in this office of the domestic priest, in this invocation of the body, in this intention, and in this blessing; svāhā!
Varuṇa is the overseer of the waters.
Vāyu is the overseer of the intermediate space.
(…) // see 1bcd PS_15,7.3 Sūrya is the overseer of heaven.
The moon is the overseer of the lunar mansions.
Vasu is the overseer of the years.
(…) the year, the overseer of the seasons;
Agni is the overseer of the trees of the forest.
Indra is the overseer of ritual actions.
(…) Savitṛ is the overseer of all impellent forces.

The *hiṃkāra* is the overseer of the *sāmans*;

May they protect me in this sacred formulation,
in this rite, in this office of the domestic priest, in this invocation of the gods, in this intention, and in this prayer— svāhā!
Gods of gods, gods among gods, supreme gods above the gods, stride forth!
You who are first, [stride] into the second; you who are second, into the third. Three times eleven are all the Vaiśvānara gods.
O great ones, do not obstruct me!
May I be able to accomplish that which I am doing; svāhā!
(PS 15.9.6, Anuvāka 2)
Like a cloud, his appearance becomes formidable when the armored warrior advances into the lap of battle;
with an uninjured body, may you be victorious!
May the greatness of that armor protect you.
With the bow may we win cattle, with the bow may we win the battle, and with the bow may we conquer fierce conflicts.
May the bow turn the enemy's desire away;
with the bow may we conquer all hostile armies.
As if about to speak, it comes close to the ear.
Embracing her dear friend, she twangs like a woman; this bowstring, stretched upon the bow, cries out as it carries one across the assembly.
Moving together like a woman to her husband, like a mother to her son, may they carry us in their lap;
acting in harmony, may they pierce our enemies away.
These two pressing-stones, quivering, [strike down] the enemies.
He, the father of many, whose son is many, being a victor in the encounter, makes wide space by descending.
The quiver, bound upon his back, conquers all hosts and armies when it is discharged;
standing in the chariot, he leads the steeds before him.
Wherever the skillful charioteer desires, there he goes;
praise the greatness of the reins!
The traces follow and control the mind from behind.
Making loud noises with their hooves like bulls,
the horses, striving for booty along with the chariots, overtake the enemies with their forefeet as they spring forward.
They destroy their enemies without retreating;
the chariot-stand is his oblation,
whereon his weapon and his armor are laid.
There may we sit upon the auspicious chariot, always well-disposed;
the Fathers, who dwell in sweet assembly, are bestowers of vital strength.
They are steadfast in hardship, powerful, and profound; they possess diverse armies, have the strength of arrows, and are never exhausted.
These heroes of true being are vast and conquerors of hosts.
O Brahmanas, O Fathers, worthy of Soma; may Heaven and Earth, auspicious and faultless, be gracious to us;
may Pūṣan protect us from distress, O you who increase the cosmic Order.
May no one who intends us evil have power over us.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below, against the malevolent one.
May Indra from the front and from the middle grant wide space to us, his friends, as a friend.
He wears beautiful wings; the deer is his tooth.
Bound with cow-hides, she flies forth,
impelled; where men run together and apart, there may the arrows grant us protection.
The garment is the eagle, the ghee is in its mouth;
the mind is the golden-winged arrows. May they not strike us as they fly down from yonder.
O Savitṛ, may those sent from here be victorious! Like a serpent with its coils, he encircles the arm,
warding off the strike of the bowstring.
The hand-guard, knowing all ways,
as a man, shall protect the man from death on every side.
They strike against their shoulders.
Striking at their hindquarters,
O horse-whip, urge them on;
make the horses prevail in battles.
From heaven and from earth its vigor has been brought;
from the trees its conquering power has been gathered; the strength of the waters has been brought hither, encompassed by the products of the cow.
Worship Indra’s thunderbolt and his chariot with an oblation.
Indra’s thunderbolt is the vanguard of the Maruts; it is the offspring of Mitra and the navel of Varuṇa.
O God, graciously accepting this our offering of oblations, O Chariot, take up the offerings.
O Lord of the Forest, may you indeed possess firm limbs.
Our friend, the furtherer, the possessor of noble heroes—
O chariot, girt with ox-hides, be firm;
may your rider win all that is to be won.
Cause the earth and the sky to resound; let the world, scattered in many places, take heed of you. O drum, together with Indra and the gods, [be victorious].
Drive the enemies far, even further away!
Roar aloud; bestow strength and vigor upon us!
Shout out, driving away all misfortunes!
Drive away misfortune from here, O drum;
you are the fist of Indra—be firm! Conquer in the terrifying battle; let them conquer!
Let the drum resound with its banner;
let our horse-winged heroes fly together;
O Indra, may our chariot-warriors be victorious!
May Indra provide the forepart for the chariot upon which Maghavan has mounted to conquer;
like a vigorous herdsman, may he guard it with his cattle.
Born invincible, he was the first to desire to win;
like the thunder of Parjanya,
his roar resounds, and like that of Indra and Agni, it cleaves asunder.
A thousandfold hero, winning a hundred, winning ten thousand— O chariot, be gracious here!
[Thou hast] the wings of a hawk and the forelegs of a deer.
The fist of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts—you are bound with cow-hide; be firm.
He raises his arms again and again like one who has joined them together.
The formidable one, pressing forward, sacrifices to both banks;
by his powers he draws up his bright garment and casts out new raiments for his mothers.
Fierce are your two rims and fierce are your two fellies; fierce are the spokes of your great chariot.
Fierce are the poles here, and fierce is your bending pole-shaft.
Fire is the eye and the starting-point of the chariot;
with that, go forth crushing the unfriendly and the enemies.
The spokes, the nave, and the axle are your strength.
Fierce are your two scrotums together with their testicles;
on your penis are the straps and the terrible sheaths.
Your place is the binding, and your seat is the chariot-box.
Strength is in the cow-pen, the wild beast is one member; O people, stride forth toward the stall and press the juice for the great feast!
By him Vṛtra has been struck down.
May he be fierce through his dominion and progeny. Ascend as a conqueror with your might;
as a thousandfold hero, go forth crushing your rivals and enemies.
Perform heroic deeds upon the pair of flanks;
then place this and that chariot of his in readiness. Let the eight seers join together their eyes.
The horses, bright and running straight, follow you;
may the Supporter grant it to you like a father. Place it in your lap as you move; it shall prolong your life.
Sewn together by poets, it was fastened upon the chariot; that bow-bearer, with the bow as his mind,
brought these broad-middled [arrows] into existence after having cast them forth.
For the well-being of horses, those things created by the sages—
may the gods grant you protection through them.
We invoke Agni and the lords of the forest.
May the herbs and the plants,
Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Sūrya—
may they release us from distress.
We invoke the god Savitṛ,
the Ordainer, and Pūṣan; we invoke Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost.
We call upon King Varuṇa,
Mitra, Viṣṇu, and also Bhaga.
We declare Vivasvant to be a portion of you [...
We declare the Gandharvas and Apsarases [to be portions of you].
The Aśvins, Brahmaṇaspati, and the god named Aryaman— these are they.
We speak of the wind, of Parjanya, of the intermediate space, and likewise of the quarters; we speak of all the regions as well.
We speak thus day and night concerning both the sun and the moon.
We address all the Ādityas;
may they release us from distress.
May they release me from the curse.
May Day and Night, and likewise Dawn,
and Soma the celestial— one whom they call the Moon— release me.
We declare that there are five royal plants, of which *soma* is the best:
*bhaṅga*, *darbha*, *yava*, and *sahas*.
May they release us from distress—
those seven domestic animals,
and those wild beasts of the forest.
We speak to the śakuntas, the birds; may they release us from distress.
We speak this to Bhava and Śarva.
And he who is Ugra and Paśupati—
those arrows of theirs which we know, may they release us from distress.
We speak of the sacrifice, the sacrificer, the Ṛg-verses, the Sāman-chants, the healing remedies, the Yajus-formulas, and the priestly offices.
May they release us from distress.
We invoke the seasons, the lords of the seasons, the months, and the years.
May the years and months be equal for us;
we invoke heaven and the constellations.
The earth, the yakṣas, the mountains,
the oceans, the rivers, and the ponds— they [are yours]. (See PS 15,14.3)
We speak here of the seven seers; we speak of the divine waters, Prajāpati, and the ancestors with Yama as their chief.
We address all these gods,
who are true to their covenant and who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
Together with all their wives, you [O Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus]... // See 1d PS_15,14.5. Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus.
The gods, the divine Atharvans, the wise Aṅgirases— they are...
Those gods who dwell in heaven, those who dwell in the intermediate space,
and those powerful ones who have taken refuge upon the earth—
O gods, go forth from here toward the south,
behind the cattle, moving eastward.
From the east the Śakras,
from the north the Viśve Devās, having come together—
(they) … // see 1d PS_15,14.8.
We name the Arāyas, the Rakṣases, the serpents, and the Puṇyajanas;
we name the one hundred and one deaths.
May they release us from distress.
May the five divine quarters and the twelve divine seasons [protect us].
O Bhartṛhari, may those ten seasons which are the fangs of the year be ever auspicious to us.
We speak of the Real, the Lord of beings, he who is the lord of all beings;
we speak of all beings.
May they release us from distress.

As far as the sky, as far as the earth,
as far as the sun revolves—
so far, O fierce herb, do you [prevail].
Protect us all around, O Arundhatī!
Unharmed, he digs for you; unharmed, I dig you up.
May all our bipeds and quadrupeds be free from disease;
you are the sister of the gods.
You are the wanderer among the Maruts;
the living man whom you reach shall not come to harm.
You are named Arundhatī;
you are in the third heaven from here. Therein is the ascent to immortality.
Therefore we speak to you with this:
"May the waters be auspicious for your heart; may they also be auspicious for your vital organs."
May Vāta be auspicious, may Bṛhaspati be auspicious; may the Sun shine auspiciously upon you.
May Indra and Agni be auspicious for you.
May the night be propitious;
may the plants upon the earth be auspicious for you, and may the herbs also be favorable to you.
For among many plants, I have found you, the potent herb; O Arundhatī, I have brought you here.
"May you not cross over from here"— thus,
as if desiring him to live,
Arundhatī would have cursed the Dasyu.
This goddess is the healer of ignorance and of that which is caused by wind;
sprinkle after us, performing that [remedy].
It shall indeed be a remedy;
it is the medicine for that which is caused by wind.
The divine Arundhatī has come.
Do not fear; you shall not die.
You will indeed become free from disease.
This is the remedy for what has been caused by wind.
The goddess Arundhatī has arrived.
The Arundhatīs converse like cows that have gone forth to wander.
Whomever I approach while he is afflicted, make him one who possesses a protector, make him one who possesses a protector! Make this one of mine subject to old age and death.
"O herb, make [him] a man;
for you, O Arundhatī, are the queen of all these herbs."
For you are protecting,
life-giving, and full of vigor;
O Arundhatī, I have brought you hither.
"May you not cross over from here"— thus [he spoke].
And for one pierced by a poisoned [arrow],
there is that which is the poison of evil, the evil of evil.
O Arundhatī, you are the destroyer of poison for that which has been bitten by a serpent.
— of the evil [karma] cast off by means of a countermeasure (…) // see 4bcd PS_15,16.5

Arundhatī (…) (see 15.16.4cd, PS_15,17.3).
Whatever poison is on the earth, whatever poison is in the plants—
That poison which the Brahmins collect from the plants for the sake of a woman...
That which the Brahmins collect is the harsh poison of the venomous serpent. […]
O Arundhatī, you belong to him who has been cast down by death, and to him who has been bitten by venomous serpents.
The destroyer of poison for the poison. Compose yourself; I have driven the consumption away from you;
you have ascended to the highest world.
Live by means of water, O vessel;
come hither from the city of the living.
O Apsarases, [I have] your liver.
I split open your bladder; I split open the Caṇḍāla, I split open the Arjuna,
and I split open Vṛtra for you.
Beneficial to all people, belonging to the five tribes,
adorned with great gold ornaments, and crested— all these were [struck] by Indra’s thunderbolt.
The bubble-like sorceries have been struck down;
with the base of the mortar, [I strike] Andhācī and Asitācī.
Kill this Vatsapa!
From afar I beheld them as they came rushing down from heaven.
May Indra strike down the Apsarases who steal the oblation of the gods;
let them be struck away from here.
Like female demons from a threshing floor,
go away to that man;
he goes away to the ocean.
May the celestial beings go to heaven;
may the female cranes go to the lake;
[and whatever is] in the cave of Ulungula.
Let those belonging to the Asuras go away;
O Āskandikā and Viskandikā,
let them dance away into the distance.
Let that dog dance with the spotted deer;
for the spotted deer is one that eats gold.
The divine dog Pariplava—
his name I have grasped for his safety.
Today I cut away your roots;
dance far away from here.
I break your terrible ribs.
And the *kīkasā*s were created by Brahmā;
there are thirty-one *aśvavatī*s and four *guṅgū*s.
Ten are auspicious, ten are cooked,
and twenty-five are long-haired;
this [is for] the owl-like creatures.
I pay homage to the Apsarases.
Those who sway upon their swings like garlands on a festoon.
(…) Those which move forward together with the rays of the sun... [PS 15.19.1] ...move forward together with the rays of the sun.
