Before a hundred autumns have passed,
may our out-breath, in-breath, and diffused breath, as well as our life-span and sight, be for beholding the sun.
O Bhaṭṭa, by a path that is neither too far nor too near,
go to the ancestors of King Yama—
those who are our father’s fathers and those who are our grandfathers.
To those who have entered the wide mid-air, and to those who pervade the earth and the sky—
to those ancestors we pay homage with reverence.
Those leaders who, striving in the highest realms, have cast off hostilities and are childless— they, having ascended to heaven, have found a world for themselves.
Shining upon the back of the firmament—
“The lowest heaven is full of water; the middle one is full of *pīlu* trees.”
"The third is indeed the radiant sky," in which the ancestors sit;
this indeed is the highest.
He sees the sun in the sky;
as a mother covers her son with her garment,
so do thou cover him from the earth.
This very thing, and indeed nothing else,
shall grow old; and yet another [thing] likewise— just as a wife [covers] her husband with a garment.
— Cover him with earth!
I cover you with the auspicious garment of the mother Earth.
May there be well-being for living beings; may that [well-being] be mine; may there be *svadhā* for the ancestors; may it be yours here.
O Agni and Soma, you who prepare the way, [grant us] a pleasant [resting place].
They have bestowed a treasure upon the gods and opened up the world;
let Pūṣan be sent forth— he who abandons those who travel by means of vehicles— let him go there by the paths.
May Pūṣan, the wise guardian of the world whose cattle are never lost, lead you away from here;
may he entrust you to these ancestors. Bhaṭṭa, [he] gives [you].
Agni [is for] the gods who are easy to find;
may Viśvāyu protect your life; may Pūṣan protect you on the distant path ahead.
Where the doers of good deeds abide, where they have gone—
there may the god Savitṛ place you.
This garment has come to you first for us.
Depart from here, O breath, whatever you have sustained here before;
knowing it well, pass over to your sacrifices and pious works; go to that place where your many [descendants] go.
I yoke these two carriers for you, to lead you to the world beyond; by means of them, [go] to the abode of Yama.
And go to the assembly. Envelop yourself with the cow-hides as a shield against the fire; cover yourself completely with fatness and with wisdom.
But let not the bold one, exulting in his fury and seeking to consume you,
strike you down with his weapon as he takes the bow from the hand of the dead.
Together with dominion, splendor, and strength—Bhaṭṭa... together with power;
right here you [are], and here we [are], possessing excellent heroes.
May we conquer all enemies and hostile intentions.
Taking the staff from the hand of the deceased,
together with his hearing, luster, and strength.
Take hold of abundant and flourishing wealth; come hither toward the world of the living.
This woman, praising the world of her husband—
Do not fall away; let the mortal man approach you, O lady, observing the ancient law.
Bestow upon her offspring and wealth here in this world.
Arise, O noble lady, toward the world of the living;
come to this breath of life that lies here. This [world] belongs to him who took your hand and desired you.
You have become the progenitor of your husband. (PS 18.68.12, Anuvāka 11)
I saw a young woman being led away,
a living one being carried off from the dead;
she who was alive had been shrouded by blind darkness.
From the east we have led her toward the west; O inviolable cow,
knowing this, you go toward the world of the living, traversing the path of the gods.
This is your Gopati; delight in him. Cause him to ascend to the heavenly world, reaching up to the sky and up to the reed-thicket.
O Agni, you are the crossing-place of rivers; you are the essence of the waters. O Agni, that which you have completely consumed by fire—
Extinguish it once again;
let the *kiyāmbu*, the *vatra*, the *śāṇḍadūrvā*, and the *vyalkaśā* grow up there.
This is one for you, and that beyond is another; enter into union with the third light.
Be gracious to our body in this union.
Beloved by the gods in the highest gathering place.
Arise, go forth, run forward;
make your home in the watery gathering place.
There, in harmony with the ancestors, rejoice in Soma and in the *svadhā* offerings.
Depart from your body and gather yourself together.
Let not your limb be loosened, nor your body;
enter fully into this well-established mind. Go to that place where you take pleasure in the earth.
May the Soma-loving fathers anoint me with splendor; may the gods anoint me with honey and ghee, furthering my sight.
May they increase my old age with the fullness of years.
May Agni anoint me with splendor;
may Viṣṇu anoint my wisdom in my mouth. Bhaṭṭa. meṃ.
May all the gods bestow wealth upon me;
may the pure waters purify me with their cleansing streams. May Mitra and Varuṇa encompass me.
May the Ādityas, the pillars of heaven, strengthen me; may Indra anoint my hands with splendor;
may Savitṛ grant me long life.
He who was the first among mortals to die,
the first to depart for this world—
to Vivasvat’s gathering place of men.
Worship King Yama with an oblation!
Depart, O Fathers, and come back again—
this sacrifice of yours is anointed with honey.
"Grant us wealth here, O Bounteous One; bestow upon us riches consisting of all heroic sons.
Kaṇva, Kakṣīvat, Purumīḍha, and Agastya.

Like herds of cattle in a land abounding in food, he has looked upon them.
When the fierce one [Indra] performed the final birth of the gods,

The radiant dawns have shone forth as an eternal law.
All that the gods carry is auspicious;
may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, protect me from the eastern direction.
The earth, extended by the arms [of the gods], is as if above the sky;

May Dhātṛ protect me from destruction from the southern direction; … (see stanza 2, PS_18,71.3).

Let all the sons of immortality hear, who have taken up their stations in the celestial realms;
I have ascended after the three steps of the radiant form.
I follow the four-footed path with my vow;
by means of the syllable, I measure this out and purify it at the navel of Cosmic Order.
For the sake of the gods he chose death; for the sake of progeny he did not choose immortality.
They made Bṛhaspati the seer of the sacrifices.
O Agni Jātavedas, you have bestowed your beloved body upon Yama; being praised, you have carried the oblations away after making them fragrant.
You have given to the ancestors; they have eaten with the *svadhā* offering; eat, O God, these presented oblations.
Seated upon the lap of the ruddy ones, bestow wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations.
O fathers, bestow that wealth upon your sons; bestow vigor upon them here.
O fathers who have been consumed by Agni, come hither!
Sit in every assembly, O you who are excellent leaders; eat the oblations presented upon the sacrificial grass,
and bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
The Soma-loving ancestors have been invited to these sacred grasses, to these dear offerings;
may they come hither, may they listen here.
May they speak for us and protect us—
those former fathers of ours, worthy of Soma, the most excellent ones who followed after us to the drinking of Soma.
May Yama, rejoicing with them, desiring [the offerings], eat the oblations according to his desire, together with those who desire them—
those who, striving, have thirsted for the gods.
O Agni, knower of the *hotṛ*-office, fashioned by hymns with chants, come hither with those who find the way well,
with the true *kavya* ancestors who sit at the *gharma* vessel.
O Agni, come with the thousand who are true, eaters of the oblation, worthy of the oblation, and who are borne on the same chariot with Indra and the gods, you who praise the gods.
With the former ancestors who sat at the *gharma* sacrifice,
approach this mother, the earth—
the wide-extending, most gracious Pṛthivī.
Soft as wool, O Earth, you who possess the sacrificial fee—may she protect you from the lap of Nirṛti.
Open wide, O Earth; do not press down upon me.
Be easy of access to him and easy of approach;
as a mother covers her son with the hem of her garment,
so do thou, O Earth, cover him.
May the earth, swelling wide, stand firm;
may a thousand columns rest upon it. May those dwellings be pleasant and dripping with clarified butter.
May there be shelters for him here at all times.
The earth props itself up for you;
bestowing this world upon you, I have not been afraid.
May the ancestors support this pillar; here Yama shall prepare your dwelling-place.
Atharvan [supports] the full cup.
That [soma] which you have brought for Indra, the possessor of the prize— let him create for it a world of good deeds;
therein the drop flows at all times.
O Agni, do not let this cup of ours be tilted;
it is dear to the gods who are worthy of Soma. This is the cup from which the gods drink.
In that very [place], the immortals rejoice.
When the black bird has pecked at you, or the ant, the serpent, or even a wild beast;
May Agni, the wise one, and Soma, who has entered into the Brāhmaṇas, satisfy us with all that from every side.
The plants are full of milk.
Abounding in milk is my speech;
moreover, that which is milk is full of milk— with that, do you two quicken me together.
"Imā nari" is one [verse].

Having abandoned blame, go again to your setting, O Bhaṭṭa; having indeed abandoned reproach, unite with a body full of splendor.
Those who were cremated by fire and those who were not cremated by fire—

the self-ruling one [brings] this guidance of the breath.
Just as he wills, he fashions his own body.
Grasp it, O Jātavedas;
let your splendor be powerful.
O Bhaṭṭa, burn his radiant body; O Bhaṭṭa, burn it! Then place him in the world of those who have performed meritorious deeds.
Give back again, O Lord of the Forest,
that which was placed within you,

May he sit at the assemblies, speaking.
May the mist be auspicious for you; may it settle auspiciously upon your back.
O cool one, O you who possess coolness, O refreshing one, O you who possess refreshment—
unite with the female frog in the waters!
Quench this very fire!
May Vivasvat grant us fearlessness; let death depart and immortality come to us.
May there be many heroes for me here;
may I possess abundance in horses and cattle.
May Vivasvat establish us in immortality.
May he who is the good protector, the swift-giver, the bounteous one—
protect these men from the reach of old age;
let not their life-breaths go to Yama.
Worship with oblations him who, as the sage of the fathers and the guardian of thoughts, has established himself in the mid-air by his greatness—
O you whose friends are all, [worship] him with offerings.
May Yama grant us further life to live.
Ascend to the highest heaven, O seers; do not be afraid.
O Soma-drinkers, O drinkers of Soma, this oblation is prepared for you;
we have come to the highest light. (PS 18.75.9)
Agni shines forth with his lofty banner; the bull bellows loudly across the two worlds (heaven and earth),

The buffalo grew in the lap of the waters;
when they beheld you with longing hearts as you flew toward the vault of heaven like a well-winged bird.
The golden-winged messenger of Varuṇa,
the swift bird in the womb of Yama—
O Indra, bring us wisdom.
As a father [instructs] his sons,
O much-invoked one, teach us in this prize-winning [contest]; living, may we attain the light.
"ye te pūrve" is one [verse].
PS 8.19.5 is repeated as PS 18.75.13 (75), Anuvāka 12.
Ascend the mother of the Jātavedases; I cause you all to ascend together by the paths of the fathers.

Go by those god-traversed paths, by which those who have sacrificed go to the heavenly world;

May [the sacrificial ladles] yield every desire for the sacrificer:
the *juhū* has supported the sky, the *upabhṛt* the intermediate space,

The image of the worlds, the full-backed one— may she, the full-backed one,
milk out for the sacrificer his own abode and vital strength.
O Dhruva, ascend the all-knowing earth.
Step upon the intermediate space with the *upahṛt*;
go to the sky with the *juhū* together with the sacrificer;

All the milch-cows, free from anger,

— From the north, from the center, from the intermediate space,
and from every direction, O Agni, protect us from the terrible! O Agnis, with your most peaceful bodies...

become a horse that carries on its back and carry us to where they rejoice in communal revelry with the gods.

bestow upon him, ordained by the Brahman, the lotus-seat of Agni and union with the world of the righteous.

him who belongs to Prajāpati, who is fit for sacrifice, and known by Jātavedas; making him cooked here, let them not look away.

May the fires enjoy him who has offered all; may the gods recognize his share in this.

About to fly up to the back of the firmament,

Agni is your Hotṛ, Bṛhaspati is your Adhvaryu;

May this sacrifice, offered and completed, proceed.

the gracious cow full of sweetness, for our well-being.
O Agni, do not harm the strengthening, exhilarating Aditi among the people in the highest heaven.

with sesame for their calves, yielding nourishment for him, be ever-present and never-failing.

May they sit near him as he speaks upon the surface of the waters,
milking forth nourishment without wavering—

For him, create a world as vast as his kinship.
Be right here a winner of wealth; be here in thought, here in resolve.
Dwell here, becoming more heroic, bestowing vital strength, and never failing;
may you satisfy our sons and grandsons.
These waters are honey-sweet;
yielding the ancestral offering (*svadhā*) and the immortal nectar (*amṛta*) for the fathers,
may the divine waters satisfy both [the gods and the ancestors].
O Waters, send forth this Agni;
may our fathers enjoy this sacrifice—
those who attend upon the strength of the months.
May they bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.

may they be full of *svadhā* for you.

Sarasvatī, whom the doers of good deeds invoke as they approach the sacrifice with the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).

Come forth both of you; drive away that which has oppressed you from here. O inviolable ones, turn toward us; that will be more desirable for you.

May the fathers recognize you as you depart;
gather your body limb by limb;

Parṇa, the king, is the covering of the sacrificial pots;
may vigor, strength, endurance, and vital energy come to us,
bestowing long life upon those who live.
For long life lasting a hundred autumns!
That portion of vigor which belongs to those who sacrifice here has become the sovereign lord of the stone-eaters.
Worship him with oblations, O you who have Viśvāmitra as friend;
may that Yama grant us further life.
Just as [there is] a palace for Yama...

even so do I sow this dwelling,
so that you may be many for me.
Support this gold which your father supported in former times, as he went from this world to the hand of his father in heaven.
Drive away [the disease] from the right side.
Those who are living and those who are dead, those who are born and those who are worthy of sacrifice— [may they all be freed].
Let a stream of clarified butter flow for them,
a hundredfold, drenching all;
the far-seeing bull of hymns flows on in purification.
The hero of the days, the furtherer of the dawns, the breath of heaven,
has bellowed toward the jars—
the jars that Indra brought from heaven, entering them with his inspired thought.
Your brilliant smoke spreads across the sky; your flame is extended like the sun shining with its light.
O purifier, you shine with compassion.
The moon advances toward the appointed place of Indra; as a friend, he does not disregard the agreement of his friend.
Like a bridegroom toward his brides, Soma flows into the jar by a hundredfold path,
as the Soma-loving fathers approach.
Along the deep paths traveled by the fathers,
bestowing upon us progeny and wealth.
For long life, for a hundred autumns!
Depart, O Soma-loving fathers, by the deep paths that lead to the ancestors.
Then, in the month, come back again to our house, O Bhatta, with oblations and food, possessing good offspring and brave sons. They have eaten and they have rejoiced.
The beloved ones have shaken themselves free; they, possessing their own splendor, have been praised.
Go back, O fathers, to your homes.
That single limb of yours which Agni Jātavedas has left behind, leading you to the world of the fathers—
that I now cause to enter back into you.
O all you ancestors, together with your limbs, rejoice! O so-and-so, here is your mind;
[we call it] like sisters [calling] a brother-in-law.
Cover him with earth;
rest here, do not be afraid,
you who dwell in this stall amidst the dung.
Bestowing vigor, united and true to their vows,
O houses, living, may we sit down near you.
The gods have bestowed vigor upon me.
I have brought strength for men and strength for the ancestors;
full of strength be my home.
The gods have granted me milk, and men as well;

May my houses be full of milk.
O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one.
Now, O Āditya, under your law, may we be sinless before Aditi—
those [hundred] of yours, O Varuṇa, those [thousand].
The great, sacrificial nooses are stretched out;
from them may Varuṇa, Soma, Indra, all the gods, and the Maruts of beautiful praise release us.
O Varuṇa, release from us all those snares—
those by which one is bound together, those by which one is bound apart—
so that we may live for a hundred autumns.
O King, protected and guarded by you,
we implore your wrath to be appeased with prostrations; we implore it to be appeased with sacrifices and with oblations.
O wise King Varuṇa, may you loosen those sins committed by us;
the moon is within the waters.
The fair-winged one speeds through the sky;
O you whose rims are gold, the lightnings do not find your track.
My wealth is in these two worlds, heaven and earth.
Sing, O Gāya; sing the *bṛhat* loudly; sing with splendor, O Atharvaṇa!
Praise the god Savitṛ.
Praise him, the son within the ocean, the youth of Truth,
whose speech is guileless and who is most gracious.
May that god Savitṛ, the lord of treasures, pour forth for us treasures;
may he grant both excellent hymns of praise and a good path.
O officiating priests, press the Soma for Indra and wash it;
may he who hears the call of the praiser hear our invocation as well.
Press the Soma for Indra, the drinker of Soma, the wielder of the thunderbolt;

May the drops of the soma-juice enter into you, as birds enter a tree, through the plant.
O roaring one, strike down the adversaries; drive away those possessed by demons. O gods, let that weapon be far from us!
May the curse of mortals be far away!
May our gift be like a friend; may Indra be our friend, and Savitṛ our friend.
May Bhaga, whose laws are true, be our friend.
May the goddesses, the wives of the lords of men, protect us with their great sheltering aid.
May they attend with unbroken wings.
I praise Agni, the All-Becoming; may he crush the serpent, the *balāsa*, and the fierce consumption.
O Aditi, keep divine fear far from us;

I praise Heaven and Earth, the mountains, and the waters.
May the Lord of Truth— Heaven, the Sun, the wide mid-air,

May the formidable Bhagas come to us for our protection.
May Indra and Pūṣan protect us; may Varuṇa and the Maruts protect us.

May Heaven and Earth protect us for our aid.
May the pressing-stone protect us, may Soma protect us from distress;

May the divine Aśvins, the doers of wondrous deeds, protect us; may Dawn and Night likewise grant us wide space.
May the Son of the Waters, who is never thwarted by anyone, [protect] even that.
O Aditi, as a god, grant us protection upon our heads.
Tvaṣṭṛ, Parjanya, and Brahmaṇaspati [have granted] my divine speech.
May Aditi with her sons and brothers protect us; may there be invincible power for our protection—
Aṃśa, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman.
May Aditi protect us from distress;
may his hatred depart unharmed; drive away the enemy who is near.

O Father Heaven, drive away misfortune from here!
O Soma, those who with their words and wondrous deeds cause our bodies to burn—

O Soma, with you as the archer, with you as the bow, [let them be struck]. With you as the archer, [let them be struck].

O Bhaṭṭa-kara!
Let us strike them down with our staffs and with wondrous deeds!
Let the foot-followers lead them away by the foot;
let the Fathers strike them down with their weapons.
Just as not one among these [deities] lives by means of that path on which Soma, Aditi,
and the guileless Mitra go.
Therefore, be our protector.
O Soma, whoever, being ill-disposed toward us who praise you well, seeks to harm us—

He who seeks to harm us, O Soma—strike him down.
Whether he be a kinsman or a stranger,
strike down his strength.

along with whatever belongs to him that has been destroyed,

Those oaths which belong to the earth,
those which are in the wide mid-air, and those which are in the onset of the wind—

O gods,
cut off their root, as one cuts the root of the *urvāru* gourd. O gods, whatever evil-doer has committed evil...

Let it flow away.

may your embryo likewise be firmly supported within the mountains.
Following the offspring for the sake of well-being.
Having flowed, those active ones have flowed through the day and through the night.
I, whose rite is excellent, address the divine waters;
the waters have been spoken of as fit for ritual action.
Let them release [the waters] from here for the sake of guidance;
let there be leaders immediately for the journey.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, human beings perform their work.
May these waters and plants be auspicious for us.
Of your hundred vessels and thousand veins, those which are intermediate have stood [there]. (Bhatt.: those intermediate ones have stood.)
The ends have come together;
the sand-made barriers have stood firm even across [the space].
Stay here, O Soma; do not move away. Those sisters who go forth, all dressed in red garments—[stay here].
Like women without brothers, they stand there with their luster destroyed.
Stay, O lower one! Stay, O higher one!
Moreover, you stand in the middle;
and let the little finger stand. Let this great vessel stand firm. (PS 19.4.16)
Section 1.
Homage to the slayers of gods, homage to the slayers of kings,
and also to those who are the slayers of commoners.
To them, O Death, be salutations;
to you, salutations! Salutation to your higher speech, and salutation to your distant speech.
O Death, homage to you for good intention;
homage to you for evil intention;
homage to you for your sorcerers.
Homage to you, O medicines;
homage to you, O roots, O Death;
this homage to the Brahmins.
The ninety-nine tendons that meet together—
may they all perish from here.
Like the reverence paid to those who have passed away,
the seven and seventy [veins] converge upon the shoulder-joints.
(From here let all those [curses] perish like the insults of one who has been humiliated.
// PS_19.5.5 Those which are five and fifty, Bhatt. [reads] "yāḥ" (a misprint).
The neck-ropes come together toward them;
let all those spells perish from here like the honors paid to the low-born.
Our food, our non-food, and the essence—O fierce one, those are our food. May we eat your groats; may we consume them.
For you are not that [self] which you have obscured;
[you are] Babhru and Babhrukarṇa.
The blue jar-house;
behold the corpse! O Tāvilikā, at the appointed time! (Bhatt.: O Tāvilikā, at the time!)
This Ailava has caused [the offering] to flow;
here, enjoying his own oblation with his mind, svāhā!
Svāhā! Whatever I do here with my mind, for whomsoever I offer this into you, O terrible one—
for the sake of releasing these who are bound.
People regard you as "the Earth," but I know you all around as "Nirṛti. O you who possess the oblation, you are the being; this is your portion.
Therefore, let that be performed for you; Svāhā!
O Nirṛti, most desirable one, release from us those iron fetters.
In agreement with Yama and Yamī—
being in accord with him who hates us and whom we hate— cast all those snares upon him who hates us. PS_19,5.12
You are the best of herbs;
the trees are your attendants. May you be our attendant.
Whoever seeks to harm us—
whether he be a kinsman or one who is not a kinsman— whoever seeks to harm us.
Having crossed over all my kinsmen, may I become the most excellent,
just as Soma is among the plants.
The best oblation is thus spoken of:
"O Lord, may I become the best among men, even as thou art the best among the trees. (PS 19.5.15)
"Varuṇa shall ward off [evil]"— this is one verse.
"By the word of Indra,
and of Mitra and Varuṇa..."
By the word of all the gods, we ward off consumption from you,
just as Vṛtra [held back] these waters.
He has propped apart those who were moving in every direction.
Thus, with Agni Vaiśvānara, I ward off your consumption.
With the firm oblation, we touch Soma with that which is firm; we enter [into him].
May Indra here make the tribes bring tribute exclusively for you;
I have brought you hither, you have come within.
Stand firm, immovable;
let all the people come to you;
let not the kingdom fall away from you.
Be right here;
do not fall away, remaining as immovable as a mountain.
O Indra, stand firm here;
establish the kingdom here.
Indra has established this.
With the firm oblation,
may Soma and this Brahmaṇaspati speak in his favor.
Surely for you, O [sacrificer], is the god Savitṛ;
surely the god Bṛhaspati;
surely for you are both Indra and Agni.
May the kingdom be firmly sustained for those who uphold it.
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth;
the oceans and the mountains are firm.
Firm indeed by his law, firm is this king of the people;
a bull from heaven, he is the bull of the lord of bulls.
This one is the bull of the earth;
you are the bull of all that exists— be the sole bull.
The ocean rules over all flowing waters;
Agni is the master of the earth;
Sūrya rules over the constellations.
You are the sovereign of the Asuras,
the preeminent one among men.
You are the half-share of the gods; become the sole bull among them.
May they circumambulate their own paths.
Indra and Pūṣan have sped forth;
let those armies of the enemies be confounded today, far away.
The enemies, bewildered, move about like headless serpents.
Now, let Indra slay the best of these who have been obstructed by Agni;
bind the bull’s hide upon them.
Strike fear into the deer;
let the enemy flee away,
and let the cow come hither.
O bull-like Agni, you gather for yourself all the riches of the noble man;
you are kindled at the place of libation.
Bring those riches to us.
Agree with one another; be united;
may your minds be in harmony.
As the gods of old, being of one accord, attend to their portion;
the mantra is common, the assembly is common.
May your hearts be equal and your minds be in harmony; with this common oblation I offer for you, so that you may be of one accord.
The Sun rises from the sky before all things, he who has ascended [them],
roaring like a bull.
The Sun, seen by all, the destroyer of the unseen, has risen over the mountains— he who knows the lifespan, the wise one.
I have brought the herb of Kaṇva that has been heard of, the all-healing one;
by means of it, bring those unseen [demons] to rest.
The cows have settled in the stall; the wild beasts have entered their lairs; the lights of men have gone out.
Those who were not seen longed for you;
you flow forth from the Himavat and go toward the Sindhu.
O divine Waters,
grant me that healing medicine for the heart which shone forth from my eyes.
With his heels and his chest,
he struck all those waters; Tvaṣṭṛ made them as useless as a damaged cart-pole.
O queens of the Sindhu, wives of the Sindhu, you who are all rivers—
grant us the healing medicine for that.
With that, may we enjoy [it] together.
May the divine folk purify me; may the sages purify me with their inspired thought.
May all beings purify me;
may Pavamāna purify me. May Pavamāna purify me.
For wisdom, for skill, for life, and so that we may long behold the sun—
O God Savitṛ, [grant this] by both means.
With the purifier and the pressed juice,
cleanse us so that we may see;
[remove] the first onset of envy.
Whether it be low or high,
that anger and heartache, that grief—
we expel it from you with our mantra.
Whatever is seated in your heart, that restless mind— because of that, I release my envy toward you.
Like the breathless hide of a bellows,
as the earth is dead-minded,
so is the dead-minded one more dead-minded than the dead.
Just as the mind of one who has died is supreme, so too is the mind of the immortal one among mortals supreme. May both Heaven and Earth, the wise ones, protect me.
May Śukra and Bṛhaspati fulfill my sacrificial fee;
may Svadhā take heed of me, and may Soma, Agni, Vāyu, Savitṛ, and Bhaga come to me.
May mind come back, may life return; may sight come back, may intention return.
May Vaiśvānara, the undeceivable protector of our bodies, [grant this].
May he stand within us, protecting us from misfortune and from blame.
We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies; we have united with an auspicious mind.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, the bounteous giver, create wide space; may he mend whatever is injured in our bodies.
Bhaṭṭa:
This is that superior [gift] for the one who is united,
by which I adorn Indra for his attainment.
Increase his dominion and great glory,
as rain makes the grass grow. O Agni and Soma, increase his dominion!
Increase his wealth;
furthermore, in the conquest of the kingdom,
make him superior to his rival.
Whether one is a kinsman or a non-kinsman,
whether born [there] or a stranger.
For the sacrificer who presses the soma,
grant us all that;
may great glory, impelled by Indra, increase.
O thousand-edged one, well-fashioned and powerful,
who hastenest along for long life,
increase the one who offers oblations for the sake of complete success.
Glorious is Indra, glorious is Agni, glorious was Soma born; glorious is he over all that has come to be.
"I am the most glorious.
O Agni, we who are glorious through our glories would honor you, the glorious one, with this oblation.
Grant us that sovereignty impelled by Indra;
may we abide under your protection and your favor. [As one draws] the string from a bow...
I draw forth your anger from your heart;
then, having become of one mind, let us two associate like two female friends.
We lead away your wrath; let us two associate like friends.
Beneath you, we place your wrath with a stone.
We place [it] down by means of the Guru.
I trample upon your fury with my two heels and my two forefeet.
May your punishment pass away;
I drive away your wrath.
Golden was the path that led [there].
The oars were made of gold;
the ships were golden,
by which I brought Kuṣṭha away.
Bhaṭṭa [says]: "Born on the mountain Suparṇasuvana from the Himavat, [he] drove away [the darkness]. (PS 19.8.13)
They approach with riches that which is renowned;
with *kuṣṭha* plants, [there is] the destroyer of fever.
Bhaṭṭa: For you, O Kuṣṭha, who are born among the mountains as the most powerful of plants—
O destroyer of fever by means of the *kuṣṭha* plants, destroy the fever from here! PS_19,8.15 (8) Anuvāka 2.
Offer great reverence to the Idāvatsara, the Parivatsara, and the Saṃvatsara;
may we abide in the benevolent favor of these worthy of sacrifice.
May we also, O auspicious ones, be in a state of goodwill. May those many paths of yours that lead to the gods,
which traverse heaven and earth, [be ours].
They move about;
whichever of them brings us non-deprivation, O all you gods, bestow that upon us.
O Autumn, Winter, the Cool Season, Spring, Summer, and the Rainy Season, bestow all prosperity upon us here.
O Bhaṭṭas, may we abide in the rains; may we share in the cattle and the plants; may we be in your windless shelter.
May Vaiśvānara come forth from afar for our protection;
may Agni deliver us from distress with his hymns.
May Vaiśvānara come to us,
together with this sacrifice and this my excellent hymn of praise.
Vaiśvānara, together with the Aṅgirases, has fashioned for us the hymn and the sacrifice;
may he bestow upon them splendor and the light of heaven.
I have conquered you as you were marked out; I have conquered you as you were hemmed in,
just as a wolf seizes a sheep.
Thus do I crush your deed,
just as the thunderbolt strikes down a tree forever without resistance.
Thus may I, with the dice, strike down that gambler without resistance— him who is swift among the swift and slow among the slow.
May fortune come from every side to the people who revere the gods;
may that which is placed within my hand be accomplished for me.
As far as heaven, as far as earth,
as far as the sun shines—
so far do I create my poison for you.
As long as the rivers flow,
they rise up panting like cattle from their stall.
For those who behold the poison of snakes,
no speaker of falsehood is found; he whose bow is spotted has struck down [the enemy].
Having settled upon the head at the junction of the vessels,
the poison has caused the limbs to fall apart.
O gods, let not the serpent slay us, our children, and our men;
may he not release his grip upon us as if we were bound.
I shall not close that which you have opened.
I join your teeth with your teeth; I join your jaws with your jaws.
I join your tongue with [my] tongue, I join your mouth with [my] mouth.
Homage to the black serpent!
Homage to Tiraścīrajī, to Svajā, to Babhru; homage,
homage to the divine hosts.
For the mind, for consciousness, for thought, and for intention; for perception, for hearing, and for sight.
May we worship with an oblation for out-breath,
in-breath,
and diffused breath, which possesses abundant seed.
May we worship Sarasvatī, the far-reaching one, with our oblation;
may the divine seers not forsake us.
You who protect the body, pure ones born of austerity,
immortal ones, attend to us mortals; grant us extended life that we may live.
This indeed is the remedy, this is the remedy of Rudra,
by which he [warded off] the arrow with its single-pointed shaft.
They spoke against Śataśalyā:
"Sprinkle him with *jālāṣa*, drench him with *jālāṣa*!"
The cooling, auspicious medicine— grant that to us for our life, and grant us peace and bliss.
And let nothing cause us distress;
may you forgive our offense, and may everything be a healing for us.
May the bounteous Indra make us glorious.
May Soma, Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Agni make me glorious;
may the god Savitṛ make me glorious,
and may I be dear to the giver of the sacrificial fee.
Just as Indra is glorious between heaven and earth, as he is among the waters and the plants,
so [is he] among all the gods.
Thus may we be glorious among the gods.
O glorious ones, may we approach the glorious Indra with glory and honor him with oblations.
May he grant us a kingdom impelled by Indra;
may we abide under his protection and his favorable proclamation. May Varuṇa, Soma, and Agni come hither!
May Bṛhaspati come here with the Vasus; all you kinsmen, of one mind, gather around the glory of this formidable lord.
Bhaṭṭa:
"Come here, do not go away; may Pūṣan create a path for you from beyond. (PS 19,10.10)
Vāstoṣpati has called after you; O kinsmen, may this delight be yours in me. Whatever vigor is within your hearts— [may it be mine].
Whatever intention has entered the mind— that intention I satisfy with the oblation of clarified butter.
May delight born within me be yours. All of you, come to my call, as if to that of Indra and Agni, with minds intent upon me.
May Bṛhaspati yoke you for me;
with one mind, follow my word!
I seize your minds with my mind.
Come to my mind with your thoughts;
I bring your heart under my control.
Come as followers along the path that leads to me.
Let your eye go to me, let your breath and the Creator follow my path; may he prepare the way for you—
both those who are great and those who are children.
Come after me with those who have gone before.
According to Bhaṭṭa,
[the verses] beginning with "The aśvattha tree, the abode of the gods" (PS 19,10.15) are recited at the end of the *ajāyata* formula.
PS 7.10.6 is repeated:
"You are born from the gods, established as the friend of Soma."
Be gracious to his out-breath, in-breath, and sight; you have bound him to the iron post. (Or:
you shall bind him.)
He who was addressed by a thousand deaths—
Yama shall give you back to me again;
let us honor that god with an oblation.
That bond which the goddess Nirṛti has fastened upon your necks, so that it cannot be untied—
that I loosen for you, for the sake of long life and strength.
—Eat the food free from disease, being impelled [by us].
Homage be to you, O Nirṛti, who possesses all boons; homage be to you!
Untie this iron bond.
Release him from the iron bonds;
in agreement with Yama and the ancestors,
cause him to ascend to the highest heaven.
Offer this oblation for internal burning with clarified butter; it is the destroyer of sorcerers.
O Agni, burn away the demons from afar.
Let them not consume our bodies.
O Piśācas, Śarva has shattered your necks; may Agni crush your backs.
I have brought you, O plants of all-pervading power,
into contact with death; [drive] away the Piśāca from below us.
Make us free from piśācas from the north;
O Indra, make us free from piśācas from behind and free from piśācas from the front.
Indra was the first to perform the handless-act against the Asuras;
we sever the arms of our enemies.
By this oblation,
may our enemy be rendered handless;
may he who comes against us with armies for battle be struck down.
O Indra, strike them down with a great weapon;
let their destroyer, pierced through, run away. May wrath depart; may it go far away. May it depart.
— Lower their arms, which are yoked by thought;
O Parāśara, crush their forward-flying vigor and bring wealth hitherward to us.
Those who stretch [the bow], those who draw it back, and those who run while shooting—
may you be handless enemies; may Indra [overcome] you!
May Indra drive you away today.
May the enemies be rendered handless;
we cause their limbs to wither away.
O Indra, so that we may distribute their sacred knowledges among our herds, let there be handlessness for those who are handless, and let it befall him whom [we hate].
O gods, you hurl the arrow;
may my warriors be victorious through the steadfast Indra who shares the earth.
The *aśvattha* tree has grown upon the *śamī*;
there the rite for a male child was performed;
that indeed is its remedy.
That which they bring for women is that.
Bhaṭṭa says: ...
for semen indeed exists in the male, and it is discharged into the female.
That indeed is the knowledge of the son; Prajāpati spoke it,
and Prajāpati approved it.
Sinīvālī has fashioned [this child];
she has placed female offspring elsewhere, and here she has placed a male.
Bhaṭṭa: Or rather, [the verse] "yā oṣadhayaḥ somarājñīḥ" (PS 11.7.5) is repeated at PS 19.12.3;
[then] "muñcantu mā śapathyāt" (PS 19.12.4).
And also from that which belongs to Varuṇa,
and also from the fetter of Yama, and from every evil deed against the gods.
Whatever we have committed with the eye, whatever with the mind, and whatever with speech, whether waking or sleeping;
May Soma, the wise one, purify me from that sin by means of the *svadhā* offering.
May the sacrifice be victorious; may Agni be victorious.
May Soma be the conqueror; may Indra be the conqueror. May this man prevail over all hostile armies.
Thus, O Agnihotra, we worship with this oblation.
May there be *svadhā* for you, O Mitra and Varuṇa; cause the progeny-bearing dominion to swell here with sweetness.
Drive away enmity and misfortune to a distance.
"Bestow upon him sovereignty, splendor, and vigor! [This is one verse. "This hero... [is another verse].
PS 7.4.6 is repeated at PS 19.12.9: "Like the spreading flame of a fierce fire, he departs while lamenting like one intoxicated."
To that ruddy, brown Takman,
who possesses glowing wealth, let there be homage;
homage to Yama, and homage be to Death.
Homage to King Varuṇa, the radiant one;
homage to the Lord of the Field; homage to Heaven; homage to Earth; homage to the plants.
This [fever] which makes people green,
burning them like fire with its scorching heat— therefore, O *takman*, become sapless.
Then go away, either facing downward or toward the lower direction.
Bhaṭṭa: Now follows the supplementary verse (anvaṅ):
"May Indra conquer, may he not be conquered; may he rule as the supreme sovereign among kings."
To be celebrated, to be praised, and to be extolled— may you be one to be approached and honored here.
O Indra, you are the supreme sovereign, the seeker of glory.
You are the conqueror of existence for all people; you rule over these divine subjects. May your sovereign power be long-lived and undecaying.
In the eastern direction you are the sovereign king, O Indra; in the northern direction, O slayer of Vṛtra, you are the destroyer of the Dasyus. Wherever the rivers flow, that is your conquest.
To the south: "Thou art the bull, to be offered.
Anuvāka 3.
I call upon you, O Indra, from afar, before the narrow straits; I call the fierce one who is most mindful.
The one-born with many names—
whatever weapon of the army rises today,
seeking to strike us down.
There we enclose Indra’s arms on all sides;
we enclose Indra’s arms.
May the Protector who protects all around protect us!
O God Savitṛ and King Soma,
make me well-disposed for my well-being.
The gods have given; Sūrya has given; Heaven has given; Earth has given; all the Sarasvatīs have given.
With a focused mind, [one should perform] the neutralization of poison:
"O gods, you *upajīkas*, whatever water you poured upon the desert..."
Therefore, O daughter of the Asuras, you have been begotten by a god who has defiled this poison.
You are the sister of the gods; you were born from heaven and earth;
you have made poison sapless.
Drive out the loosening of the bones, the loosening of the joints, the heart-disease that has taken hold, and all phlegm.
And that which resides in the limbs and in the joints—
O Aṅgeṣṭhā, I destroy the phlegm of the one afflicted by phlegm, like a lotus.
I cut his bond,
like the root of an ūrvāru gourd;
let him fall away from here, rendered powerless.
Like a bird from its dwelling, like a year-old calf from its mother—
run away, O non-slayer of heroes!
Be virile, breathe forth, grow, and expand;
let your member grow according to its proper parts.
With that, drive away the woman.
That by which they make the emaciated fat, and by which they urge on the sick;
Therefore, O Brahmaṇaspati,
extend his limbs like a bow;
I extend your limbs.
Step upon it as one places a string on a bow; stride like a deer toward a red bull,
never growing weary.
O gods, since the dove, sent as a messenger by Nirṛti, has come here seeking [us],
we shall praise you and make amends for it.
May it be well with our bipeds and quadrupeds!
O gods, may the dove sent to us be auspicious; may this bird be harmless in our home.
May Agni, the sage, enjoy our oblation;
may the winged missile spare us. May the winged missile not harm us.
The female owl makes her dwelling in the fire-chamber;
may she bring us peace for our cattle and our men; O gods, let not the dove harm us here.
Rejoicing in nourishment, we lead the cow around, smoothing out the difficult places with our feet; with a verse, drive away the dove that has come to displace us.
Having abandoned its strength, let it fly away— the swiftest of flyers.
I drive you out, I push you away, O pigeon, together with the demon.
Since you do not suffer there again, we cause you to go thither.
Bhaṭṭa: gamayāmasi (misprint). PS 19,13.17 (13):
Just as this draft-animal, O Aśvins, comes together and moves forward;
Thus let your mind come together with mine and turn toward me;
I draw your mind to myself.
Like a royal horse on its back,
like grass cut by a scythe—
may your mind be entangled within me.
From the hands of Bhaga, [the power] of collyrium, honey-juice,
costus,
and spikenard.
I bring this entreaty.
Here comes Aryaman from the east, with his hair-locks loosened.
Bhaṭṭa Viṣatastuka,
having desired it, [performed] for his wife and for the maiden who did not know her husband.
O Aryaman, this woman has come from her own home to the assembly of others;
O Aryaman, surely consider her case!
Another approaches the assembly.
Dhātṛ has supported the earth, Dhātṛ has supported the sky and the sun.
May Dhātṛ bestow upon this maiden a husband according to her desire;
may the waters send forth sweetness for me.
The Sun brought light for me;
all the gods born of fervor have done so for me;
and the god Savitṛ has granted me wide space.
I have upheld the earth and the sky;
I have generated the seven rivers together;
I am both the truth and the falsehood that I speak.
I encompass all speech and all vital power;
I have spread out the earth and the sky; I have created the seven seasons together.
I have encompassed all speech, I who took pleasure in Agni and Soma as my two companions. First [of all gifts] for us from the oxen...
O Arundhatī, grant protection to the milch-cows, to the barren cow, to the birds, and to the four-footed creatures.
May the herb Arundhatī, together with the gods, grant protection;
may she make the cow-pen full of milk.
And [protect] the men from disease.
I address the manly,
multiform, fortunate,
and life-giving one.
May she carry away Rudra’s missile far from our cattle.
Yama, Death, Aghamāra, Nirṛtha—
Bhava, Śarva, the archer Nīlaśikhaṇḍin,
and the divine hosts rose up with their armies.
May they spare our heroes.
With mind, oblations, fervor, and clarified butter,
[I offer] to Śarva, to the King, and to Bhava.
I pay homage to those worthy of homage; let them lead the poison of evil away from us. Protect us from the poison of evil and from slaughter!
May we be in the good graces of Agni and Soma, the Maruts of pure will, the All-gods, the Maruts of the All-gods, and Vāta and Parjanya. PS_19,14.15 (14)
Knowing with the mind and being fully aware, O Bhaṭṭa, let them not contend with divine wrath;
let no loud clamor arise among the many.
When the day of Indra has arrived, may the arrow fall upon those who have struck out against us;
may your minds be united and your vows be one.
We bring our intentions into harmony;
those of you who are divided in purpose,
we cause them to agree with one another.
May there be a making known of your mind, and likewise a making known of your heart;
and also that which is weary of the vulva.
By that he makes you conscious:
"May your bodies be united, may your minds be united, and may your skins be united."
May Brahmaṇaspati and Soma bring you into harmony; may there be concord between us and our own people.
Grant us consciousness from the enemies;
O Aśvins,
bestow consciousness upon us here.
Just as the Ādityas and the Vasus became united with the Maruts, fierce and free from resentment,
even so, O eater of the three-fold food, be free from resentment.
Make this people of one mind;
drive that rival away from his home who attacks us.
With unassailable oblation,
Indra has driven him away. Go to the three distant realms!
Go beyond the five peoples;
go beyond the seventy luminous realms as far as the sun is in heaven.
The god Indra has sent you to the furthest distance,
so that you shall not return again.
For through eternal years,
O Apāmārga, you have become one whose fruit is directed toward us.
Drive all my curses far away from me.

And whatever our rival curses us with, and whatever our kinsman curses us with— Bhaṭṭa-varīyas (perhaps a misprint for Bhaṭṭa-bhārgava?). PS 19,15.10: And whatever our rival curses us with, and whatever our kinsman curses us with.
Whatever curse Brahmā utters from his mind,
all that is beneath our feet;
[the curses] hated by the wicked, impelled by the gods.
As a creeper shakes off dust with water,
so may you shake off all curses from me.
When they sit around him and prepare him for seeing, Agni is fully kindled by his tongues.
It rises up from the heart.
From the fire Sāntapana, I take hold of the station for the sake of long life.
Truly, he whose mouth Death beholds emitting smoke— he who knows his fuel— [is not seen by him].
One who places his foot upon a path prepared by a Kṣatriya does not step into a pitfall for death.
Successive enemies do not slay him, nor does he go down into ruin—
the wise Kṣatriya who [knows] this of Agni.
He utters the name for the sake of long life:
"The sky has stood firm, the earth has stood firm; this entire world has stood firm."
These mountains stand firm;
the horses have stopped in their course—
he who has breathed forth at the expansion.
I call upon that herdsman who has uttered the supreme goal, who brings [them] back and turns [them] away.
The *āvṛt* (turning), the *nyāvṛt* (returning),
the *abhyavartana* (turning toward), and the *āyana* (coming); these are the four *āvṛts* of Agni.
With these we satisfy you;
O Jātavedas, turn back!
May there be a hundred ways for you to return.
A thousand are your turnings back;
with them, bring him back.
O divine Soma, be one who does not let the waters flow away.
O Maruts, be gracious to us in this sacrifice!
Let not overwhelming power find us, nor ill-spoken word; let not hateful misfortune reach us.
May that divine weapon which seeks to slay and approaches today with the intent to kill pass us by.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, drive that evil away from us, both from here and from there.
O Varuṇa, ward it off! Grant us great protection; ward off the deadly weapon far away.
O Indra, Maghavan, drive away our enemies to the east; O overcomer, drive them away to the west;
drive them away to the north, O hero, and drive them away to the south.
So that we may rejoice in your wide protection.
By this oblation of the existent, may he swell up again.
May the wife whom we have found for him increase with essence;
may she increase with progeny.
May he increase through royal power;
may these two shafts be possessed of a thousandfold strength and remain undecaying.
Tvaṣṭṛ begot his wife;
Tvaṣṭṛ has given you as her husband. Tvaṣṭṛ [bestowed] a thousand lifespans.
May he grant you long life.
He flies through the intermediate space,
beholding all beings.
This is the greatness of Śunaḥ Divya;
for him I offer this oblation.
Your birth is in the waters, your dwelling place is in heaven.
The ocean is your self, your greatness upon the earth;
this is the majesty of the divine dog;
for him, I offer this oblation.
Those three Kālakāñjas who dwell in heaven like gods—
I have invoked them all for protection.
For his safety, [we pray to you],
O divine dog who does not slay heroes, whom you cause to faint.
I drive you away with a prayer;
do not strike down this man,
O tawny one with iron fangs.
The divine dog Pariplava—
his name I have grasped for his safety.
"May he live for us.
"May this lord of the atmosphere, the nourisher, protect us."
Grant us incomparable abundance within our homes.
O Lord of the Sky,
you must maintain strength within our dwellings.
May nourishment come, may wealth come!
O God Saṃsphāna, you rule over thousandfold prosperity;
grant us of that, and may we enjoy it from you.
May we be full of devotion toward you; svāhā! (16) Anuvāka 4.
You are the controller; you restrain the hand;
you drive away the demons, grasping both progeny and wealth.
This one has become a wrist-band.
O wrist-band, hold fast the womb for the sake of producing an embryo.
O boundary-stone, place a son within me;
bring him hither, you who have come. Bring back that which you carried as a bracelet.
Aditi desired a son;
Tvaṣṭṛ bound him for her so that she might give birth to a son.
I take the name of the one who has come from afar,
the King Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra.
By that path by which the Aśvins brought Sūryā Sāvitrī to Vāsava Śatakratu.
Therefore Bhaga said to his wife: "Let him bring [the bride] hither.
That hook of yours which bestows wealth—
O great Indra, you are golden; with that [splendor], O Śatakratu, bestow a wife upon this man who seeks a wife.
O Medhā, come first to us with cattle and horses;
you are among the rays of the sun.
You are our one worthy of sacrifice.
I [invoke] wisdom, the foremost,
endowed with sacred knowledge, praised by the seers.
Drunk by those practicing the holy life,
I choose the protection of the gods;
wisdom in the evening, wisdom in the morning.
We have praised Medhā, rising up from the midday;
we have praised Medhā, rising up with the ascending sun.
The gods are in the essence of the earthly king,
in the body of Bhaga, and in his strength.
May Soma bestow life and splendor upon him; may Bṛhaspati [bestow it].
O Jātavedas, grant him long life.
O Tvaṣṭṛ, bestow offspring and vigor upon him;
O Savitṛ, send forth for him abundance of wealth.
May he live a hundred autumns through you.
May this blessing bestow upon us vigor, good offspring, skill, and wealth that brings great luster;
may Indra, conquering with might, win lands for us.
Making my other rivals inferior,
Savitṛ has come here with the razor; O Vāyu, come with warm water!
The Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, being of one mind and highly wise, have gathered together at the pressing of King Soma.
Bhaṭṭa: (a)vapan. PS 19,17.13:
With that razor with which Savitṛ, the knower, shaved for King Soma and Varuṇa.
By that [act], O Brahmins, may this [child] be born; may this hero be tireless and long-lived.

May Prajāpati hold fast again and again so that it may be well-sown: those veins and arteries of yours...
They have entered into your limbs;
from all of them together, we call forth the poisons.
O Rudra, that arrow which you have aimed at your limbs and your heart—
this very one we [withdraw] from you today.
We pull apart the one who spreads in all directions.
Homage to you, O Rudra, as you cast [your bolt]; homage to your arrows that have been aimed.
Homage to those being released;
homage to you who are extended; [homage] to those directed downward around the head.
Those hundred vessels of yours—
let them burst apart for you,
each separately, following that pit of blood.
Let the Rodanāvatī rivers flow along that Lohitāvaṭa,
so that they may not take delight within this [place]. Bhaṭṭa, let them not take delight.
Like water flowing in a favorable direction.
Bhaṭṭa:
May the sun go favorably westward; may the rivers made to flow westward flow back.
May this stream of yours flow downward; may it cut through the plants. [Bring] this barley with the eightfold unions.
They have drawn [thee] forth with six yokes; he indeed has driven away the injury from thy body as it turned toward thee.
The wind blows downward; the sun shines downward;
the cow yields milk downward.
May your ailment be brought low.
Indeed, the waters are healers; the waters drive away disease.
May the waters, flowing toward the ocean,
carry away your malady— those who come here for battle.
Having made them into banners in their ranks,
Indra bound them with a cord;
you, O Agni, have bound them together at the meeting of day and night.
As many as the streams flow, as many as the hosts thunder—
Indra has encompassed them all with his bond.
O Agni, do thou unite them at the meeting—
those who are highest and those who are lowest, as well as those who are middlemost and those who meet in between.
Indra has bound them around with a cord;
you, O Agni, have bound them together at the meeting of day and night.
Bṛhaspati is your binder.
May Savitṛ provide the bond; may Indra and Agni provide the bond;
may Bhaga and the two Aśvins provide the bond.
O divine Sūrya,
with all those rays of yours which are extended across the sky when you have risen, protect me today.
Make me pleasing to men;
place me among those who shine with sacred knowledge (*brahman*), and place me among those who shine as kings.
O Lust, bestow lust upon me among the Vaiśyas and Śūdras; O Lust, [bestow] lust upon that lust which is in gold.
Those splendors which are in Agni and those which are in Sūrya— O Bṛhaspati, Indra and Agni, bestow those splendors upon me.
Release me from evil, O self-controlled one; being merciful, grant us favor and establish me in auspicious abodes.
Bestow upon us that which is unswerving!
O Evil One, you who do not leave me—
him indeed we abandon you.
O immortal one with a thousand eyes, having spoken against us elsewhere,
we [meet] at the turning point of the path.
We purify you who are free from evil. Go to him who hates us;
slay him whom we hate.
You are girt like a corpse;
I have found no enjoyment in you.
O Evil One, I split your head!
So that you may not suffer further:
May Indra protect us from death’s noose by day for our well-being.
May the sky protect us from the middle,
and the queenly earth for our well-being;
may Sūrya protect us by day.
May Vāta protect us from the snare of death for our well-being;
may Day and Night protect us for our well-being.
May Soma protect us by day from the noose of death for our well-being. Bhaṭṭa, [protect us] by night.
PS_19,19.6. May Soma protect us by day from the noose of death for our well-being.
May the waters protect us from within;
may Nirṛti have no power over us.
May your eye and your heart be united. (Bhatt reads *cakṣuṃ*)
The mind is the dwelling of the mind;
by means of an oblation of clarified butter (ghṛta) for this cow that has a calf of the same form, [one attains the goal].
That reconciliation which Kakṣīvat—
the son of the Aṅgirases— discovered,
by that may the gods [favor] you two today.
They have brought you two together in love;
there is a reconciliation for you both in mind and a reconciliation in heart.
Moreover, whatever weariness there is in Bhaga,
with that I bring you two together;
I [unite] your mind with my mind.
I seize you with my eye; thus, embrace me, so that your mind may remain fixed upon me.
May that [enemy] turn back toward me like the wheel of a chariot;
let him be like a blade of grass cut down by a gust of wind.
He has enveloped me with his mind. I have moved around you from the male relative, from the mother, and from the sister.
I have brought you away from other women with this herb,
you who are Indra’s consort.
In which assembly they sit;
its leaves are gold and its bark is silver.
Therefore, O Aśvattha, homage to you,
who fills the intermediate space with your branches and with your root.
Homage to you, O Aśvattha tree, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns;
you whom even the wild beast does not reach.
O Aśvattha tree, homage to you, who, flying with both wings like a bird, supports the entire heaven.
Born under the Jyeṣṭhaghni constellation,
do not harm the parents of Yama’s two liberators while growing; may they be pleasant and auspicious to you, even as tigers.
May he carry us across all difficulties.
On the tiger-like day was born the hero, born under the stars, the all-hero, the excellent hero.
Do not harm your parents as you grow; may the gods accept this oblation for you. Those Rohiṇīs who have the gods as their husbands...
Like a milch-cow, she swells;
may the three Vyashṭakās there proclaim everything for your progeny and for the world of living beings.
When the gods, the Śakras, churned man with man by means of two moist kindling-sticks,
there the pair of like origin was brought to fruition.
With your excellent splendor, [grant us] living offspring who reach old age.
O Aśvins, strike down the winged bird, the glider, and the mouse;
shatter his head, crush his jaws, and destroy his teeth.
Just as the *vyadvara* does not devour our grain, so do you two grant us safety for our crops.
O *tarda*, O *pataṅga*!
O you who are well-cooked,
eat this grain;
do not harm it, but depart.
O Lord of the sacrifice, O Lord of the slaughter,
you whose teeth are sharp, hear us; like a Hotṛ priest, consume the oblation.
O you with severed tongues, approach! O devourer, with your tongue that reaches to the jaws,
[drink] this divine nectar.
May the first one thirst;
pierce him from behind with your flame at his vital spot—
those who are born of the clouds and those who are born of the wind.
Those who were born from the sky,
the sons of Marīci—
we bind their mouths as well.
Those who were white, those who were green,
those who were black, and those who were red,
under the command of Kabandha.
We crush the locusts;
do not fly toward the grain through the intermediate space.
Sit upon the ridges of the mountains;
eat grass and skulls like locusts among the people.
Just as well-yoked horses carry their burden properly,
even so, O urine, flow forth.
Open the mouth of the bladder;
let the opening of your bladder be released like that of the ocean, the great sea.
I open wide your urethra, as one opens a dam for a stream of water, [for those drops] which rise up from the ocean.
The female ants that crawl upon it,
they know, belong to one who suffers from urinary disease,
and to both his male and female organs.
The wrinkles of the head, the wrinkles of the mouth, the wrinkles from limb to limb, and the wrinkles of the face—
all those wrinkles, O Indrāṇī.
Having wiped it away from the skin.
Bhaṭṭa: Having wiped away [the impurity] from the skin and from the body— those wrinkles that have arisen on the skin and those that have arisen upon the body.
All those folds of Indra’s wife she fastened upon the branches of the *śamī* tree;
may my own fold come to the *śamī*.
It grows and leaves me behind;
they have made this wife of Indra the one who holds fast.
Section 5.
Just as the sun from heaven withdraws the splendors of the stars,
even so do I [withdraw] those of my rivals.
I take to myself splendor and sensory power;
whatever splendor belongs to my rivals and whatever glory belongs to my kinsmen.
May Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, Dhātṛ, and Savitṛ establish that [strength] within me,
as well as the cattle belonging to my rivals.
And whatever wealth is among rivals,
may Savitṛ, having conquered it as if in a game of dice, establish that within me.
May truth alone be victorious, not falsehood;
may the path of truth be straight and virtuous.
Speaking the truth, let us worship with kindled fuel.
By truth may heaven and earth be expanded;
by the truth of the portion of Speech and by the benevolence of Rudra.
May we, through Indra speaking for us, obtain the people; may we find that which is your drawn bow, O Rudra.
Or whatever has been fashioned in your speech by which we dispute— of that,
you must destroy the essence.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, destroy his hope, both that which is true and that which is false, he who [hates] us.
With speech he seeks to conquer the eater;
O Prāṇa, rise up, rise up! Let her not sit down here in abundance; fill this [space].
Sprinkle [us] from above,
as if from the midst of the ocean;
and may the ocean flow with a hundred streams.
With a thousand streams, inexhaustible,
Indra has approached from the east;
like a full stall, fill this!
Pour forth here, pour out completely; make us prolific with male offspring. Here, O cows, be propagated.
Here are the horses, here are the men;
let him who bestows a thousandfold sacrificial fee sit down here, facing toward us.
To Jyeṣṭhaghni among the constellations,
to the day, and to the night— this homage I offer to Viśvakarman.
May that auspicious one be gracious to us.
O Agni, let him not slay the eldest among these; he avoids this one who uproots the very foundation.
Unloose the snares that are to be grasped, knowing them; release the father, the son, and the mother—release them all.
O Agni, do you unloose their snares.
Do not harm the father from whom you arose through three [generations];
do not harm the mother who gave you birth, nor transgress against her.
Untie the snares that are to be grasped, those which bind,
and those which the wise ones avoid through sacred knowledge.
O Agni, loosen the bonds of these;
may there be prosperity day after day for one born from you.
Turn back, do not go further!
O wealthy ones, Agni and Soma, you who are the restorers of wealth, follow after us and increase his riches.
Bring them back again; bring them near again;
may Indra restrain them.
May Agni bring them hither;
I place you on every side with strengthening food, with ghee, and with milk.
Whatever gods there are who are worthy of sacrifice,
may they endow me with wealth.
Homage be to the serpents!
To those who are upon the earth, those who are in the intermediate space, and those who are in heaven—
to all those serpents, homage!
And those who are in the bright realm of heaven, O Bhaṭṭa,
and those who are in the rays of the sun,
and those whose seat is established in the waters—
Homage to those serpents!
Those arrows of the sorcerers, or those of the trees— homage to them!
Homage to those serpents who lie in the pits;
may we increase this [offering] with the remnants of the barley-oblation.
So that he may perform heroic deeds like one resplendent,
may you, together with the gods, overcome your rivals;
may your dominion be long-lived and undecaying.
May the gods protect the life of the remnant with this man-like, barley-based oblation rich in milk;
for the gods have indeed placed great vigor within it.
May Indra bestow vital strength upon this man.
May he unite him with the remnant of the oblation, with hymns, with long life, and with splendor; may he bestow milk.
For the gods have deposited great manly power in him;
may Indra bestow vital strength upon him.
May Vāyu bring them together.
May Tvaṣṭṛ sustain us for prosperity;
may Indra speak in our favor; may Rudra provide for our abundance.
Just as the gods and asuras did,
and just as men have done, so [do this] for the sake of thousandfold nourishment.
O Aśvins, fashion the two marks;
with a red axe,
create a pair upon the two ears.
O Aśvins, let that mark be made by you;
may it be multiplied through progeny.
The black path is for the golden-winged birds.
Clothed in water, they fly up toward heaven and return again from the seat of Cosmic Order;
indeed, by means of this clarified butter, the earth is spread wide.
Make these plants full of milk, O Waters;
when you stir, O Maruts with golden ornaments upon your breasts, you cause both nourishment and favor to swell there.
O Maruts, where you pour forth honey for man—
O Maruts, send that water-flood with rain so that you may fill all the hollows.
He stirs like a maiden pierced by needles,
like a wife for her husband; he is the domestic lord, like Tvaṣṭṛ and Pūṣan.
May the Earth, the source of well-being, come to us, O Bulls! May she,
bestowing all regions with good pasture,
be our leader toward this wealth.
May they come hither, yielding sweetness, free from disease, longing, and multiform;
becoming many as they are born again and again.
May Indra delight you here, O cows;
may Prajāpati generate these offspring; may Tvaṣṭṛ, being well-disposed, bestow them.
May the Year, in harmony with the seasons,
the Lord of Prosperity, bestow prosperity upon me.
You are indeed named Sāhasī.
You were born from force; as the forceful Indra among the gods,
we dig you up for the sake of force.
By that divine medicine of a hundred joints,
possessing a thousand stalks, which is invincible.
I perform the restoration once again.
What has been brought back?
I have grasped the name of the divine healing power of *sahas*.
The consumptions have departed from the man by means of a blessing alone;
let Destruction go away.
Let there be nothing whatsoever here for her;
casting off the snares of this living being,
may I drive away the one hundred and one deaths.
Those hundred and one snares of yours, O Death, intended for the slaying of mortal man— those we bind with the magic power of the sacrifice.
We drive away all [sorrows] with oblations;
let the hundred and one deaths belonging to Nirṛti depart from here beyond.
Let us drive away their darkness;
we bestow upon them breath and light.
These are the thrice-seven obstructors.
Indra said to me through them:
"Ward off the poison! Render the poison ineffective!"
O Maruts, what shall we say? This great hymn of praise for Indra deserves a thousandfold reward.
This indeed wards off poison:
"The sky has stood firm, the earth has stood firm, this entire world has stood firm."
The terrors of poison stood [before him] like a weak man facing a sharp-edged arrow.
It flies away swiftly;
even so, fly away into the sky,
O Bhaṭṭa, together with the rush of the wind!
Just as the eye of one who possesses sight flies forth, radiant with its banner...
(see 10c)
Together with the rays of the sun,
as the mind, whose banner is wrath,
flies away over leagues.
Fly away from here into the sky,
O Bhaṭṭa, along the flow of the ocean!
Go down from right here!
— Become fierce, do not be weak!
O Bhaṭṭas, let all your gods be summoned!
May all your subjects choose you;
through this understanding and oblation,
we cause you to come down to us.
May Indra here make the tribes bring tribute exclusively for himself;
Indra, Kaśyapa, and Agni [are the ones].
Iḍā is your fourth friend; with that which has been and that which is to be, together with the seat,
I cause you to come hither.
Consumptions do not hold him back, nor does a curse reach him,
who possesses this remedy of guggulu.
The fragrant scent of the medicinal guggulu pervades;
the fragrant scent of the medicine guggulu pervades.
Therefore, the consumptive diseases flee in all directions like deer pursued by arrows; [so too does] the *gulgulu* and *saindhava* salt.
Or whatever fodder belongs to the ocean—
of both these I have taken the name for his safety.
The gods ploughed this barley, mixed with honey,
upon the Sarasvatī at the Maṇa;
Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, was the master of the plough.
The Maruts, the bounteous givers, were the plowmen;
O large-leaved, fortunate one, you who are upright in sleep, O observer of the cosmic order!
Like a mother to her sons, be gracious to our hair, O Śamī!
That intoxication of yours which is unshorn and that which is shorn...
By which you make a man loathsome;
like a female owl that has killed a fetus, you wander— of such a progeny as yours, I shave the hair.
I place before me the goddess Ākūti, the fortunate one; may she, the mother of thought, be easy for us to invoke. Whatever hope I pursue, may that be mine alone.
May I behold her entered into my mind.
O Bṛhaspati, come to us with intention; come to us with intention.
And so, bestow upon us prosperity; and so, be easy for us to invoke.
May Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa [fulfill] my intention.
May he acknowledge this speech,
he from whom the gods and deities were born; may Kāma, the excellent leader, follow after us.
Let us now summon the mind with the Nārāśaṃsa hymn and with the prayers of the Fathers.
May our mind return to us again for the sake of will, for strength, and for life, so that we may long behold the sun.
May our fathers and the divine folk grant us back our mind;
may we be united with the company of the living.
O Soma, may we, bearing your mind within our bodies, abide in your law, possessed of progeny.
May Mitra and Varuṇa grant me luster; may the goddess Sarasvatī grant me luster;
may both Aśvins grant me luster.
May you two, adorned with lotus garlands,
bestow that splendor which is placed within the sacrificer and that which is established in the sacrifice.
Whatever luster is in the *surā* that is brown, may I partake of that luster.
[The waters] which flow forth from the springs.
From the streams of heaven,
from the rivers— of all those waters, I sprinkle you with splendor.
When they made King Śakadhūma the constellations, they bestowed upon him an auspicious day.
From that, the kingdom was born.
May there be a blessed day for us in the evening; may there be a blessed day for us in the morning.
O Śakadhūma, always grant us an auspicious day,
you who have made our days auspicious for us.
In the evening, in the morning, and likewise by day— to you, O King of Constellations,
son of Śakadhūma, be constant homage!
That which they call the smoke of power, the first-born light of the stars in the beginning— may that make our gain full of sweetness.
And may he bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
(PS 19.24.20) (Anuvāka 6)
In the pit of the sacrificial post, a spell for causing estrangement has been prepared by the power of the gods;
may Agni be between you two.
Just as [one might think], "May it not prevail over you two," or just as a man hates,
