May the mountain be between you two, so that it may not come into contact with you. Your intentions are diverse; [your] thoughts are diverse.
May your minds be diverse;
turn away from each other in all directions,
so that you may not remain together.
In this case, there are two *kamala* syllables and two *tuṇḍa* syllables; [the reading] "Bhaṭṭa aḍadve kamaḍadve na maśīkṛtaṃ taṃ galāpate" is incorrect, for it should be "Bhaṭṭa namaśītakam."
O Bhaṅgulāpata (or Bhaṅgurāvata), burn this:
whatever belongs to you, or whatever does not belong to you, neither was it yours in the past, nor does it belong to you now.
Just as wealth in a dream perishes, so too does this [wealth] perish from that;
Āgila, Gilāpāpacita, Gila!
May the small, reddish-brown [creature] perish,
for the sake of long life,
for great strength, and for well-being.
Suparṇa told this to me:
"This is the healing balm for one who is embraced; like sifting flour through a sieve, they purify it."
The wise ones fashioned speech from all their limbs; from those limbs I sever what is clung to you.
Cut away what is clung [to you],
for you, O Urva, are indeed a healing medicine; the celestial, well-winged Urva spoke thus.
This is the medicine that embraces [all]:
"I have come as the Conqueror, the architect of all, well-armed."
I am the one who, providing for my friend,
am difficult to overcome in every direction;
I am the path of the assembly.
I am the domestic priest of the people; fashioning friendships,
may enduring speech abide in me.
I have won your eye, I have won your speech, I have won your assembly; having taken your security and well-being—
— May I become the highest.
May Agni, in agreement with Brahmā, the slayer of Rākṣasas, drive them away from here.
The enemy who, having an evil name, lies within your body, in your womb—
[that] enemy of yours [who lies] within your body...
May Agni, the slayer of Rākṣasas, together with the Brahman as his ally, drive away from here that one of evil name who has taken refuge in the womb.
Whatever monstrous Rākṣasas, whatever stingy spirits, and whatever female sorceresses there are— may Agni protect you with his powerful body.
May the slayer of demons protect you from them.
And may Agni and the god Savitṛ, bestowing food and vigor, [protect you].
Protect me from evil conduct;
may you two lead me toward good conduct. Through your protection, may I attain well-being.
This is it, I draw near to it; this is it, I call upon it—
whatever we have heard from you,
may the Lord of Speech bestow it upon us.
May my learning abide in me alone;
let me not commit theft for the sake of offspring, nor may I be deprived of my learning.
O Agni, make our toil fruitful; bestow wealth upon us.
O you who abide in the midst, full of splendor—
It was made for life and for luster; win it among all the gods,
win it for yourself in Bṛhaspati.
Through ghee one obtains progeny; through ghee one attains wealth;
through ghee one gains long life and splendor.
O Parjanya,
the rivers yield their fruit for you as an embryo for our well-being.
The boundary-makers and the goddesses of Brahman have bestowed long life and splendor,
just as an elephant [bestows it] upon a female elephant.
Step followed step;
even so, O inviolable cow, follow the calf's step with your own step.
Just as the wheels of a chariot scatter dust upon the paths,
even so do I cast away my mind.
The heart for the sake of winning;
the first word of Indra, the subsequent word of the gods.
The third word of the Aśvins— with that we cause the cow to come hither.
Up from here [rise] the two dark, trembling ones.
Like two vultures you have soared toward heaven;
burning, intensely burning,
you burn up the heart of this man.
Scorch it, scorch it thoroughly; kindle it, kindle it up!
O Agni, burn away the poison of the serpent.
Burn the husk like straw;
know that for those who sit [in stillness], there is no movement, and for those who have gone [beyond], there is no joy.
Bhaṭṭa: "The black cow dedicated to Sarasvatī has gone to the deepest darkness, just as the night is most dark. (PS 19.26.12)
The cow is black, with a black path;
like swift aids according to their form,
even so is this my head.
Just as the consecrated Aṅgara, or Darvidāka, or Asita,
was the stain upon Anuṣyaṅga.
This very head of mine is like a black flame that subsides from a forest fire being consumed by flames.
O Naiṣadha, just as his face is,
so too is this my head;
whatever he does with his mind and whatever he does with his speech.
While he offers with sacrifices, oblations, and sacrificial formulas,
may Nirṛti, in agreement with Death, destroy his clarified butter before it is even seen.
May the Yātudhānas, Nirṛti, and the Rākṣasas slay him with untruth;
may they, impelled by Indra, churn away his clarified butter.
May that which he offers not be consumed;
O powerful Agni, we set you, the sage, around us as a fortress.
O you of bold color, day by day the slayer of the treacherous, the winner of light,
the two sovereign lords.
Like two hawks swooping down together,
let the clarified butter strike down the one who attacks us and seeks to lead us in battle.
To the earth, to the trees, to the plants,
to Agni the overlord, svāhā! To the intermediate space, to the breath, to the birds...
To Vāyu, the lord, svāhā!
To the sky, the eye, to the stars,
and to Sūrya, the lord, svāhā!
The long-pepper plants spoke together from their birth onward:
"The living person whom we may reach."
That man shall not suffer harm;
he possesses the medicine that cures what is cast out and the medicine that heals what is pierced.
The gods fashioned her as the remedy for poison and ignorance, saying, "She is sufficient for bringing one back to life."
The Asuras dug you in;
the gods sowed you up again.
O Bhaṭṭa, the gods [are] yours.
Pippalī is the remedy for that which is caused by wind; it is the medicine cast against [disease].
What the owl says is in vain.
Whatever footprint the dove makes in the fire—
homage be to that Yama, to Death, whose two messengers have arrived here dispatched.
O Nirṛti, whatever messenger has come to your house of ours— whether sent or unsent—
let that be the abode of the dove and the owl.
You have come here to this state free from enmity; you have settled here for the sake of great heroism—
O you who first reached the heights.
To him who has beheld the path for many,
who rules over these two-footed beings and those four-footed— homage be to that Yama, to Death.
Just as Sita spreads his power, fashioning forms through the magic of the Asura,
even so does this my member, by its own might, become an object of praise.
May he make it whole with this limb. Whatever [limb] belongs to the horse,
that of the mule, the elephant, and the donkey;
As great as the vigor of the horse,
so may my generative power increase; as the generative power of Tāyādara.
By the wind, [my] member has been made thick.
May my member increase as much as the member of another man.
Whose power, harnessed for this purpose,
strikes down the people and the forest like a tree; that might of Indra is unassailable.
The bold power of the bold one stood firm of old,
as the great and delightful might of Indra.
May he grant us that wealth, abundant and adorned with golden ornaments;
may Indra, the most powerful lord among men, bestow it upon us.
O Agni Jātavedas, master of bodies, bring long life here; so that I may remain here for a long time.
The sovereign lord of creatures,
the self-controlled one— may Indra grant me long life, and may the divine Bṛhaspati grant me long life.
May all the gods and day and night bestow life upon me;
may the life-giving [waters] purify my life.
May the vital breath restore my vital breath,
that which the gods created for the gods when they were departing for heaven, each according to his proper place.
Let the roaring waters of the ocean rise up from the sea;
let the surging waves of the ocean swell forth.
With those waters we satisfy you—
those waters which are celestial, and those which have arisen from the wind.
Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, is one whose self is satisfied;
with those [waters], we satisfy you.
Those which are dry and those which are greenish-yellow.
All the herbs together, which have grown upon every ground—
with them we satisfy you.
May our wisdom, the all-formed favor,
and our lofty songs enter us; may she anoint my many verses as one anoints cows.
Just as the ear-piercer [is] among the worlds according to their respective domains:
consecration, austerity, Mātariśvan,
and Bṛhaspati are the womb of this speech.
May many Vedas and sciences be in me;
O Agni and Soma, bestow glory upon us! Whatever austerity you perform with heat, O Agni...
We observe this:
may we be dear to those who have heard [the Dharma]—O venerable ones of excellent intelligence! (PS 19.28.12)
That consumption which has seized you as you were being born from your mother or from your father— that we cause to perish away from you.
May that consumption of yours which is seated in the heart, or that which is in the navel and has reached the belly, enter into another [person].
Moreover, that consumption which has taken refuge in the upper [parts], we cause it to perish away from you; let it, having entered, rest upon another.
The disease of the head, the disease of the limbs, the swelling of the sinews, the consuming fever, and the creeping eruption;
whatever consumption is in your marrow, in your joints, or in your bowels— [drive it away].
We drive that consumption away from you;
let it enter and settle elsewhere.
May Agni, the slayer of demons, sharp and with sharp horns,
slay the demon; may he drive away the enemy and cast out the one who speaks evil.
May strength and vigor come to you from afar, from heaven,
and from the mountains and hills.
Bestowing life upon you from every side.
May the earth give back your vital breath, may the divine sky, and may the intermediate space give it back.
And may the divine heaven, O Soma, restore your body again and again.
Furthermore, Pūṣan is that which is the path and well-being;
Kaṣkiṣā, Kaṣpiṣā,
and Yevāṣā are this very one.
Desiring what is desired, they move through the sandy and dusty regions; those unseen ones do not see those who are seen.
O Lord of Wealth, slay those seen and those unseen with the weapon of Indra—
these and the Viśvarūpas.
The vultures and the cranes have been slain by you.
Desire what you desire; do not turn back toward me, do not face me.
May your mind run after me like a calf toward its mother; may it hasten toward me, O Abhīla and Abhimādanī.
May she be intoxicated with passion for me;
we know you by name, O winged arrow. PS_19,29.8
I win over your mind, so that your mind-stealing spirit shall be mine; your mind is placed within me.
Like a chariot upon its carriage,
yonder sun has risen together with my favor.
I am the domestic priest of the people,
honey-handed and honey-tongued; may eloquent speech, which sustains all, abide in me.
May I behold [him] among men with the banner of insight;
may it be ours alone, the lofty [light].
From all the quarters among all the kings:
[grant me] something sweeter than the sweet, more honeyed than honey.
O Ādityas, make the friendship of our friend dear to us;
O Agni, you are the sacred formulation, you are the Brahman.
Know this for us and speak it; whether it shall be so or not,
eat of this oblation, svāhā!
I inquire of Heaven and Earth;
I inquire of Indra; I inquire of Bṛhaspati; I inquire of the gods worthy of sacrifice.
For what purpose is this life? To depart from it.
O King Yama,
this ladle, raised and prepared for the sake of consciousness, is offered;
please accept this oblation.
Rejoice in the oblation of one who has not yet died;
let that which belongs to one who has died go to Destruction. Whatever has flowed away from you in the flesh...
Whatever is in the churning-stick, whatever is in the rice—
may Agni, the possessor of all remedies, protect you from that distress.
The wind that blows upon you from below and from above,
and the waters which are beneficial to all— [may they protect you].
May they protect you from distress.
We cast away death and destruction, and we cast away consumption.
Just as you, O sinless one,
have become superior through your great strength,
may Vaiśvānara purify us with his rays.
May Vāta, swift with the vital breath through the atmospheres,
and may Heaven and Earth, rich in milk and observers of cosmic order, purify me with their milk, O you who are worthy of sacrifice.
May Prajāpati protect us with the five seasons, and the year with all its abodes; may our vital breath remain right here in this friendship.
I cause that to enter back into myself.
O you who are pure, bright, and purifying, take hold of the auspicious and truthful speech dedicated to all the gods.
Praising her at the communal feasts,
may we be masters of riches.
Grasp the splendor belonging to Vaiśvānara.
May we long behold the sun rising, whose bodies have broad backs, who rejoice here in the shared banquet, and who are worthy of praise.
The *avātaka* is my medicine;
the *avātaka* is the recitation.
You are the *narācī*; do not pierce me.
Seeking the remedy for disease, bring here the soothing linctus;
he draws it out from the milk.
That is the medicine for the discharge;
it has destroyed the disease in the reed-filled rivers.
In the jars and in the pitchers is the medicine for sprinkling;
that medicine I prepare for you.
Eat the meat, drink the water;
O fluttering, trembling one, look around!
We have found what we sought.
This oblation is the destroyer of Piśācas;
by it we slay the flesh-eaters and all the Yātudhānīs.
The foot-soldiers desire you;
the chariot-warriors desire you; they purchase you with cattle and horses.
You are indeed like nectar.
The medicine named Amṛtā has been brought forth from the earth.
The speaker said this to me:
"May it carry me across.
You are the eye of the person.
You are the eye of the cow, the eye of the horse;
you are the eye of what has been and what is to be, and the eye of the Apsarases.
You are the eye of the fair-winged bird, the eye of the serpent, and also the eye of the dog; you are the eye of everything that sees.
"Even as I spoke to the thousand-eyed one, who seizes everything that moves and watches over all— "
Show me the male sorcerers;
show me the female sorceresses.
I have looked across this earth.
Beyond the sky, beyond the sun,
beyond all this that has come into being— beyond these have I looked out upon the sorceresses.
Show me the male sorcerers;
show me the female sorceresses;
show me all those who intend me harm.
Thus, O Herb, I take hold of you.
In this very way, O thousand-eyed one,
may you look back upon me as I approach.
You are the subduer of sorcerers;
these thirty-three unborn serpents are on the far side of the adder.
With their afterbirth,
we wipe away the eyes of the malevolent one who lies in wait as an adversary.
Let Viṣūcī go forth, cutting away,
bearing [it] like a bow (pināka);
let the mind of the reborn woman go in all directions.
"Prosperous are those who seek evil!
Away, O waylayers! Let the one who seeks evil flow away!"
Neither many nor the young shall dare to overcome you;
O departed one, stir your feet!
Carry [the bride] to the house of the one who bestows gifts;
let Indrāṇī go first,
unconquered and unwearied upon the path.
This Phalguni-gem has come hither with power, O Giver of Strength,
by which Indra [overcame] the heroes of the Dasyus.
He overcame the Asuras.
May the gods sprinkle me with splendor and with milk; may both Heaven and Earth sprinkle me with splendor.
May the god Savitṛ bestow radiance upon me; may the sage Kaśyapa bestow radiance upon me.
May the waters bestow radiance upon me.
The plants have bestowed luster upon me;
all beings, having come together,
have placed luster in my mouth.
Those which stand spread out in front like cows setting forth on a journey,
they are the healers of the wind-afflicted.
The long peppers are those that carry one across;
they are the urine of Rudra,
the navel of immortality.
Your root is established in the earth; you are named Viṣāṇā, the medicine that drives away disease.
May there be well-being for you from both kidneys.
May there be well-being for your joints and well-being for your marrow;
may there be well-being for your back, for your bones, and for your entire body.
For no mortal has ever reached the cruel power of your bodies, O Agni;
let the monkey bear the sharp point.
Like a cow its own afterbirth,
he bellows both together and apart like a roaring beast when he devours the upper wood of the lower [millstone].
Crushing head with head and jaw with jaw, let him scatter the stalks with his swift, tawny steeds.
Like well-winged birds, they have raised their voice toward the sky.
In their stall the dark, impetuous ones have danced;
as they descend to the appointed place of the lower one,
they have received much seed from the offspring of the Sun.
With the Bhaga [tree],
with the Śāṃśapa, with the Sāṃśapha,
together with Indra, the companion of the earth.
I make myself fortunate;
let the enemies flee away—
[he] who is blind, he who is one who returns [to life].
Fortune is bestowed upon the trees; may fortune be mine, O Śāṃśapa tree!
May my enemies flee away.
Just as you overcame the trees together with Indra, the winner of the prize,
so do you make me fortunate.
Let the enemies flee away!
Let the dark-blue and red [demon] born from the Himalayas depart!
I have destroyed the *kīśmīla* born from the fertile fields and born from heaven;
[the one] born from the cloud and born from the rain.
Furthermore,
we destroy the kiśmīla that has arisen from heaven, and furthermore, that which has arisen from the ocean.
You who are born from the mist, you who are born from the dewdrops, you who are born from the waters—
you who are the embryo of the lightnings.
O Kiśmīla, be gracious to us!
May these grains of sand, brought hither from the river, not cause us to fail.
With those [dice] which were gathered together, I have destroyed Yama’s *kīśmīla*—
you, O Vibhīdaka, first of all.
The Asuras were conquered and slain;
you are the dispeller of rivals— shake off our enemies.
May the Vibhītaka tree split asunder my rivals,
like a bull with sharp horns.
And so, may they seize our rivals; and so, may they slay those who plot against us.
May the Conqueror drive away our rivals.
You have made my enemies low;
prosperity has overcome both.
That which is the leaper and the one who leaps beyond—
The rat, the kakubha, and the worm;
the upajīkas and the upakvasas—
all these we crush to pieces.
I bind the mouth, the face,
of the scorpion with muñja grass, so that it may move about without making a sound.
Let him depart from the fertile fields!
The rat with a sewn-up mouth has been driven away; he who was proclaimed against us has been repelled.
I crush his teeth;
we drive out his eyes.
O Aśvins, [protect] me with honey.
O Lords of Auspiciousness, anoint me with honey,
so that I may utter speech full of splendor among the people.
I am glorious, glorious as one who looks upon the blinking [world];
I have come here glorious.
And may I be renowned there for all this that has come to be and for all that perceives.
I am glorious compared to everyone. O Apottuda, uncover [the truth]—
whether this exists or whether it does not.
Having fashioned a golden limb, make the eye fruitful and free from defect for both eyes.
The cataract and the film—
may the gods remove that! May my mind be possessed of sight.
May my heart possess vision;
may my mind possess vision;
may my eye possess vision.
Bestow sight upon my two eyes.
(PS 19.32.19) [Anuvāka 8]
Soma is king, and Savitṛ is king;
Bhava is king, and Bhuvana is king;
Śarva is king, and Śarman is king.
May those gods grant us protection.
May Bṛhaspati with the Ādityas, and Bhaga together with Soma, [grant it] to us.
May all the gods, the wide mid-air,
and those gods grant us protection. And may they drive away what has been pierced.
— And so, loosen that which is stretched tight; O All-Gods and Maruts, do not hurl your weapon at us!
This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean;
our homes are in the midst of the lake.
Turn their faces away. Upon your path of approach and your path of departure,
let the flowering durvā grass grow.
Let either a spring or a lotus-filled pool arise here;
[I cover] you with the caul of the frost.
O Śālī tree, we wrap ourselves around you;
be a cool lake for us.
May Agni grant us medicine.
This darbha grass is free from anger,
for oneself and for one's companion; it is the dispeller of anger.
May it be the pacifier of your wrath!
This tree which has many roots reaches down to the ocean.
The darbha grass is established upon the earth; may it be free from anger toward you.
May the arrowhead be driven out from your temples.
We lead you away by the chief [artery],
so that you will not speak according to your own will, but shall attend to my mind.
The snares with which Parīvitta is bound,
and those which are fastened limb by limb from head to foot—
may they be loosened for you, for they are meant to be unfastened.
May Pūṣan wipe away the sins of the embryo-killer.
The gods wiped this off upon Trita;
Trita wiped it off upon human beings.
Therefore, if they have not brought you into the midst,
I shall drive you away by means of this sacred formulation (brahman).
Bhaṭṭa: Enter the rays of light, or the smoke, or enter the wind, or go to the clouds, or enter the mist.
May that [sin] vanish like the foam of rivers;
O Pūṣan, may the female slayer of the embryo be cleansed of her misfortunes.
O Agni, burn away the demon!
That which has been brought in the jars shall go forth invincible;
he has become one who lives.
That which has claws, that which has hooves, that which has a fetus, and that which has flowers; the wild bean, the fish, and the Madhūlaka.
He shall drink that which flows from the ocean— [the water] which is free from outflows and free from disease.
The divine waters from the Himalayas,
which bring well-being to all— may those healing waters come here.
O fortunate one, covered with skin,
with teeth as your bedding,
O wise one, like a single cow in a pen!
I have sprinkled you around with splendor,
like the leader of swans, looking forward at the path ahead.
O tongue, do not tremble;
speak as you did before.
May I rise up full of splendor.
For a Brahmin and a Kshatriya,
for a Shudra and for an Arya, and for whomever else we may desire.
And for one who perceives everything,
cast your two feet forward—
let your mind be directed forward.
May your wrath, directed toward that which is nearer than this, be turned back.
Bhaṭṭa [says]:
"O Blessed One, for the goat and others, there is light in front and darkness behind. (PS 19.34.4)
We bring you back again from this place of the threshing-floor, just as one brings back rice from the rice-threshing-floor.
They smooth it with cotton-wool;
even so do I bring your wandering mind together, directed toward me.
You are the best of those who possess fragrance,
you are the middle of the two carriers; with you the bride has stepped forth.
I take that splendor from you.
From your head, for those who are on the head,
for the young women seeking a husband.
O wife of the Bhaṭṭas,
I have taken from the head of the bull that which is the sweetest part in your limbs.
Whatever love is in your heart, that we cause to enter into me;
may it shine and gleam within me.
Become a steed with the speed of the wind when you are harnessed; go forth at Indra’s impulse, swift as thought. Let the divine Maruts harness you.
May Tvaṣṭṛ bestow speed upon your feet.
O steed, that speed of yours which is placed in secret— that which moves in the hawk and that which is in the wind— [is yours].
By that strength, O powerful steed, may you, victorious in battle and bringing us across, conquer the fray in the assembly.
May you be seated upon the mind.
May he be superior to the eye;
having become superior to the wind,
may he be victorious in battle and a deliverer in the fray.
O Steed, may your body, carrying your own form, bestow upon us what is desirable and grant protection to you; O unassailable gods, for the support of the great [world].
May you ascend to heaven like a divine light.
May Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra who conquers the obstructing foe, lead me to the unassailable state.
May he lead my chariot, may he lead my charioteer, and may he lead my horses well for me;
may Indra lead me by that means.
May the path that is fearless and easy to traverse—
the sacrificial fee— carry me across; may I not suffer harm in the clash of battles.
O Hṛtsuka, bend down around us; O Bhaṭṭa, place [the remedy] upon our body.

O Ādityas, pay homage;
do not falter at this sacrifice,

I open the opening of both the narrow and the wide with my creative power;
having extracted the Veda from those two, I bring it forth.
Now we perform the rites.
From whatever treasury we have brought forth this Veda, into that very place we deposit it again.
What has been done is performed by the power of Brahman;
therefore, O gods, protect me here with your ascetic heat.
Vaiśvānara has generated [me].
May Agni grant us a new favor,
increasing upon the earth with his might;
O Purifier, shine upon us.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, resplendent, invoked by the Jamadagnis,
you have shone from the back of heaven.
Agni Vaiśvānara, the great,
dispels the darkness with his light—
the bird-like, golden-hued one.
The remedy for the head has been brought; it is blue-hued, world-seeing, and shining—

Anumati has consented; the plowmen have consented;
the laborers have consented.
The cows have followed along in thought:
homage be to the girdles, to the lower garments, and to the heart.
Homage to the Lord of the Field;
homage to the Consort of the Field!
I cause your heart to burn with fervor.
Rubbing with his hand,
O Keśin, through your virile power— may your testicles not wither like the head.
May Agni warm you; may Sūrya warm you; may Vāta yoke you.

let your mind go even to the wild beasts and the rays of light.
I shall lift you up from your place of falling.
I drive you out from the houses;
do not touch them for the sake of sitting down. Rise up and go forth to the assembly hall.
Drive her away, O you who possess the *śimidā* disease; likewise, make her possessed by the *ulkā* fire, for the sake of both her husband and her father-in-law.
O Sage, utterly destroy the essence on the shoulders of Hara, the knowledge above the eyebrows, together with the plucking-out.
Together with the rush of the wind, together with the rays of the sun,

We cause the co-wife to perish—
those with long tongues and loud voices, by whom even wet garments [are dried].
The cows, the mothers of clarified butter,
have prepared the medicine in heaven from the white, honored ones.

I cut them all;
I cut their first [cord], and I cut their middle one as well.
And so, I cut off their very last strand, like a lock of wool;
go away, O Lord of the Mind!
Why do you praise what is not to be praised? Go away; I do not desire you. Wander among the trees and the forests.
Whatever we have committed through involuntary speech, through outbursts of anger, or through slander— whether while awake or while sleeping— may Agni remove all those evil deeds.
May he place those things we do not enjoy far away from us.
O Indra, O Brahmanaspati, whatever we perform falsely, even though it be our own prayer—
May Pracetas, the descendant of Aṅgiras,
protect us from those who hate us;
O Lord, make me superior here.
Overcome those who attack us;
drive away from us the sorcery and drive away from us the curses.
O gods, [ward off] the intention of him who seeks to harm us with his mind or who seeks to harm us with evil; [ward it off] from both.
Open up the hearts and minds!
Like a horse ill-yoked to the pole, carry ten [loads] back again for the sake of resistance.
O Brahmaṇaspati, having made him [your] food,
crush him with your two tusks—
he who has been born beyond his own kin.
From above the head you have grown up;
you, the driver away of rivals,
shake off our enemies.
O Bhaṭṭa, this [enemy], most heavy with rage, having been cast down upon the earth, is overcome by his many kinsmen. O Bhaṭṭa,
[he who was] most venerable [is now] humiliated.
Therefore, I shall cut him down so that he will go to destruction; Sthāman has gone to destruction, the one without dominion.
He removes [the enemy] from the eye of the one who stands firm;
he is the king of the one who stands at the end, who follows him.
He will rise and go;
the king has gone to his dwelling,
and the sun has gone to heaven.
Rising up, O slayer of Vṛtra, Plīha, King of Aṅga, who does not slay heroes—
just as one [takes] the path, the byway.
He goes upon the great path;
even so, O spleen, do thou [depart] from us, from whence you have come to us.
The strength given by Indra to the two Asuras,
Śitaṅga and Etadchālvata, has been granted to you; O Kaṇvas, drive away those who are inauspicious and unwelcome.
Therefore, you are the guardian of these houses;
O Agni, you are the lord of the house,
the progenitor of creatures, and their giver.
Drive away the ill-omened, unpleasant, and ever-hostile Kaṇvas; let the wicked one perish,
having bound the cruel thing upon his skin.
Cause fear to the deer;
let the wild animals flee after him. O Bhaṭṭa, destroy the wild animals along with their tracks.

for that one I offer this oblation.

that wind, which causes the whirlpool, has been brought to a halt.
I lead back your mind as one leads a horse with a halter; I bind your mind to me.
Just as shoes are for the feet;
as is liquor, as is honey,
as are dice upon the gaming board.

do not leave me behind, nor cast me off.

Like wine with *māsura* seeds,
may you be dear to your husband;
may you be fortunate among your brothers-in-law.
Draw forth from here the divine word like an arrow that has been shot;

May they overcome and abandon [all evils].

may the Viśve Devas guard us from above.
O God, protect me from the Rākṣasas.
Protect me from human *rakṣas*!
Protect me from every *rakṣas*!
That mountain which is three-peaked—

let that flying,
upraised thing remain like a chronic cough.

From here let consumption depart;

Perish together with the rush of the wind, along with the whirlwind!

You are the pacifier; may you bring peace.

Depart, O evil of the mind;

They have come forth;
they have come up from the depths.
Bhaṭṭa: [I] think.

The two blind ones have spread the wind; the two who cause movement are the weaving and the winding, the sacred law is the shuttle, and the bowstring is the warp.
May all the threads be confounded in the blind, outstretched wind;

The spider, the Śakas, and the Kṛttikās, the wives of the gods,
have spun out this thread.

May Agni come as our first leader, and Bṛhaspati.

may he grant us all that possesses a self as our sacrificial fee.
As a seer, you extend the path of the sacrifice,
meditating upon the back of the *ṛta*,
by which you carry the oblation, O divine messenger.
From here he is wise; from there he is more desirous of gain.
With honey in his hands, honey on his tongue, honey-colored, and devoted to honey.
And may Bhaga, the sweet commander, protect me with splendor—
she who returns with the thrice-seven.
Bearing various forms,

Driven away by speech, she who was possessed of Indra (Bhatt.

Let it reach the one who performs it against you:

Having gone away toward the west,
like one who has struck poison with poison,
let the evil-intentioned one pass beyond.
May we rejoice together with the mind;
may both Heaven and Earth protect us from distress.
Drive away from us all hostilities with this barley-offering,
against the one of evil heart who has performed a sorcery.
Bind them upon their necks.

Like galloping mares,
the *kṛtyā* has been struck down by the plants; the enemy has been struck down by the plants.
O Meha, do not stay here; follow along the difficult paths;
let my rival perish from this place.
Go far away,
O inhabitant, you whose name I utter and upon whose watering-place you delight!
From the furthest distance,
we cause her rival wife to perish;
[we cross] thirty-three mountains.

O Maruts who dwell in the ocean, you have exhilarated yourselves;

O Agni, I become free from that debt.
— O Agni, let this be your portion: those seven ridges of yours, those three,
those that are your hollows and those that are your heights.
O Agni, may these three luminous realms— the eightfold ones from near at hand— be of one mind with you.
Knowing this, deliver the debt to Yama. O Jātavedas, those bodies of yours which are upright,
those which are transverse, and those which are lengthwise— [with these come].
O Agni, being praised by those [goddesses] who are thy companions, do thou,
knowing them, carry away this debt to Yama;
destroy the grayness from the head.
O herb, bring that blackness to us;
make our hair grow and render it even blacker.
As collyrium, so is the moon;
as [ointment] from Mount Trikakuda, so is that.
Because of its production, it is your ash, O Bhaṭṭa. (Or: it is your support.)
As the dawns break forth,
wherever he is, wherever he stands,
may the sword destroy him from there.
"O Bhaṭṭa, may he who sits upon the [sacrificial] grass perish!
The divine, well-winged one has declared this to be the remedy for gray hair."
From the great heaven, from the mid-air, a drop of water has fallen upon me for the sake of sap; may I, O Agni, be united with power and milk. Bhatt. agni(⟨gne⟩).
[It is] by the sacrifices of the seers, by what is well-done, and by their deeds.
If a fruit has fallen from a tree, or if it has come from the intermediate space, that indeed is Vāyu himself.
Where the body is untouched and where there is no clothing, Nirṛti does not reach that place beyond;
[there] is fragrant ointment and indeed clothing.
Upon this purified gold, which is like the moon,
all purifiers are spread out; may he live for a hundred autumns under your protection.
He who crushes the breastbones and approaches the talīḍya [disease],
he drives away every jāyānya.
Whatever winged bird, whether dwelling in the quarters of the sky or otherwise, flies down and enters a man;
I know your name, O Bhaṭṭavaiya; from whence you are born as a husband, that indeed I know. I truly know your name.
Since you are born again and again from [her] who gives birth,
how indeed could you be slain there,
since I am offering the oblation?
He who enters his mouth and makes the belly large—
the wasting disease that is born therein.
I have caused that rival wife to perish.
My face has grown from my ascent; my hips have grown from my ascent.
I am born from the ascent of all; I am born from the nourishment of the bull.
I am sweeter than wine.
I am sweeter than salt, more desirable than cows—
she whom the wind blew away.
O Great Bull, with moist navel;
O Goddess, I give you this charm for that earth of yours.
I take from you the power of dryness.
Yoked together by the mind, O you of excellent seed, let us both properly prepare the oblation for the gods.
May those to whom this portion belongs enjoy it; may they rise up unagitated with auspiciousness.
By that light through which the gods ascended to heaven—
By which path the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Rudras [went],
by which the Aṅgirases ascended to heaven—
by that same path may you two sacrificers go forth in safety.
That which Aditi cooked, desiring sons;
that by which Kaśyapa encompassed all creatures; that rice which is cooked as the Vaiśvadeva offering.
May that inexhaustible portion be ours.
The breath of Soma purifies from the east; may the wind blow from the south, the domain of Indra.
From this direction comes the mother who faces westward.
May that wind be auspicious for us here, O gods;
may the breath of Mitra blow from above,
and may the wind blow upward from Bṛhaspati.
The wise Wind who blows through the mid-air— may that god be auspicious to us here.
He who blows from the north and he who blows from the east.
May that god Vāta, who blows from the south and from the west, and who blows along the upward heights, be auspicious to us here.
O Vāta, you blow through the three intermediate spaces; you blow from the three distant realms.
O thousand-eyed slayer of Vṛtra, protect us!
Driving away the hereditary disease and the blemish from this side;
there, no wife wandered in misery, nor did she weep while being struck, nor did she carry [the burden].
May Indra, the far-seeing doer of great deeds, bestow upon us great invincibility;
may Indra confound the enemy army.
Let the Maruts slay them with their might;
by the impulse of Agni and Vāta, destroy them, scattering them in all directions.
Neither heaven, nor earth, nor Aditi, nor Dhanañjayā belongs to them;
may Agni bestow sight upon them.
Let them go back again, utterly defeated!
O Indra, shatter the village of our enemies; whoever approaches us as an adversary, desiring to kill us.
Just as I shall cause the settlement of these people, driven away by Indra, to follow my will;
let those driven away by Indra make their yoke-bolt crooked.
Let those who seek to harm go away by distant paths;
may we, being victorious, overtake them.
Driving away the dwellings with fire,
may Agni tear apart the occupied village of our enemies, driven forth by Indra.
May these beings be worthy of our praise, for whom I perform this service with an oblation of clarified butter;
indeed, [I honor] the auspicious god Aryaman.
The maiden has sacrificed to him;
may that god, the slayer of Vṛtra,
release her from here and not from there.
O King Varuṇa, this sister of yours prepares an oblation;
bring her husband here to her.
O Subhadra, who art desirable;
O Lord of Wealth, cry out and grant us a boon that is pleasing to the mind.
Make everything auspicious;
make her husband desirable to her,
from behind and from before.
From above and from below,
the track of Bhaga is full; with that, we turn this [wheel] toward us.
And by splendor and by fortune:
there is no blood in the winged moth, nor in the grasshopper, nor in the gadfly.
There will be no falling together, nor will there be exhaustion; there shall be no lowliness here.

protect us from the demon on every side; the cattle have lowed in response.

That which [was prepared] for you from the season, according to the seasonal rite, which Dhātṛ fashioned for you;

Right here move about unconfined.
May I be united with cattle, and may cattle be united with me. You are the seed of heaven, the navel of the earth.
You are the navel; make me the navel.
You are the seed of heaven, the power of earth;
you are power; may I be subject to your power.
You are the seed of heaven, the acquisition of earth;
you are acquisition, may I be acquired for the sake of acquisition.
You are the seed of heaven, the nourishment of earth.
You are nourishment; may I be subject to you for the sake of nourishment. You are the seed of heaven, the prosperity of earth;
you are prosperity; may I be subject to you for the sake of prosperity.
You are existence; you have come into being; may I come into being.
You are the bright; you are the radiant. Just as you are the radiance of the radiant, so [may I be].
Thus may I shine with the radiance of the shining one.
Every evening, Agni is our householder;
every morning, he is the giver of goodwill.
Be the bestower of wealth for every possessor of wealth;
kindling you, may we nourish our own bodies.
Morning after morning, Agni is our lord of the household.
Evening after evening, you are the giver of good cheer; be the bestower of wealth upon wealth. Kindling you, may we prosper for a hundred winters.
He who curses openly, and he who steals by stealth, whether through conscious intent or through wrathful rivalry—
Bhatta reads *stāyad acittyā*.
May Agni release those bonds; may the god Varuṇa, whose laws are firm, ward off curses.
Send forth your speech toward Agni,
the bull of the peoples;
may he carry us across our enemies.
He who shines forth beyond all from the furthest distance—
may he carry us across our enemies.
The Agni who utterly consumes the Rākṣasas with his bright flame—
may he carry us across our enemies.
He who looks out upon all beings and beholds them together—
may he carry us across our enemies.
The winds blow honey for the one who follows the cosmic order;
the rivers flow with honey;
may our cows be full of sweetness.
Sweet be the night and sweet the dawn;
sweet be the earthly realm.
May the plants be sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Forest be honey-sweet for us;
may the Sun be honey-sweet;
may the Sky, our father, be honey-sweet for us.
O Waters,
you are indeed the sources of bliss; grant us strength for great joy and for the sake of vision.
Whatever most auspicious essence you possess,
grant us a share of it here,
like longing mothers.
Therefore we come to you,
for whose abode you quicken us;
O Waters, give birth to us as well.
This spotted bull has come; he has settled again in his mother and in his father, moving toward the light of heaven.
From his out-breath flows the in-breath;
moving within, he shines;
the Mighty One has illumined the sky.
Speech shines across thirty realms; it has taken refuge in the winged bird, day after day at the break of dawn.
When the Śakras ascended their voice,
desiring to win the mid-air,
the bull-like gods rejoiced together.
Bhaṭṭa: Śakra, having empowered his speech, uttered these words of vast resonance: "For he has released [his voice]. PS 19.45.14.
The buffalo-bulls bellowed in the sky.
Śakra indeed uttered these words:
"O upholder of the Law, you shine forth."
The sacrificial grass, free from intoxication, has approached.
Bhaṭṭa: "O Vimada, you are firm, a supporter, unsubdued, well-sustained by Viśvakarman. (PS 19,45.16 [45])
Let not the ocean destroy you, nor the eagle; being unshakable, make this firm!
You are the victorious, the subduer; subdue!
Overcome the enemy who attacks with force;
you possess a thousandfold power, so quicken this man.
You have arisen from the waters and from the essence of the earth.
From Viśvakarman you were born;
Tvaṣṭṛ, knowing it, fashions your form. That divine birth of yours was in the beginning.
Bhaṭṭa omits *vidvān*. "O Adhvaryu, the sixty and ninety bonds,
released between the Hotṛ and Agni— " PS_19,46.3.
The very wise one attains the ripening of his deeds; knowing the way, he follows the path of *ṛta*.
He who is the *adhvaryu* priest knows the seven *hotrā*s.
The Hotṛ priest, sacrificing first, anoints [the offering];
he who knows how to divide the oblation performs the sacrifice and the ritual upward.
In this matter, when the oblation is being divided, may he not be deprived of his share; let him not strike down the one who is entitled to a portion,
nor may he be recognized as one without a share who has gone astray.
May Vāta blow healing upon us, bringing auspiciousness and delight to our heart;
may he prolong our lives.
And you, O Vāta, are our father,
and you are our brother and our friend; as such, grant us life.
O Vāta, that medicine which is placed in your house, hidden in secret— that give us, so that we may live.
You who are neither living nor dead,
you are the womb of immortality for the gods, O Dream;
Varuṇa is your mother and Yama is your father.
Just as they pay back a sixteenth part, just as a half,
just as a debt,
so do I [pay back] all evil dreams— Bhatt. [evil] dreams.
We lead away what is unpleasant.
You are named Araru; we know you thus, O sleep.
O sleep, bestow upon us the state of good dreaming.
The gods do not eat the oblation before him;
he is excluded from the world of the righteous, for he has taken pleasure in evil thoughts within himself.
For he is indeed the most wicked among men:
he who is a slayer of mother, a slayer of father, a slayer of sister, and those others who are evildoers.
The ritual rules have cleansed this [soma] for you, just as men cleanse their impurity;
thus the gods have driven it forth.
Even for a killer of a fetus, this world exists; they do not release the bond of one who, though distressed, has offered the oblation for the sake of the kingdom—
these powerful ones loosen the fetter.
The worm that creeps here, whether it moves forward or backward, or is covered with bristles— that one the healing medicine surrounds.
You are the scorcher of scorpions.
The peacock eats the scorpion;
we eat the peacock.
This medicine, which crushes the scorpion, surrounds it on all sides.
Indeed, the waters are healers.
The waters drive away evil spirits;
the waters are the healers of everything;
the waters are the destroyers of scorpions.
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals;
you are to be praised at the sacrifices.
O gods, whatever vows of yours we, being more ignorant than the wise, have violated—
may Agni, the knower, satisfy all that for us.
He who has entered into the Brahmins of Soma;
we have come to the path of the gods so that we may awaken to that which we are able to do.
May Agni, the wise one, sacrifice; he indeed is the Hotṛ;
may he arrange the sacrifice and the seasons.
Drive away the *śimidvatī* [demoness].
Like those with evil dwellings or ill-placed feet,
cause her mind to fall away from all future years.
Like cooked meat with a sword,
make the birds fall;
let them fly down after the deer.
Destroy the rays [of light] following after;
turn the two oxen apart, and turn the yoke-animals apart as well.
And that sun has spread you two apart, upward and in all directions;
[there is] fierce poison, fixed poison.
Great is the power of poison;
it has shattered the head of the wild ass into a hundred pieces.
Burn him up as fire consumes a cow-pen;
let the earth turn him into wealth, you poison that creeps over him!
Burn him completely like fire!
Seize his flesh;
cause his hair to fall away.
Cut him at the neck down to the nape; crush him as he lies supine.
May I be sweeter than honey.
Sweeter than honey,
indeed, was the honey in my mouth.
An ornament has been placed upon your face;
you gaze intently at me,
like a thirsty deer longing for water.
May the frog call out for me from beneath my feet,
as if from the hoof of a cow;
may he call out for me from beneath my feet.
Like a frog from a cow's hoof,
so do your wheels fall away; like a dog caught in a snare, you are struck down.
Speak for us of a spacious stall,
rich in heroes and many men,
so that from here they may not perish.
Thus speak for me to the cow-pen!
O son-in-law of the daughter, speak; O brother-in-law, speak!
Afterwards, may he rise up as a demon of the buttocks; O hero, slay the Kiṣkindhas!
What the owl says is in vain.
Whatever footprint the pigeon makes in the fire—
for that Yama, the one with listening ears, the seer worthy of praise— let there be homage today.
May the goddess Nirṛti place far away from us those bonds that belong to Indra and those that belong to Varuṇa;
those bonds that belong to Vaiśvānara and those that belong to the Maruts.
May the goddess Nirṛti place far away from us those [nooses] belonging to the Viśvedevas and those belonging to Viśvakarman. May the goddess Nirṛti place far away from us those [nooses].
Nārada, Kitava, Varuṇa, and Soma desired great majesty;
Viśvakarman found it in the ocean.
I place the wasting of the senses within him.
Whatever [wasting] has entered your hands, your eyes, or your mind— [that I place within him].
"By means of Praskanda, I cause his aggregates (skandhas) to be shattered by Klanda.
Three goddesses, the Apsarases, each one by one, go to the realm of the Pretas; this is the name of one of them."
May the Apsarases, taking pleasure in the clarified butter, partake of it by the power of the thousandfold; Svāhā! I have passed you with my mind—I have passed you with my heart.
I have passed you by with all my limbs;
for thus has the abandonment been performed.
These are the ones toward whom you rejoice.
All you women, having gathered together, speak to this man who is possessed by passion:
"The act of casting it away has been performed."
Heaven and Earth have granted me release; the god Savitṛ and Bṛhaspati have granted me release;
and Agni and Sūrya [have granted it] for you.
He has performed an abandonment of brilliance:
from heaven, from the earth, from the wind, and from the rivers.
Indra brought the *saṃskanda*;
he has come, he has gone to this place.
The *saṃskanda* [is] vigor by means of vigor.
Your name was established by the gods;
your name is Hiraṇya, O Bhaṭṭa, your name is gold. May you, O herb, rise up together with wealth.
The ocean is united with the rivers;
heaven and earth, both, are united; the wife is united with her husband in the womb.
O herb,
join together your aggregates; join together the cranial plates of your head, your womb, and your two jaws.
We join together all your limbs with *skanda*;
O Dhātṛ, bestow glory upon me.
Make me a sovereign through glory;
may Indra, the lord of the people, the bounteous one, lead me with fame.
In me be that great vital power, in me be skill and wisdom;
may the Gharma shine forth through the three worlds for me.
Through the Gāyatrī metre, through the light of Virāj,
may I obtain its milking.
Bhaṭṭa: from that; cf. VSM 38.28b: "May we obtain the milking of that [soma]. PS 19,48.18:
"The two Ṛk-sages, Mātariśvan and Aṅgiras, who are established upon the same seat."
O gods, make me glorious; grant me glory! Svāhā!
We merchants invoke Indra;
may he, our protector, go before us, knowing the way, slaying the enemy, the highwayman, and the wild beast.
May he be the lord and the giver of wealth to me. May there be for us bargaining, haggling, and selling;
may he make us the possessors of wealth through counter-bargaining.
May they, rejoicing together, enjoy the oblation;
may our going forth and our rising up be auspicious,
as I engage in bargaining with a counter-bargain.
Desiring wealth for himself,
may Indra bestow radiance upon me in this matter, as do Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, Soma, and Agni.
Those many paths of yours that lead to the gods, which traverse heaven and earth—
of those I place myself within the luster of glory.
So that, having purchased it, I may bring back wealth—
those snares of Nirṛti which are hidden from the one clothed in rags.
The wearer of armor is released from them by setting down the *viṣkandha* [amulet]. Indeed, that is no longer merely a garment.
In that which they pierce the person,
the form is smeared with blood;
therefore, that must be removed.
Rising up, the ignorant man, though possessing much to enjoy, does not find the auspicious path that leads away from what is unpleasant.
Whatever one performs together with this [mantra],
having accepted it through the Brahman, he makes that auspicious by means of it.
One is released from the noose of the Arka;
by that, the giver beholds clearly those two tigers who have descended and turned downward.
The father and mother who desire to devour [the child]—
O Brahmaṇaspati, Jātavedas, do you, by means of the sacred word (brahman), make those two teeth here auspicious.
The rice you have eaten, the barley you have eaten, the beans you have eaten, and likewise the sesame—
this portion of yours has been set aside as a treasure-trove.
Do not harm the father and the mother;
may you two be non-terrible, united, in harmony, pleasant, toothless, and most auspicious.
Do not harm the father and the mother;
let your terrible power be directed elsewhere than toward their bodies.
With this [hymn], may Indra and Agni be united.
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, make King Soma, the protector of the earth, seize [the wealth] from my enemies.
I have undertaken this vow,
sharpened by the Lord of Ascetics,
where there are my enemies, O Bhaṭṭa.
I take hold of those who hate me.
By means of this taking and binding,
we bind our enemies.
The out-breaths and the in-breaths of these, the life-forces and the lives—I have cut them all away.
Svāhā! To the one who has rushed forward, accompanied by the Maruts, svāhā!
Hail to Jayadvīra at the invocation!
Hail to Bṛhaspati, who is accompanied by the Viśvedevas! May Heaven prevail! May Earth prevail!
The intermediate space has attained its own [rightful] place;
the departed ones have caused the oceanic waters to cast out the dart.
May the wind drive you forth, may the earth with its power drive you forth;
may the waters of the ocean drive you forth.
They have extracted the thorn.
May Sūrya cause you to move forward together with the healing constellations.
The Preta has caused the oceanic waters to expel the dart.
The amulet made of *pūtudru* wood which [is mine]—Bhatt. omits "which [is mine]"—[has expelled it].
The universal remedy has arrived;
may it drive away from us all evil dreaming and whatever darkness there is.
Drive away from us all evil dreams, and drive away misfortune and ill-fortune;
then [grant us] golden luster.
O Maṇi, always make me so! Indeed, I am ever the Blessed One,
possessed of the senses, the subduer of enemies.
This pautudruva amulet which has ascended with wealth for me,
has ascended with Indra.
A man, a horse, wealth, and gain— a man, a golden necklace—
may you grant me a male child, O Herb!
"Place this [seed] for the woman,
so that when a son is born, no one at all shall say, 'There is no joy.'"
O herb, place a son for this woman in this very way—
with a stallion, with a bull, with a *ṛṣya*.
You have been purchased, O herb;
a white horse is your wealth.
This golden, green [amulet] is yours;
bestowed here by King Soma,
may it bring about the birth of a son.
Whatever manly strength, wealth, sacred knowledge, learning, and treasure I possess—
may the Guardian of the Treasure protect all this of ours here.
As far as I have come, having distinguished myself in the assembly of women;
whatever manly strength, wealth, and sacred knowledge I possess, and these bold fires that are within me.
May Hariścandra protect us here until I return from wandering to the next village;
here I am, having returned from wandering to the next village.
— May there be clear manly strength, wealth, and sacred knowledge.
Whatever pure thing is here within you, that I take for myself.
For Sūrya was the first to come, O Śakra, when you, Maghavan, harnessing your two tawny steeds by the thousands, subdued the Dāsa race for the sake of the slaying of the Dasyus and for the Ārya.
O Indra, much-invoked, as you wield the thunderbolt with your arms,
you hasten for the slaying of the Dasyus;
quickly crush their firm joints!
O you who possess intense lack of faith, cast down these many who are unrestrained with your deadly weapon!
Behold now Indra, the purifier of wonders.
Like many arrows falling together,
let the sages turn back those who attack our spirited and generous lord; may they be struck down by those fearless ones.
To the current year, to the recurring year,
and to the full year, we announce this:
whatever misfortune we have incurred in our vows.
We anoint the evil-hearted one with that impurity.
O Lord of Vows, whatever vow of mine has been disturbed by impurity— may day and night restore that for me.
May the moon, the physician, rise in the east;
may the sun favor this with its rays—
that vow which I have transgressed.
With thought, with mind, and with the heart—
may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle that within me.
I offer these vows to Agni, the lord of vows;
may he grant me great splendor and glory.
May he grant me long life. May the wind blow pleasantly upon the cows;
may they graze upon the nourishing plants.
Rich in fat, blessed with life, and bringing delight— O Rudra, be gracious to those who move on feet.
Those who are of one form, of all forms, and of like form...
O Parjanya, grant great protection to those whose udder Agni knows as their birthplace, whom the Aṅgirases fashioned here for the sake of heat.
Those who extended their bodies among the gods, whose forms Soma knows— may they swell forth in abundance for us.
O Indra, may you grant that they be rich in offspring within the cow-pen.
Prajāpati, bestowing these upon me, has brought them—
though they are many— into my cow-pen.
May we be united with their offspring, living long through many autumns;
she stands firm and bellows aloud.
The tawny one is the much-murdering;
indeed, murder was born from the *hālīkṣṇa*,
from rice, from beans, and also from barley.
Just as the ash of a sharp-edged tool cannot be used for softening clay, so too, O Halaghnaka, do not soften it.
Drive them out from the villages, drive them out from the quarters,
so that the donkey with its hideous appearance shall bray at the property of others.
Thus, O seat of the bold ones, you whose leaves are sharp, strengthen them; as a slayer of Vṛtra and a powerful one, strengthen them.
The plough is sharp-edged,
well-fashioned, and full of sap; it draws forth the cow and the sheep.
And [offer] the swelling, excellent [oblation]; [recite] the Prastāva; [prepare] the chariot-vehicle;
draw tight the auspicious leather thong.
Stir up the goad for good fortune;
for the sake of good fortune, strike the right [side] of the harnessed draft-animal with the goad.
Always take up the honeyed plow in the fields;
may Parjanya rain down upon it.
For the sake of abundant grain to be produced—
these very ones have been seen approaching upon the sacrificial altar.
Bhaṭṭa says that the Ṛkṣarā Āyatīs declared: "Agni is the bearer of the oblation to the gods;
he is the mantra, the Hotṛ, and the lord of the sacrificial offering."
Bhaṭṭa:
These [waters] have come, bringing delight;
they bear the udders of honey. (PS 19.51.15)
Learn from them as they yield inexhaustible milk;
you are the *iḍā*s, rich in honey.
May those multiformed ones enter me,
together with breath, splendor, heat, and strength.
Milking the bright milk from the cloud of heaven,
the navel of Cosmic Order reveals the nectar;
milking clarified butter, she flows forth, nourishing on every side.
Milking forth vigor, never failing, may the doers of good deeds sit near her with their funeral offerings (*svadhā*).
She who swells with ghee—seek her! (Bhatt.: "Seek the spring of ghee!")
Enter this womb;
those libations which you prepared while living— may they be sweet-dripping for you.
May the essences of the plants,
may my intentions, all be united for me—
[united] with that which is full of vigor and full of milk.
I have followed the hand of the earth.
You are the lead-out of the hand; you are the lead-out of the path.
Thus we cast all evil dreaming away upon the sacrificial post.
May my field be full of milk.
May there be milk and grain;
may my cultivation be rich in milk— may I myself become rich in milk.
For the bull-like, great Agni, the finder of light, the radiant and resplendent one, I offer this white oblation;
may he make us firm and strong. May he [make us]... for us.
And may he grant us long life to live.
O Agni, I truly know your name; by your names you are threefold protected.
May the three nourishments and the threefold sacrifice attend us;
growing through the milk of Prajāpati,
may we be long-lived and radiant.
Living long, may we sit near you.
The two broad-nosed messengers of Yama, who delight in the life-breath and are made of udumbara wood, move among the people.
I know; Sūrya knows.
What will these two do?
He has not deceived me, for I have approached him with intent to deceive.
I am not a ripened one by birth, nor am I a disciple; I am the overcomer, the conqueror of all, the vanquisher of armies, the finder of light—
he who is this entire world, that indeed am I.
He has stood firm, he has risen up; the sage has been born.
He has measured out the breadth of the earth;
as sovereign ruler, he has occupied all the worlds.
He, through his will, knows the sacred ordinances of Varuṇa.
Bhaṭṭa: Prajāpati, possessed of offspring—may he, being possessed of offspring, make me possessed of offspring. (PS 19.52.12–13)
The sun is full of splendor; may it make me full of splendor.
Soma is full of milk.
May he, full of milk, make me full of milk.
Thirty testicles belong to the *kābava*, ten testicles to the *ulūka*.
O Kardama, you have four [enemies];
O Ugrakāśinī, cut them down even at their roots!
You are born of Asura; we cause you to perish from here.
You are born of Indra, born of Soma.
We send him forth from here;
let the fish Urva drink its honey-water as it passes by.
It is without outflows and free from disease. (PS 19.52.18) [Anuvāka 13]
Thou art swift and thou art agile;
thou art the kindling-stick of Prajāpati, named Saṃsiti, the hairy one. Through thee, Prajāpati, desiring a firm foundation, established himself; he stood firm.
Just as Prajāpati, desiring a firm foundation, found a firm foundation through you, so may I, desiring a firm foundation, find a firm foundation through you.
May the bridegroom come to me; may the students of sacred knowledge come to me. Svāhā!
You are prosperity and you are the foundation.
May they go to the state of the student of sacred knowledge belonging to Prajāpati; svāhā!
You are sleepless and you are without abode.
May they go to the state of the Brahmachārin of Prajāpati… Svāhā!
You are desire and you are the Yakṣa.
May they go to the state of the student of Brahmā, of Prajāpati... svāhā!
You are fame and you are glory.
May they go to Prajāpati, the student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārin*). Svāhā!
You are water and you are greatness.
May they go to the state of the student of Brahmā, of Prajāpati; svāhā!
You are food and you are the eater of food.
May they go to Prajāpati’s [world] as students of sacred knowledge; svāhā!
And you are one who bestows, and you are one who grants;
may they go to Prajāpati,
the student of sacred knowledge, svāhā!
You are according to desire and you are the cow of plenty.
May they go to the state of the student of sacred knowledge belonging to Prajāpati; svāhā!
You are one who brings forth and you are one who gathers together.
May they go to Prajāpati,
the student of sacred knowledge, svāhā!
You are the one who points out and you are the one who directs.
May they go to Prajāpati, the student of sacred knowledge; svāhā!
And you are his consent, and you are the one who gives consent.
May they go to Prajāpati, the student of sacred knowledge— svāhā!
You are victory and you are complete victory.
May they go to the state of Prajāpati’s student, svāhā!
You are the gathering together and you are the victory in battle;
may they go to the state of the student of sacred knowledge belonging to Prajāpati, svāhā!
Agni is the lord of the earth; may Soma protect you. We know you; know me.
You are a lord; make me a lord.
Of cattle, horses, men, students of sacred knowledge, prosperity, and food—
Vāyu is the lord of the intermediate space, Soma [is the lord] of food. (See 15bcd) PS_19,53.16
Sūrya is the sovereign lord of heaven; may Soma protect you. We know you; know me.
You are a sovereign lord; make me a sovereign lord.
For the prosperity of cattle, horses, men, and students of sacred knowledge, and for the acquisition of food—
may the Vasus find wealth for me; may they find my home, progeny, cattle, gain, prosperity, and a firm foundation.
May the Vasus who bring wealth come to my house: progeny, cattle, acquisition, prosperity, and a firm foundation.
May the Vasus who bestow abundance come together to my house.
Offspring, cattle, wealth, prosperity, and stability.
You are victory; may I be victorious; may I conquer earthly hosts.
You are complete victory; may I conquer completely; may I conquer human hosts.
You are the conqueror; may I be victorious; may I conquer all hostile armies.
Awaken him, rouse him up; do not let him sleep. Do not disregard him.
Stand upright, look toward me;
do not praise others at all.
Bring them hither, turn them back!
—Turn them back toward you; we cause all his thoughts to be won over by means of the god of love. 19.54.2
The Maruts heat the Smara when Jātavedas is kindled;
let his mind fly upward.
May that delight find its pleasure in me. O Gaṇapati, make me a leader of the hosts; do not treat me like a mere grain of barley.
Do not make the one with a retinue one without a retinue;
therefore, do not cut me off from him.
Make the one with a retinue one with a retinue.
Therefore, do not let us perish.
O increaser of the host, increase my host—
of cattle, horses, men, and Vedic students— for the sake of prosperity and the enjoyment of food.
O increaser of the host, increase my host;
[increase] my cattle... [and] my food.
O increaser of the host, cause my host to grow.
For cattle, horses, men, and those practicing celibacy, as well as for prosperity and the consumption of food—
whatever is dug up and whatever is not dug up—
all that is sapless poison.
Whether it be ground or unground, all that is sapless poison;
whether it be smeared or unsmeared.
All that is tasteless poison. Just as a she-wolf or a tigress whose cub has been devoured becomes frantic with hunger, so it is here.
Thus you have become restless,
sent by my anxieties,
like a blazing tuft of cotton.
May you become one whose forehead is ablaze with fire; thus, sent by my prayers, become one whose forehead is ablaze. PS_19,54.14
Cry out, O Lalā! Bhaṭṭa, cry out, O Lalā! Wither with desire for the Dasyu! Sent by my mental agonies, he is laughing! (PS 19.54.15)
Under the control of these two, this entire world— both that which is moving and that which is stationary— is placed,
and it moves.
May those two seize me as I speak here; may they not leave me behind as a witness in this matter, O Prajāpati, according to my true nature—
[those] who [seize] me as I speak with heart and voice.
May the god Indra, Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, and the lord god Mṛtyu pursue him with speech, with the ear, and with the mind, desiring to seize him.
Just as one does not extract the third dawn from the living soul.
Bhaṭṭa [says]:
